docs.title: Home
docs.text:
miniblue

Local Azure development. One binary. No account needed.

miniblue is a free, open-source Azure emulator that runs entirely on your machine. Test your Azure apps locally without an Azure account, network connection, or credit card.

docs.title: Why miniblue?
docs.text:
Azure developers have to juggle 5+ separate emulators (Azurite, Cosmos DB Emulator, Functions Core Tools, etc.) just to get basic local dev working. miniblue replaces all of them with a single binary on a single port.

docker run -p 4566:4566 -p 443:4567 -p 4567:4567 moabukar/miniblue:latest

That's it. 32 Azure services are now running locally.

docs.title: What's included
docs.text: Service Description Resource Groups ARM resource group management Blob Storage Containers, blobs, upload/download Table Storage Entity CRUD operations Queue Storage Send/receive/peek messages Key Vault Secrets management Cosmos DB Document CRUD (SQL API) Service Bus Queues, topics, messaging Azure Functions Function app registration Virtual Networks VNets and subnets DNS Zones Zone and record management Container Registry Registry management Event Grid Topics and event publishing App Configuration Key-value configuration store Managed Identity IMDS token endpoint DB for PostgreSQL Flexible server + database management DB for MySQL Flexible server + database management Azure SQL Database Server + database management Azure Cache for Redis Cache management + key listing Container Instances Container group lifecycle Public IP Addresses Static/dynamic IP allocation Network Security Groups NSGs with security rules Load Balancer Frontend IPs, backend pools, rules, probes Application Gateway L7 load balancing, WAF, routing rules Storage Accounts ARM management with shared key auth

docs.title: Works with your tools
docs.text:
• Terraform - metadata_host = "localhost:4567" and you're done
  • azlocal CLI - like awslocal for LocalStack
  • Azure CLI - custom cloud registration
  • Any Azure SDK - just point the endpoint to http://localhost:4566
  • curl - standard REST API

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# Install
go install github.com/moabukar/miniblue/cmd/miniblue@latest

# Or use Docker
docker run -p 4566:4566 -p 443:4567 -p 4567:4567 moabukar/miniblue:latest

# Create a resource group
curl -X PUT "http://localhost:4566/subscriptions/sub1/resourcegroups/myRG?api-version=2020-06-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"location": "eastus"}'

Get started →

docs.title: Adding a new Azure service
docs.text: Every service follows the same pattern. Here is a step-by-step guide.

docs.title: 1. Create the handler package
docs.text:
Create internal/services/yourservice/handler.go:

package yourservice

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "net/http"

    "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
    "github.com/moabukar/miniblue/internal/store"
)

type Handler struct {
    store *store.Store
}

func NewHandler(s *store.Store) *Handler {
    return &Handler{store: s}
}

func (h *Handler) Register(r chi.Router) {
    r.Route("/yourservice/{resourceName}", func(r chi.Router) {
        r.Put("/", h.CreateOrUpdate)
        r.Get("/", h.Get)
        r.Delete("/", h.Delete)
    })
}

func (h *Handler) CreateOrUpdate(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    name := chi.URLParam(r, "resourceName")

    var input map[string]interface{}
    json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&input)

    h.store.Set("yourservice:"+name, input)
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
    json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(input)
}

func (h *Handler) Get(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    name := chi.URLParam(r, "resourceName")

    v, ok := h.store.Get("yourservice:" + name)
    if !ok {
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
        return
    }
    json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
}

func (h *Handler) Delete(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    name := chi.URLParam(r, "resourceName")
    h.store.Delete("yourservice:" + name)
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
}

docs.title: 2. Register in the server
docs.text:
Edit internal/server/server.go:

import (
    // ... existing imports ...
    "github.com/moabukar/miniblue/internal/services/yourservice"
)

func (s *Server) setupRoutes() {
    // ... existing routes ...
    yourservice.NewHandler(s.store).Register(s.router)
}

docs.title: 3. Add to the health check
docs.text: In internal/server/server.go, add the service name to the services slice in healthHandler.

docs.title: 4. Add azlocal commands (optional)
docs.text: Add a handler function in cmd/azlocal/main.go and register it in the switch statement.

docs.title: 5. Write tests
docs.text: go test ./internal/services/yourservice/...

docs.title: 6. Update documentation
docs.text: Add a page under website/docs/services/ and update website/mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Store
docs.text:
The store.Store is a thread-safe in-memory key-value store. Every service uses string keys with a prefix:

h.store.Set("rg:sub1:myRG", resourceGroup)        // Resource group
h.store.Set("kv:myvault:dbpass", secret)           // Key Vault secret
h.store.Set("blob:blob:acct:cont:file.txt", blob)  // Blob

Useful store methods:

Method Description Set(key, value) Store a value Get(key) Retrieve a value (returns value, bool) Delete(key) Delete a key (returns bool) Exists(key) Check if a key exists ListByPrefix(prefix) List all values matching a prefix CountByPrefix(prefix) Count keys matching a prefix DeleteByPrefix(prefix) Delete all keys matching a prefix

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
Use internal/azerr for Azure-compatible error responses:

import "github.com/moabukar/miniblue/internal/azerr"

azerr.NotFound(w, "Microsoft.YourService/resources", name)
azerr.BadRequest(w, "Invalid input")
azerr.Conflict(w, "Microsoft.YourService/resources", name)

docs.title: ARM-style routes
docs.text:
For resources managed through Azure Resource Manager, use the standard ARM URL pattern:

r.Route("/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.YourService/resources", func(r chi.Router) {
    r.Get("/", h.List)
    r.Route("/{resourceName}", func(r chi.Router) {
        r.Put("/", h.CreateOrUpdate)
        r.Get("/", h.Get)
        r.Delete("/", h.Delete)
    })
})

docs.title: ARM Resource Engine
docs.text:
Most miniblue services are hand-written chi route trees over map[string]interface{} bodies. That does not scale to azapi-driven Terraform (arbitrary bodies, 100+ resource types, resources at management-group scope). internal/arm is a generic ARM resource engine that serves registered resource types with one shared implementation. It is introduced incrementally and coexists with the existing handlers.

Status: the engine serves Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions@2023-04-01 at subscription scope. Everything else still uses its own handler.

The agreed design direction for evolving the engine is recorded in ARM foundations.

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
The engine is a chi root middleware, registered in server.setupRoutes before the authorization middleware:

request -> CORS/logging/recover/request-id/headers -> arm.Engine -> authorization middleware -> chi routes
                                                         |
                                       registered type at an allowed scope? -> serve
                                       anything else                         -> next

For every request the engine parses the path with arm.ParseID. It serves the request only if the type chain (Namespace/type[/child...]) is registered and the scope is one the type allows. Anything else, including unparsable paths, goes to next unchanged.

Why a middleware and not chi sub-routes:

  • A registered type claims its own paths, so there is no route conflict with the existing /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/... trees. Migrating a handler is "register its type, delete its chi routes".
  • It must run before the authorization middleware, which 404s every Microsoft.Authorization path except role assignments and definitions.
  • It inherits request IDs, structured logging, panic recovery and Azure response headers.
  • It does not depend on casemirror.go: the parser is case-insensitive itself, and casemirror only rewrites paths that match a chi route, which engine paths do not. The engine works with or without it.

Services are gated like the others: types are registered only when the policy service is enabled (SERVICES env var, default all).

docs.title: Resource IDs
docs.text:
arm.ParseID is case-insensitive and scope-agnostic. Keywords are canonicalised, names keep the casing they were parsed with. Subscriptions, resource groups and management groups are modelled as resources, so a scope is just another ID.

Shape Example Tenant /providers/Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions/x Management group /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/{mg}/providers/.../x Subscription /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/.../x Resource group /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/.../x Nested child .../virtualNetworks/{v}/subnets/{s} Extension resource {any resource ID}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/.../x Collection (list) {scope}/providers/{ns}/{type}

The last providers/{ns}/{type} group is the resource; everything before it is its scope, parsed recursively. A providers segment only delimits a group at an even position (names sit at odd positions), so a resource may be named providers. ID.ScopeKind() classifies the scope, ID.Key() is the lowercased identity.

docs.title: Store
docs.text:
arm.Store sits on store.Store, so it works with the memory, file and Postgres backends.

Key Value arm:r:<lowercased id> the resource document, as JSON text arm:i:<lowercased parent>\|<lowercased type> sorted list of child resource keys
  • Lookups are case-insensitive; the stored document keeps the casing of the PUT that created it, so id and name never change with the casing of later requests.
  • Listing reads the index and then each child: O(children). It does not call ListByPrefix, which is O(n) on the memory backend (upstream issue #95).
  • Only DeleteTree scans by prefix. The engine uses it only for types that declare Children, never on a plain delete.
  • Documents are stored as JSON text and decoded with json.Number. The file and Postgres backends decode stored values into interface{}, which turns numbers into float64 and corrupts integers above 2^53; a string survives every backend unchanged. Request bodies are decoded the same way, so numbers round-trip verbatim. Hooks therefore see json.Number, not float64. Callers never share state with the backend.
  • Writes are atomic within the process. Store.Update(id, fn) runs the read, the change and the write under one store lock, shared with Delete and DeleteTree. PUT (create-or-replace, and keeping the creating casing) and PATCH (update-if-present, 404 if not) are each a single Update, so a concurrent DELETE or PUT cannot be undone or overwritten by a PATCH, and concurrent first PUTs agree on one creator. The lock is one mutex per Store, not per resource: operations are small and an emulator does not need more. It does not coordinate several miniblue processes sharing one Postgres.
  • State lives only in the backend, so /_miniblue/reset clears it.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
Request Result PUT {id} 201 on create, 200 on update. Full replace. GET {id} 200, or 404 ResourceNotFound DELETE {id} 200 if it existed, 204 if not GET {collection} 200 {"value":[...]}, sorted by ID PATCH {id} Only for types with PatchTags. Replaces tags, other properties are ignored. other methods 405 MethodNotAllowed

Bodies are raw passthrough plus the server-owned id, name and type. A body name or id that contradicts the URL is a 400. An api-version that is not in the type's list is a 400 InvalidApiVersionParameter; a missing api-version is accepted, like the rest of miniblue. Errors are written through internal/azerr.

Not done by the engine yet: parent existence checks (a subscription, resource group or management group is not required to exist), provisioningState, long-running operations, $filter/paging.

docs.title: Registering a type
docs.text:
reg.Register(arm.Type{
    Name:        "Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions",
    APIVersions: []string{"2023-04-01"},
    Scopes:      arm.ScopeSubscription, // | arm.ScopeManagementGroup | ...
})
Field Meaning Name Namespace/type, matched case-insensitively APIVersions accepted api-version values Scopes bitmask of allowed scopes: tenant, management group, subscription, resource group, resource (extension) Children nested types ({Name: "subnets"}); they inherit APIVersions and Scopes PatchTags enable PATCH of tags Hooks.Validate func(ID, body) error, a returned error becomes a 400 Hooks.Defaults func(ID, body), fill server-side defaults after validation

Hooks are optional and exist for clients that drift on fields the server does not fill (azurerm). azapi tolerates raw passthrough, so policyDefinitions has none. Registration panics on a malformed or duplicate type, so mistakes surface at startup. Put registrations in internal/services/<name>/ and enable them in server.setupRoutes behind serviceEnabled.

Moving policyDefinitions to management-group scope is adding arm.ScopeManagementGroup to Scopes; the engine is covered at every scope by unit tests.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• internal/arm: parser (every scope shape, casing, resources named providers, invalid paths), store (memory, a JSON round-trip backend and a file reload; exact numbers; Update atomicity), engine CRUD with synthetic types at every scope, children, hooks, PATCH, concurrent PUT/PATCH/DELETE, error cases.
  • tests/arm_policydefinition_test.go: policyDefinitions through the real server, including coexistence with the authorization handlers.
  • tests/terraform/azapi/policy_definition: the acceptance test. terraform apply, terraform plan -detailed-exitcode must report no drift, GET with mangled URL casing must return the canonical id, terraform destroy, GET must be 404. It runs in CI (.github/workflows/acceptance.yml) with pinned Terraform and azapi versions.

To run the acceptance test locally (Linux/macOS/WSL):

LOCAL_AZURE_CERT_DIR=/tmp/miniblue-certs go run ./cmd/miniblue &
SSL_CERT_FILE=/tmp/miniblue-certs/cert.pem ./tests/terraform/azapi/policy_definition/run.sh

docs.title: Migrating an existing handler
docs.text:
1. Register the handler's types (api-versions, scopes, children) in a Register(reg) function.
  2. Port the per-type behaviour that clients depend on into Defaults/Validate hooks. Keep the existing handler tests; they are the spec.
  3. Delete the chi routes for those types. Roll them out one handler per PR.
  4. Move any cascade (resource group delete, parent delete) onto Store.DeleteTree or the engine.

Good first candidates are roleDefinitions and roleAssignments; once they move, the authorization middleware can go.

docs.title: Follow-ups
docs.text:
• Management groups, multi-subscription/tenant model, RBAC at management-group scope.
  • Policy assignments, initiatives and evaluation; built-in policy definitions (ALZ looks them up by GUID at tenant scope).
  • Parent existence resolvers, extension-resource cascade, provisioningState/lifecycle hooks when a second type needs them.
  • Migrating the existing handlers and then removing casemirror.go.
  • Backend: ListByPrefix complexity (#95) and unescaped LIKE wildcards in the Postgres ListByPrefix.

docs.title: Adding a New Service
docs.text:
1. Create internal/services/yourservice/handler.go
  2. Implement NewHandler(s *store.Store) *Handler and Register(r chi.Router)
  3. Register in internal/server/server.go (import + call in setupRoutes)
  4. Add to health endpoint service list
  5. Add to supportedProviders in subscriptions handler (if ARM)
  6. Write tests in tests/yourservice_test.go

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
The Store wraps a Backend interface. All handlers use *store.Store without knowing which backend is active.

  • Set/Get/Delete: Key-value operations
  • ListByPrefix: Used for listing resources within a scope (e.g., all VNets in a resource group)
  • DeleteByPrefix: Cascade deletes (e.g., deleting a resource group removes all child resources)

Keys follow the pattern: service:subscriptionId:resourceGroupName:resourceName

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: miniblue returns mock JWT tokens with valid structure (header.payload.signature). The payload includes oid, tid, appid claims that Terraform and Azure SDKs parse. No real token validation is performed.

docs.title: Scope and Philosophy
docs.text: miniblue sits between unit tests and full integration tests. It gives you a local Azure environment that is good enough for Terraform plans, SDK smoke tests and CI pipelines without needing a real Azure subscription.

docs.title: Control plane vs data plane
docs.text:
Azure APIs have two layers:

  • Control plane (ARM) - resource management via /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/.... This is what Terraform, Bicep, Azure CLI and the Azure Portal use to create, read, update and delete resources.
  • Data plane - direct operations on the resource itself. Uploading a blob, sending a Service Bus message, reading a Key Vault secret.

miniblue focuses on the control plane first. Every service starts with ARM CRUD (PUT, GET, DELETE, List) so that Terraform and infrastructure-as-code tools work. Data plane support is added for high-value developer workflows where calling a real Azure service during local development is impractical.

docs.title: What this means in practice
docs.text: Use case miniblue support Notes terraform plan and terraform apply Primary focus ARM responses match what the azurerm provider expects az group create, az network vnet create Works ARM endpoints Upload a blob, send a queue message Works Data plane for common dev workflows Read a Key Vault secret from your app Works Data plane Complex Cosmos DB queries with SQL syntax Not yet Document CRUD works, query language is on the roadmap Service Bus topic subscriptions Not yet Basic queue send/receive works Run Azure Functions locally No Use Azure Functions Core Tools for that Azure AD/Entra ID authentication flows Mock only Returns valid JWT tokens but no real identity management

docs.title: When to use miniblue
docs.text:
• Local development - run terraform apply against miniblue instead of a dev subscription
  • CI/CD pipelines - spin up miniblue as a Docker container in your pipeline to test infrastructure code
  • SDK smoke tests - point your SDK client at localhost:4566 to test CRUD operations
  • Demos and workshops - no Azure account needed

docs.title: When to use real Azure
docs.text:
• Data plane edge cases - if your app relies on specific Azure behavior (retry headers, throttling, eventual consistency), test against real Azure
  • Performance testing - miniblue is fast but does not simulate real Azure latency or rate limits
  • Security testing - miniblue accepts any credentials by design
  • Production deployments - miniblue is for development only

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
1. Start with ARM, add data plane when it matters. A service that only has ARM CRUD is still useful for Terraform users.
  2. Good enough beats perfect. Responses should satisfy Terraform and SDKs, not be byte-for-byte identical to Azure.
  3. Zero config by default. No accounts, no credentials, no setup. docker run and go.
  4. One binary, one port. No separate emulators for each service.
  5. Tests over mocks. miniblue is not a mock library. It is a running server that your tools talk to over HTTP.

docs.title: miniblue ARM architecture review
docs.text: Reviewed: main @ d86ed0d. Scope: control-plane foundations ahead of roughly 25 new ARM types, APIM, and azapi-heavy use. Review only. No repo changes.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Evolve the engine. Don't rewrite it. The brief's hypothesis is mostly right, but it has the wrong top risk.

  1. The top risk is the store value contract, not missing hooks. Memory stores Go structs by reference. File and Postgres hand back decoded map[string]any: file does so after a restart, Postgres always. Handlers type-assert structs, so after a PERSISTENCE=1 restart, or on Postgres, they panic or silently drop data today. Blob payloads are not persisted at all. The test suite cannot see any of it. Every new type adds to this. Fix it first (ADR-004).
  2. The engine has no transport-independent entry point. It is an http.Handler and nothing more. Deployments therefore re-dispatch over httptest. RBAC and policy have nowhere to sit, and hooks are blind (no current doc, untyped errors, outside the write lock). Add Engine.Do (ADR-003).
  3. Coexistence is cheap if it is mechanically guarded. It is not a long, risky period if three guards land in Phase 1: a legacy ARM route freeze, a boot-time engine/chi overlap panic, and scope cleaners for RG cascade. With those in place, migration becomes optional per type rather than a deadline. Data-plane handlers never migrate. vm, aks and sites may stay bespoke indefinitely (ADR-007).
  4. Remove machinery, don't add it. Drop the engine's list index in favour of a prefix scan. Make api-version lists metadata, not gates. Unknown types stay strict, and passthrough is designed but not built until someone needs it.
  5. Fail closed, everywhere it matters. Engine and RBAC store reads return errors as 500s, never "not found". Unsupported policy rules are rejected, never silently non-matching. State with an old schema stops startup with a reset message, never a silent misread.
  6. Persisted state is disposable test data. A schema version stamp replaces data migrations, which removes a whole class of per-type code.

There are about 6 seams to add, not 8: Do/Resolve, Current-aware hooks under the lock, PatchMode, parent existence, Authorizer/Admitter, and Actions (Actions only lands with its first consumer).

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
Doc Decision ADR-0001 The engine is the single ARM pipeline for registered types. Guards make coexistence safe. Deployments call Dispatcher.Put in-process. ADR-0002 Strict 404 by default. Opt-in passthrough is designed but deferred until a concrete consumer exists. ADR-0003 Engine.Do, phase order, Request, hooks under the lock, Authorizer/Admitter seams. ADR-0004 Uniform JSON values on every backend, Scan, no list index, scope cleaners, a schema stamp instead of migrations. ADR-0005 Hand-written registration, api-versions as metadata, armtest conformance suite. ADR-0006 Sync only, skip-polling header, azerr.Error taxonomy. ADR-0007 Strangler pattern, a per-type recipe, waves, exit criteria. ADR-0008 Opt-in RBAC and policy enforcement, the minimum that is useful. Slice 1 Role assignments on the engine, plus opt-in enforcement. Slice 2 APIM Consumption control plane. PLAN Phased PR plan with decision gates. SPIKE The earlier spike: resource ranking, test tiers, APIM provider findings. Partly superseded; its §0 lists what changed. Scenario catalogue About 490 real-Azure scenarios per resource type, mapped to the engine, with engine lessons and a porting recipe. The acceptance list for each migration PR.

ADRs are written to be commit-safe. Suggested home: website/docs/architecture/adr/.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
# Sev Where Finding Fix 1 HIGH resourcegroups/handler.go:105; blob/handler.go:568,613,653,755,782 v.(ResourceGroup) and v.(Blob) panic after a PERSISTENCE=1 restart (file.go:39 decodes to maps) and always on Postgres. ADR-004: store.Decode[T], uniform JSON. 2 HIGH acr:224, keyvault:574,654, appconfig:119, dbpostgres:264, blob:212,353 if x, ok := v.(T); ok silently drops records in the same conditions. Lists come back short. Same as #1. 3 HIGH store/memory.go:177-182 ListKeysByPrefix returns all keys for file and Postgres. Consumers are servicebus/handler.go:198 and vm/references.go:189. Backend.Scan(prefix), with every prefix op derived from it. 4 HIGH blob/handler.go:30 Blob.Content is json:"-". Every blob is empty after a PERSISTENCE=1 restart and on Postgres. Any JSON-encoding store fix makes it fail in memory too. json:"content" plus a restart test, before the byte-KV flip (ADR-004). 5 HIGH store/file.go:33-36,39 A snapshot that fails to parse logs, starts empty, and autosave then overwrites it. Per-value decode errors are ignored. Fail startup and leave the file untouched (ADR-004). 6 HIGH resourcegroups/handler.go:141-195,170,173 Hard-coded DeleteByPrefix list. keyvault and arm: keys are missing. Imports aks and vm for cleanup (dependency inversion). Scope cleaners plus engine.DeleteScope (ADR-004). 7 HIGH .github/workflows/ci.yml:47 CI runs ./tests/... only. Unit tests under internal/ never run in CI. No race detector. Nothing exercises persisted state. go test ./..., race on internal/, and a restart round-trip test. 8 MED store/postgres.go:96,143 LIKE prefix is unescaped (_ and % in names). CountByPrefix (120) escapes, so behaviour is inconsistent. No prefix index. Shared escape helper, plus a text_pattern_ops index. 9 MED store/memory.go:142,149; file.go:51 Set swallows errors. SetIfNotExists is not atomic. Values are stored by reference, so mutating after Get races with Save's marshal. Byte-KV backends, SetNX, error-returning Lookup and Scan for engine code. 10 MED server/server.go:177-186 Routing correctness depends on middleware order. The authz middleware catches every /providers/microsoft.authorization/ path. Nothing detects overlap. Boot-time overlap guard and route freeze (ADR-001). 11 MED deployments/handler.go:188,214-218 Missing apiVersion defaults to 2023-01-01. Re-dispatch uses httptest. Nested ids are ad hoc. dependsOn is ignored. Dispatcher.Put in-process, 400 on missing apiVersion, topo sort (ADR-001). 12 MED arm/engine.go:87-95 Validate and Defaults can't see the stored doc, run outside the lock, and every error becomes 400. ADR-003 hooks. 13 MED auth/handler.go:60; identity/handler.go:~299 Every client token carries the same oid. MI tokens have no oid. Two JWT builders. Blocks any useful RBAC. One internal/token package with a per-client oid (ADR-008). 14 MED authorization/handler.go:31,206,231 Role assignment createdOn is regenerated on every PUT (drift). No 409 on duplicate. List is exact-scope only. The key is case-sensitive. Contributor has no notActions, so it is the same as Owner. Slice 1, ADR-008. 15 MED resourcegroups/handler.go:215 /resources always returns []. Engine-backed (ADR-004). 16 LOW arm/store.go The list index is a single value per parent and type: a hot row with no sub-wide list. Drop it and use a prefix scan. 17 LOW azerr No target or details. Not an error type. ADR-006. 18 LOW go.mod testcontainers (and the MySQL driver graph) sits in the main module for one integration test dir. Optional separate module for tests/integration. 19 LOW services/publicip Global counter, ignored decode errors, 202 without Location. Wave 2 migration fixes it for free. 20 INFO AzureHeaders No X-Go-Azure-Sdk-Skip-Polling-Delay, so azurerm waits about 10 s per write. One-line header (ADR-006).

From the spike, confirmed at d86ed0d. Each is a standalone fix PR with no dependencies:

# Sev Where Finding Fix 21 MED redis/handler.go:99 PUT ignores the request body. location, tags and sku are dropped, so azurerm and azapi see drift. Decode the body and echo it, keeping generated values from the stored doc. 22 LOW loadbalancer/handler.go:156,188,219,238 resourceGuid is regenerated on every PUT. Keep it from the stored doc. 23 LOW keyvault/handler.go:280 Vault PUT has no name validation (vaultNamePattern exists at :456) and no RG check. Validate the name; 404 ResourceGroupNotFound. 24 LOW website/docs/services/parity.md Lists App Service as unimplemented (sites exists) and App Config as having no labels (it has them). Update the page.

docs.title: Open verify items
docs.text:
These are tagged (verify) in the ADRs. Resolve each one with a single real ARM call or a doc check, before the PR that depends on it.

  • The real ARM error code for an unregistered type (InvalidResourceType vs NoRegisteredProviderFound).
  • Role assignment error codes: invalid name, missing role definition, invalid principal, update not permitted.
  • Role assignment list with no $filter: confirm it returns at, above and below scope. Confirm the InvalidFilter code.
  • PolicyDefinitionNotFound on a policyAssignment with a bad definition id.
  • APIM validation error code (ValidationError) and required-field rules.
  • ARM NotFound and AuthorizationFailed message wording.
  • %2F and %3B handling. ParseID uses the decoded r.URL.Path. ;rev= works decoded, but an encoded / inside a name would split. Consider RawPath if a type needs it.
  • A user-assigned identity in userAssignedIdentities that does not exist: rejected (which code) or echoed (ADR-0003).
  • A template resource without apiVersion: confirm InvalidTemplate (ADR-0001).

Resolved during review:

  • Built-in roles carry permissions[] (Contributor lacks notActions).
  • principalType is echoed, or "" when absent.
  • arm.ID parses extension resources at any resource scope.
  • The file snapshot is already map[string]json.RawMessage on disk (file.go:32), so byte-KV values load from existing snapshots without a format change.

docs.title: Phased PR plan
docs.text: Action small tasks in sets. Each PR uses a conventional-commit title, and keeps go test ./... green. Sizes: S (under 200 lines), M (200 to 600), L (over 600). A PR may start once everything in its Depends column has merged. Rows with no dependency can run in parallel.

docs.title: Phase 0: Hygiene (no behaviour change for users)
docs.text:
# PR Size Depends Notes 0.1 ci: run go test ./... with -race on internal packages S ci.yml:47 runs ./tests/... only. 0.2 fix(blob): persist blob content across restarts S Blob.Content tag becomes json:"content". Adds the restart round-trip test (create RG, blob with upload, copy and block commit, KV, ACR, appconfig and pg server; Save; reload; GET and list). A snapshot that fails to load fails startup. This replaces a backend CI matrix. 0.3 fix(store): add Decode and GetAs; fix struct-asserting call sites M Fix every site from README findings 1 and 2, and grep for .( on store.Get results. 0.4 fix(store): byte-KV backends with uniform JSON values M 0.2, 0.3 ADR-0004 §1: Scan, Lookup, SetNX, Set returns error, ListKeysByPrefix fixed. The restart test must pass unchanged. Value shapes do not change, so there is no schema bump. Fix any sites the suite surfaces in this PR. 0.5 fix(store): escape LIKE prefixes and add prefix index S Postgres only. 0.6 refactor(resourcegroups): cascade via scope cleaners S Legacy cleaners only. Removes the aks and vm imports and adds the missing keyvault cleaner. Engine docs are wired in 1.2. 0.7 feat(azerr): typed Error with target and details S Existing helpers wrap it. 0.8 feat(server): send skip-polling-delay header S One line in AzureHeaders. 0.9 build: move tests/integration to its own module (optional) S Drops testcontainers from the main go.mod. 0.10 feat(store): schema version stamp with reset-required startup error S ADR-0004 §5. Starts at 1, so state from current main is accepted.

README findings 21 to 24 (Redis PUT body, LB resourceGuid, KV name validation, parity page) are standalone fix and docs PRs. They are not gated and need no schema bump.

Gate G0:

  • CI runs the full suite with race.
  • The restart round-trip is green, including blob content.
  • The schema stamp is in place.
  • Zero struct type-asserts on store values remain (one grep, recorded in the PR).

docs.title: Phase 1: Engine foundation
docs.text:
# PR Size Depends Notes 1.1 refactor(arm): transport-independent Engine.Do and Resolve M 0.4, 0.7 ADR-0003: Request, error-returning Reader, hooks under the lock with Current, azerr errors. The HTTP adapter is thin. 1.2 refactor(arm): prefix-scan lists, subscription-wide list, scope delete M 1.1, 0.6 Drop arm:i: (leftover keys are ignored, no bump). DeleteTree always. DeleteScope, wired into RG delete ahead of the cleaners. RG existence via WithScopeExists. 1.3 feat(arm): PatchMode with RFC 7386 merge default S 1.1 PatchTags bool becomes a mode. 1.4 feat(arm): require api-version; versions as metadata; Provisioned S 1.1 Plus CheckName, DefaultIdentity, ChildID. 1.5 test(arm): armtest conformance suite M 1.2, 1.3, 1.4 Plus Registry.Types(). The policyDefinitions sample is the first consumer. 1.6 test(server): engine/chi overlap guard and legacy route freeze S Generate the initial legacy_arm_routes.txt. 1.7 feat(arm): principal context and Authorizer/Admitter seams S 1.1 Nil means allow. Principal middleware. 1.8 refactor(auth): single token package with per-client oid S The default client keeps ...0002. MI tokens gain oid. CHANGELOG.

Gate G1 (sign-off by Stu):

  • policyDefinitions passes armtest through the full server handler.
  • The hook signatures and the Type fields are frozen. Any change from here on needs an ADR-0003 amendment.
  • Startup time and RSS at idle are within 5% of main (measure: time to first 200 on /health, and RSS after 10 s).

docs.title: Phase 2: Slices
docs.text:
The two slices run in parallel. Within each, follow the Depends column.

# PR Size Depends 2.1 feat(authorization): serve roleAssignments via arm engine M G1, 0.10 2.2 fix(authorization): contributor notActions; add User Access Administrator S 2.3 feat(authorization): opt-in RBAC enforcement M 2.1, 2.2, 1.7, 1.8 2.4 feat(apim): consumption control plane via arm engine M G1 2.5 test(apim): terraform azurerm and azapi consumption fixtures S 2.4 2.6 feat(policy): policyAssignments and opt-in deny/audit enforcement M G1

Acceptance (scenarios). Each PR ports the T1/T2 rows of its catalogue page and lists the ids it ported:

  • 2.1 to 2.3: authorization. Note the real-Azure 409 RoleAssignmentExists and the type (not roleType) role-definition property.
  • 2.4, 2.5: API Management and its provider notes. Tier A only. The T3 fixtures are nightly, never per-PR.
  • 2.6: no harvested scenarios for assignments. Management-group scope for definitions is G2-T32 (management groups).

Gate G2:

  • The slices landed without new engine seams beyond ADR-0003. If they did need one, the ADR was amended first.
  • Record the actual cost per type (lines for registration, hooks and sample). If it is above about 80 lines for a simple type, revisit helpers before Phase 4.
  • Decide on the legacy Guard (ADR-0008). Build it only if enforcement on unmigrated types is requested. It is not a prerequisite for any later gate.
  • New types (the about 25 planned) may start after G2. They are engine-only, using the recipe.

docs.title: Phase 3: Platform
docs.text:
# PR Size Depends Notes 3.1 refactor(deployments): dispatch in-process via Engine.Do M G2 HTTP fallback for legacy types forwards the original Authorization header. Strip template keys. 400 on missing apiVersion. ChildID for nested ids and outputResources. 3.2 feat(deployments): order resources by dependsOn S 3.1 Topo sort. A cycle gives 400. 3.3 refactor(resourcegroups): serve resource groups via arm engine M G2 /resources from the engine. ScopeExists becomes engine-native. RG delete becomes sync 200, so drop the operationresults 202. Bumps SchemaVersion. 3.4 feat(server): derive /providers from registry S G2 Merge with the existing static list until legacy types register.

Acceptance (scenarios). 3.1 and 3.2: deployments. 3.3: resource groups. 3.4: subscriptions and providers. Conflicts to resolve first: management-group PUT/DELETE are LROs in real Azure but ADR-0006 is sync-only, and several real PUTs return 200 or 202 only (not 201), which needs a per-type status override (see engine lessons).

Gate G3:

  • An ARM template with dependsOn across an engine type and a legacy type deploys.
  • With enforcement on, RBAC and policy apply to the engine-type resources in that template, and the deny comes back as a deployment error. Legacy-type resources are not enforced unless the Guard was built (ADR-0008).
  • Decide whether roleDefinitions move onto the engine. That needs a Get fallback for built-ins. Only proceed if it is cheaper than keeping the narrowed middleware.

docs.title: Phase 4: Migration waves (parallel per type, lesser agents)
docs.text:
Follow the ADR-0007 recipe exactly. One PR per type family, titled refactor(<rp>): serve <type> via arm engine.

  • Wave 2: publicip, dns, eventgrid, redis, nsg, identity (ARM), disks.
  • Wave 4: network, networkinterfaces, loadbalancer, appgw, storageaccounts (ARM), keyvault (ARM), acr (ARM), appconfig (ARM), dbpostgres, dbmysql, sqldb, cosmosdb (ARM), servicebus (ARM), aci.

Type.Actions lands with the first listKeys consumer, which is a reviewed seam addition.

Each wave PR cites its catalogue page as the acceptance list (T1 as the Sample, T2 as tests/arm_<x>_test.go). The pages also record the bugs to fix in the same PR (for example Redis PUT ignoring the body, Cosmos container partitionKey, ACI buildResponse dropping fields).

Gate G4 (per wave):

  • The freeze file and cleaner count shrank.
  • No Type fields were added outside an ADR amendment.
  • Every PR that moved a type bumped SchemaVersion and added a CHANGELOG reset line.

docs.title: Phase 5: Heavy types and retirement
docs.text:
• Gate G5 applies per type: vm, compute, aks, sites, apps, functions. Migrate the ARM shell only on a fidelity or enforcement need (ADR-0007). Otherwise they stay bespoke.
  • Retirement PRs, each refactor(server): remove <x> when its last consumer is gone:
    • casemirror.go;
    • the authz catch-all;
    • the HTTP dispatcher fallback.

docs.title: Deferred until a concrete consumer exists
docs.text:
• Passthrough for unregistered types (MINIBLUE_ARM_PASSTHROUGH=1, ADR-0002). The design is recorded so nobody reinvents it differently. Build it when a user brings an azapi config that needs a type nobody intends to register. It is an S-sized PR touching only the chi NotFound handler.
  • Legacy Guard (ADR-0008).

docs.title: Proposed, not scheduled
docs.text: Rows suggested by the scenario catalogue (secret projection, seeded singleton children, soft-delete seam, NameTaken/ValidateLocation, provider registration state, deployments validate/cancel/export, $top/nextLink, extra armtest checks). They are proposals: each needs an owner decision, and any seam needs an ADR amendment first. New resource types listed in the catalogue (SQL, Insights, Log Analytics, Event Hubs, management groups) are engine-only registrations and may start after G2.

docs.title: Definition of done
docs.text:
Three loops. The first one keeps CI and review cheap, so do not skip it.

1. Inner loop (local, before every push). Seconds to a couple of minutes.

  • go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./internal/..., then go test ./tests -run <Type> for the area touched. CI runs go test -race ./... always. Add -race locally only where CGO is available (it needs CGO_ENABLED=1 and a C compiler).
  • New or migrated type: an armtest Sample and the T2 rows from its catalogue page.
  • Store changes: the restart round-trip test (0.2).
  • No Terraform, Docker or e2e locally. Those are CI-only.

2. PR CI (once per push).

  • Push when the inner loop is green. Then run gh pr checks <n> and wait for it. Do not poll or re-run to see if it passes.
  • On a failure, reproduce it locally, fix it in one commit, push once. A new push cancels the run in progress.
  • Terraform acceptance (acceptance.yml, acceptance-azurerm.yml) runs on a PR only when Go code, go.mod/go.sum, a Terraform fixture or example, or the workflow itself changes. ci.yml and e2e.yml skip docs-only PRs (website/**, **/*.md, issue and PR templates). All of them always run on push to main.
  • A slow fixture (API Management or similar) is never a per-PR job. Put it in a scheduled or manual workflow.

3. Review loop (after CI is green).

  • The PR description names the PLAN row, lists the catalogue ids ported, and says which (verify) marks were resolved.
  • A code-review agent checks:
    • the row's Depends were merged;
    • no Type fields, hook parameters or engine options were added without an ADR amendment;
    • every store error is checked;
    • SchemaVersion is bumped with a CHANGELOG line if the key or value shape changed;
    • the legacy route freeze file or cleaner count did not grow;
    • a Sample exists for each type touched.
  • At most two review rounds. If it is still open after that, escalate to Stu rather than iterating.
  • Stu reviews and signs off the gates (G0 to G5), not each PR.

docs.title: Rules for implementing agents
docs.text:
• Read ADR-0003, ADR-0005 and ADR-0007 before touching internal/arm or migrating a type.
  • Do not add Type fields, hook parameters or engine options without an ADR amendment PR.
  • Do not add chi ARM routes. The freeze test will fail.
  • Every new or migrated type gets an armtest Sample. Bespoke tests are only for hook logic.
  • Changing the key or value shape of an existing persisted type bumps store.SchemaVersion, with a CHANGELOG state reset required line. New types do not bump. Never write data migrations.
  • Engine and migrated code check every store error. A read error is a 500, never "not found". No persisted field uses json:"-".
  • Mark any assumed Azure error code (verify) in code comments until it is confirmed.

docs.title: Spike: what can we bring across using the ARM engine?
docs.text:
Status: input, partly superseded. This spike came before the ARM foundation ADRs. Where they differ, the ADRs and the PLAN win. §0 lists every change. The spike is still the source for the resource ranking (§3), the test tiers (§4) and the APIM provider findings (§5).

Inputs: a second Azure emulator used as inspiration only (its behaviour is not spec), the landed internal/arm engine, and the azurerm provider source (for APIM). The scenarios are in the scenario catalogue and the scenario ids below resolve there. The detailed inventory reports are not in the repo.

docs.title: 0. What the ADRs changed
docs.text: Spike said Now Where Five missing engine primitives are the bottleneck About 6 seams. The top risk is the store value contract: struct type-asserts panic or drop data after a PERSISTENCE=1 restart and on Postgres README verdict, ADR-0004 E2: accept-any api-version option; types list every client version Missing or malformed gives 400. Any well-formed version is accepted. APIVersions is metadata only ADR-0005, PR 1.4 E3: Defaults(id, body, cur) Request carries Current. Hooks run under the write lock and return azerr.Error ADR-0003, PR 1.1 E4: PATCH deep-merge, per-type opt-in PatchMode, RFC 7386 merge by default ADR-0003, PR 1.3 E6: POST actions as chi routes beside the engine Instance actions belong to the engine (Type.Actions, lands with its first consumer). Only provider-level operations (checkNameAvailability, locations/*, operations) stay as chi routes ADR-0001 E7: RequireParent opt-in, never default-on Parent and RG existence are checked for every engine type. Migration PRs fix tests that skip creating the RG ADR-0003 phase 5, ADR-0007 E0c: /resources from the registry plus legacy prefixes From the engine, when RGs move onto it PR 3.3 Stay bespoke: RG, deployments, subscriptions, auth, keyvault, network, NICs, storage, dbpostgres, aci RGs and subscriptions move onto the engine (wave 3). Role assignments move (Slice 1). Deployments stay bespoke but dispatch in-process. The ARM shells of keyvault, network, NICs, storage, dbpostgres and aci are wave 4 and optional. Data planes never move ADR-0007, ADR-0001 APIM needs no engine work and runs in parallel with it Slice 2 starts after G1 and uses Current for stable generated values Slice 2, PLAN APIM chi routes for checkNameAvailability and deletedservices The MVP needs neither. deletedservices is a strict 404 with no route. checkNameAvailability is a later PR Slice 2 ParseID must handle ;rev= and %3B ;rev= works on the decoded path. An encoded / inside a name is still open README verify list Opt-in async LRO per type; RG delete stays 202 with operationresults Sync only. RG delete becomes 200 when RGs move onto the engine ADR-0006, PR 3.3 Migrated types need a CHANGELOG note or a key shim State is disposable. A schema version stamp fails startup with a reset message. No shims, no migrations ADR-0004 §5 Conformance suite carries a CaseMode Engine responses are canonical. Moving a type off casemirror is a listed behaviour change ADR-0005, ADR-0007 Postgres LIKE wildcards unescaped (unverified) Verified README finding 8, PR 0.5 §6 phasing Replaced PLAN

docs.title: 1. Verdict
docs.text:
• Yes, a lot ports. ~25 resource types are plain registrations or hooks on the engine today or after small engine work; ~480 test scenarios were harvested (see the scenario catalogue).
  • The engine, not the resources, is the bottleneck. Five missing primitives gate ~25 rows: subscription-wide list, POST actions, parent-exists, typed hook errors, PATCH beyond tags. Land those first (S/M each).
  • APIM is feasible: medium effort, high value, and the Consumption-SKU slice needs no APIM-specific engine seams (it starts after G1, see §0). ~4 to 6 dev-days; +2 for Developer/Basic/Standard/Premium.
  • The reference is a weak oracle: no api-version validation, fully synchronous, per-service error codes, mandatory If-Match on APIM, several outright bugs. Port scenarios, assert real Azure status codes/bodies.
  • Existing hygiene bugs the spike found (fix regardless): CI never runs internal/... tests; RG delete doesn't cascade into engine-stored resources; GET …/resourceGroups/{rg}/resources always returns []; Redis PUT ignores the body; Key Vault PUT has no name/RG validation; LoadBalancer regenerates resourceGuid every PUT; parity.md is stale (App Service, App Config labels). All confirmed at review time; see README findings 6, 7, 15 and 21 to 24.

docs.title: 2. Engine work, in order
docs.text:
Superseded by PLAN Phase 1 (see §0). Kept for the Unblocks column.

# Item Size Unblocks E0a go test ./... in ci.yml (today ./tests/... only) XS engine/store/id/deployments guarded E0b RG delete → Store.DeleteTree(rgID) for engine types; add cascade test S every RG-scoped engine type E0c Back GET …/{rg}/resources with engine registry + legacy prefixes M azurerm prevent_deletion_if_contains_resources, az resource list E1 Typed hook errors {Status, Code, Message}; optional Type.NamePattern S name rules, 409s, MG/KV/EH codes E2 api-version: accept-any option; types list every version azurerm/azapi/az send (verify pins per provider release) S newer azurerm/Bicep; deployments default 2023-01-01 otherwise 400s E3 Pass stored doc to hooks (Defaults(id, body, cur)) S to M stable generated values (keys, GUIDs, createdAt) without id-derivation hacks E4 PATCH deep-merge, per-type opt-in, re-run Defaults M in-place updates (azurerm UpdateThenPoll, azapi update, az … update) E5 Sub-scope list for RG-scoped types (GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers/{ns}/{type}) M every ListBySubscription, az … list, name-uniqueness E6 POST actions: bespoke chi routes beside the engine work today (unregistered action paths fall through); later Type.Actions S per action / M generic listKeys, regenerateKey, listSecrets, checkNameAvailability E7 Opt-in RequireParent (case-insensitive RG resolver; legacy tests PUT under unregistered RGs, so never default-on) M ResourceGroupNotFound/ParentResourceNotFound negative paths E8 Generic provisioningState: Succeeded default; sync 200/201 is enough for azurerm/azapi pollers. Async headers only where a poller truly needs a URL (disk diskOperations) S to M removes per-type boilerplate E9 Registry.Types() + internal/arm/armtest table-driven conformance suite (§4) M every type forced through one contract Later Singleton/auto-created children, secret redaction (SecretPaths), opt-in ETag/412 (never require If-Match), $top/$skip/nextLink, soft-delete hooks, stateful provider registration (+optional 409 gate) M each per-type, as needed

Not needed: LRO/202 machinery for the MVP types, $filter beyond role definitions.

docs.text:
Fit: P plain registration (no hooks), H hooks, G engine-gap (needs E-items), B bespoke. Value = azurerm/azapi/bicep/SDK users. Scenario ids refer to the catalogues.

Rank Resource Fit Value Effort Needs Scenarios Notes 1 API Management (service, apis, operations, products, namedValues, backends) H H M (4 to 6 d) G1 (Slice 2) APIM-T* (52) see §5 2 roleDefinitions / roleAssignments → engine H H M G1 (Slice 1) G1-T48…56 narrows the authorization middleware to roleDefinitions; duplicate → 409 RoleAssignmentExists 3 Management Groups (+ policyDefinitions at MG scope = one-line scope-mask change) H/B H M to L E1, E7, delete/GET hooks, subscription-association move, root group G2-T1…33 engine id model already parses tenant/MG scope;
