firewall rules not in reference but required by azurerm 7 ServiceBus subscriptions, rules ($Default), authorizationRules+listKeys H H S to M auto-children, E6 G3-T83…94 ARM subscription DELETE required for azurerm destroy (reference lacks it) 8 ManagedIdentity federatedIdentityCredentials; Redis firewallRules; fix Redis PUT body H M to H S none G2-T113…127 workload-identity/GitHub OIDC value 9 App Configuration ARM: 4-key set, PATCH, soft-delete/deletedConfigurationStores/purge (409 when protected), replicas G M M E6, soft-delete hook G1-T1…23 data-plane labels/revisions/lock (409 key-locked)/snapshots: bespoke, G1-T24…30 10 ACR: name/location validation, PATCH, listCredentials/regenerateCredential, listUsages H/G M S to M E1, E6 G1-T79…97 name 5 to 50 alnum 11 Cosmos ARM: throughputSettings, InvalidKeyKind G M M E6 G1-T98…110 data-plane SQL query subset (~20 scenarios) is bespoke, L 12 Storage ARM: PATCH, regenerateKey, checkNameAvailability, SAS list actions, ARM queues/tables B M M keep keys + creationTime across PUT G3-T39…50 stays bespoke (shared-key coupling, PUT must return 200) 13 Availability sets (+VM membership), VNet PATCH/peerings/delegations, subscription locations, provider registration state H M S to M side-effects for VM link G3-T101…118, X34…36 14 Disk diskOperations poll + 409 on active SAS; ACI start/stop/restart/logs + first ACI tests; App Service list-by-sub G L to M S to M E5, E6 G1-T33…78 fills zero-test ACI gap 15 Key Vault keys + certificates data plane (Go crypto/*) B H L none G2-T94…102 biggest data-plane gap; not an engine job

Migrate-only (no new user value, do opportunistically): publicip, nsg(+securityRules child), eventgrid ARM, dbmysql stub, dns, disks. Stay bespoke (as revised by ADR-0007, see §0): data planes (blob/queue/table, KV secrets, and so on), deployments, and vm/aks/sites/apps unless a fidelity or enforcement need arises (G5). The ARM shells of keyvault, network (inline+child subnet sync), NICs, storage, dbpostgres and aci are wave 4.

Skip: LoadBalancer content (miniblue is already a superset; add PATCH tags + sub list only), RESP2/AMQP servers, RBAC data-plane enforcement, portal/MCP/CLI-wrapper suites, subscription create/cancel/PATCH (not real ARM).

docs.title: 4. Test cases to bring across
docs.text:
Method: scenarios only, re-written as our own tests asserting real-Azure contracts (reference tests are SDK-driven with weak assertions).

Tier Where What Count (approx) T1 conformance internal/arm/armtest (table-driven, needs Registry.Types()) One sample per registered type; asserts PUT 201/200, GET, list, DELETE 200/204, canonical casing, missing or malformed api-version 400, name/id mismatch 400, children cascade, PATCH; options for ETag/paging; coverage test fails build if a type has no sample. Reference has no generic contract tests, so this is net-new 25 (X1…X27) T2 per-resource tests/arm_<x>_test.go via real server (pattern: tests/arm_policydefinition_test.go) Scenario catalogue pages (see catalogue), ported as raw-HTTP httptest ~330 T3 Terraform acceptance tests/terraform/{azurerm,azapi}/<case>/ New: azurerm/{apim-consumption,sql,servicebus,app_configuration,container_registry,cosmosdb,mgmt-group}, azapi/{servicebus,storage_account_basic,virtual_network_basic,apim}, azurerm_availability_set in compute, negative fixture (invalid name must fail with surfaced 400). Batch azapi into one job (each fixture = a full CI job today); TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR; nightly latest-provider ~12 fixtures T4 client smoke tests/sdk/go, Python, scripted az Go SDK (armresources, policy defs: LRO polling, ID casing, 404 after delete), Python SDK, az cloud register + version matrix. Harness: CA-bundle trust per client (SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, certifi for az, AZURE_CORE_INSTANCE_DISCOVERY=false); document the matrix in acceptance-tests.md 3 suites T5 deployments extend bespoke handler validate, exportTemplate, cancel/HEAD, subscription scope. what-if is out of scope (needs async, ADR-0006) ~15 (X40…48)

CI cost rule: T1/T2 run in default CI (seconds, in-process). T3 fixtures are opt-in per case; anything >2 min goes nightly. Never run long-provisioning resources against real Azure from this repo's CI or from agents.

docs.title: 5. API Management
docs.text:
MVP (Consumption, sku_name = "Consumption_0"): Microsoft.ApiManagement/service (2024-05-01 + extras) with children apis→operations, products→apis, namedValues, backends (children 2022-08-01, backends also 2024-05-01; add 2021-08-01, 2023-05-01-preview, 2023-09-01-preview, 2024-06-01-preview so az/bicep users don't get InvalidApiVersionParameter).

Findings that shape the design (from the provider source, v5.10.0):

  • No LRO needed. Sync 200/201 + provisioningState: Succeeded, no Azure-AsyncOperation/Location. DELETE: 200 existed / 204 absent (engine already); a bare 202 routes azurerm into its own 20 s poller. Optional response header X-Go-Azure-Sdk-Skip-Polling-Delay: true. A malformed Location with asyncId on API PUT would trigger the provider's custom poller: never emit one.
  • Provider dereferences without nil checks → Defaults must always supply: service customProperties ({}), api authenticationSettings{oAuth2AuthenticationSettings:[],openidAuthenticationSettings:[]}, subscriptionKeyParameterNames{header:"Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key",query:"subscription-key"}, protocols:["https"], type:"http", isCurrent. Service defaults: virtualNetworkType=None, publicNetworkAccess=Enabled, derived gatewayUrl/managementApiUrl/scmUrl/portalUrl/developerPortalUrl, TEST-NET publicIPAddresses, identity via DefaultIdentity with Current (ADR-0003).
  • API names carry ;rev=N (apis/echo;rev=1): ParseID handles ;rev= on the decoded path; keep a test that echoes the original id. Alias apis/echo ⇄ current revision for CLI/Bicep.
  • If-Match: azurerm sends * only on API create/update, nothing on DELETE. Never require it (reference does → breaks terraform destroy). Optional 412 on mismatch behind an ETag flag.
  • Create flow also: GET deletedservices/{name} (404/403 tolerated), list+delete of apis and products (must return {"value":[]}; don't seed any), so types must be registered. deletedservices stays always-404 in MVP; purge_soft_delete_on_destroy documented unsupported.
  • Provider-level routes, after the MVP (ADR-0001 allows them; deletedservices needs none, strict 404 is enough): POST …/providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/checkNameAvailability (regex ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9]$, 1 to 50; AlreadyExists by subscription scan), GET …/deletedservices/{n}.
  • Tier B (Developer_1+): portalsettings/{signin,signup,delegation} (GET must work without a prior PUT; PUT returns 200 only), POST portalsettings/delegation/listSecrets, tenant/access GET/PATCH + POST …/listSecrets (id, enabled, primaryKey, secondaryKey). All seeded-default GETs.
  • Out of scope: gateway runtime (reference has none), subscriptions/users/groups/policies/diagnostics/certs (+1 week), secret masking, backup/restore.
  • Test plan: T1/T2 APIM-T* (name rules, required fields, ;rev, defaults round-trip, product state honoured, cascade delete, checkName). T3: azurerm/apim-consumption fixture with timeouts{} blocks (real provider timeouts are 3 h create/update/delete, so the emulator must answer instantly or CI hangs); Developer_1 fixture nightly only. Real APIM provisioning (30 to 60+ min; Consumption much faster) is documented, never run.
  • Reference deviations to avoid: inverted checkNameAvailability validity, forced product state, malformed async Location, plaintext secrets.

docs.title: 6. Phasing
docs.text: Replaced by PLAN. The cheap-win bundle in §3 (Insights, LogAnalytics, EventHub, MI FIC, Redis firewall, SQL firewall, ServiceBus subscriptions/rules, availability sets) is the first batch of new types after G2.

docs.title: 7. Risks / open items
docs.text:
• Resolved by the ADRs: migrated-type state (schema stamp, ADR-0004 §5), Postgres LIKE escaping (PR 0.5), casing (canonical, ADR-0005), deployments' default api-version and template keys (PR 3.1), authorization middleware ordering (overlap guard, PR 1.6).
  • Terraform acceptance is Linux/WSL only; cold go build ./... ~3 min on this box. Iterate with in-process tests.
  • Verify before asserting (could not fetch REST specs in this spike): APIM name/enum casing and error codes, latest api-versions per type, azurerm/azapi api-version pins per release, Management Group error codes, real-Azure status codes marked "(verify)" in the reports.
  • Unverified reference inferences: SQL admin password echo on GET; expectations for non-MG group-2 tests came from names/control-plane code, not assertion bodies.
  • Licence: the reference is Apache-2.0 (compatible with MIT). Only scenarios were extracted; no code or test bodies copied. If anything is ever copied verbatim, keep its notice/NOTICE obligations.

docs.title: ADR-0001: The engine is the single ARM pipeline
docs.text: Status: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ARM requests reach miniblue through three uncoordinated paths:

  1. The engine middleware (server.go:181) serves registered types (policyDefinitions today).
  2. The authorization middleware (server.go:186) catches every /providers/microsoft.authorization/ path.
  3. chi routes, wrapped by CaseInsensitiveARM(routeTrie) (server.go:85, casemirror.go), for 37 service packages.

Correctness depends on middleware order. Nothing detects when a newly registered engine type shadows a chi route, or the reverse.

Deployments (server.go:243, deployments/handler.go:214-218) re-enter the server through httptest to create each template resource. That loses the caller principal, re-parses HTTP, and couples deployments to routing details.

docs.title: Boundary
docs.text:
The engine owns every resource instance, collection and instance action of a registered type, at every scope.

Service packages keep:

  • data-plane routes (blob, queue, table, KV secrets, and so on);
  • provider-level non-resource operations: checkNameAvailability, operationResults, locations/*/usages, deletedservices if ever needed.

One rule, applied per type: once a type is registered, its chi ARM routes are deleted in the same PR.

docs.title: Guards (land in Phase 1, before any new type)
docs.text:
1. Overlap guard. At boot, chi.Walk the router. For every route:

    • substitute placeholders with sample values;
    • run arm.ParseID and registry.Lookup;
    • panic if a registered type matches.

    This is about 40 lines in internal/server/guard.go. It costs microseconds at startup.

  2. Legacy route freeze. internal/server/testdata/legacy_arm_routes.txt lists the current chi ARM patterns, one per line, sorted. A test walks the router:

    • a pattern that is not in the file fails, with "register an arm.Type instead";
    • a pattern that is in the file but no longer routed passes, with a hint to delete the line.

    The file only shrinks. Provider-level operations are exempt, so service packages can still add them: a pattern is skipped when the first segment after providers/{namespace}/ is locations, operations or checkNameAvailability.

  3. Scope cleaners for RG and subscription cascade (ADR-0004). This removes the hard-coded delete list.

Engine middleware stays first. The authz middleware narrows over time to roleDefinitions only (ADR-0008).

docs.title: Deployments call the pipeline in-process
docs.text:
// internal/arm
type Dispatcher interface {
    Put(ctx context.Context, id, apiVersion string, body map[string]any) (int, map[string]any, error)
}

The server provides the implementation:

  • if engine.Resolve matches, it calls engine.Do;
  • otherwise it falls back to the existing HTTP dispatcher, for legacy types only. The fallback copies the original request's Authorization header, so the principal survives the hop.

The fallback is deleted when the freeze file is empty of types used in templates.

Deployment handler changes:

  • Strip template-only keys before the body is sent: apiVersion, type, dependsOn, condition, copy, comments, scope.
  • Missing apiVersion gives 400 InvalidTemplate (verify code). Remove the 2023-01-01 default (deployments/handler.go:188).
  • Nested ids come from one helper, arm.ChildID(parent ID, typeName, name string). It is used for both PUT and outputResources (deployments/handler.go:87,110).
  • Order: topo-sort on dependsOn (resourceId or name). On a cycle, return 400 InvalidTemplate.
  • Principal: the caller principal flows via ctx, so RBAC and policy apply to template resources.

docs.title: End state
docs.text:
Delete each of these once its last consumer migrates (ADR-0007; casemirror stays if wave 5 stays bespoke):

  • casemirror.go;
  • the authorization catch-all middleware;
  • the RG hard-coded delete list;
  • the HTTP dispatcher.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One place to add ARM behaviour. RBAC and policy cover every migrated type automatically.
  • Legacy types keep working unchanged. Migration becomes per-type and optional (ADR-0007).
  • Coexistence risk turns into two failing tests and a boot panic, not reviewer vigilance.
  • Deployments become testable without HTTP and can enforce RBAC and policy.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives
docs.text:
• Two systems by design (bespoke handlers as first-class peers): every ARM behaviour (casing, PATCH, cascade, errors, RBAC, policy, sub-wide lists) gets implemented twice, forever.
  • Bespoke handlers as engine plugins (an engine that routes to http.Handler per type): the engine gains a second dispatch model, and handlers still own the behaviours. Hooks are the plugin model.
  • Big-bang rewrite of all 37 packages: 424 store call sites, high regression risk, no user-visible gain for data-plane code.
  • Engine after chi (NotFound fallback): the reverse is safer. New types win, and the guard stops accidental shadowing either way.
  • Keep HTTP re-dispatch for deployments: untestable without a server, and the principal survives only through a copied header. It is kept only as a fallback for legacy types.

docs.title: ADR-0002: Unregistered types are strict; passthrough is designed but deferred
docs.text: Status: Proposed (strict default). Passthrough deferred until a concrete consumer exists.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
azapi is a generic client: any type@apiVersion, body passthrough, read-back after PUT, POST actions, read-modify-write updates, and list. Verified against the azapi provider source (v2.8 and upstream main):

  • Client-side gating. schema_validation_enabled (default true) validates type and api-version against embedded bicep-types before any request. A typo never reaches the server.
  • Create: GET (404 means proceed), then PUT (200, 201 or 202 accepted), then GET read-back. A 404 on read-back drops the resource from state.
  • Sync polling. The azcore poller treats a 200/201 without async headers as complete.
  • Read: the response is merged into the configured body (ignore_missing_property defaults to true), so extra server fields don't cause drift. A location change forces replacement.
  • Update (azapi_update_resource): GET, then merge, then a full PUT, then GET. No PATCH.
  • Delete: 200, 202 and 204 are accepted. 404 is tolerated.
  • Action (azapi_resource_action): any method at {id}/{action}. 200, 201, 202 and 204 are accepted.
  • List (azapi_resource_list): GET {parentId}/providers/{type} (including subscription-wide), following nextLink.

So azapi needs: a GET that returns 404 for missing resources, round-trip storage, full-PUT replace, sync status codes, and lists at parent and subscription scope.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Default: strict. An unregistered Ns/type returns 404 InvalidResourceType (verify the exact ARM code; NoRegisteredProviderFound is the candidate) through the normal chi NotFound path.

Deferred: MINIBLUE_ARM_PASSTHROUGH=1. Not built until a user brings an azapi config that needs a type nobody intends to register. Every planned type is registered, so until then passthrough would be untested code with no caller. The design is recorded here so the eventual PR is S-sized and nobody invents a different shape. The chi NotFound handler tries the passthrough engine last:

// internal/arm/passthrough.go
func (e *Engine) Passthrough() http.Handler // synthesises a Type per request
  • Synthesised Type: any scope, Patch: PatchMerge, no hooks. api-version is required but not checked against a list.
  • Ops: PUT, GET, DELETE, list at parent, list subscription-wide. POST actions return 404. Fabricated action results would mislead users more than a clear failure.
  • Storage: the same arm:r: keys as registered types. When the type is registered later, existing data is served unchanged.
  • Logs one WARN per new type: passthrough type Microsoft.Foo/bars; register it for fidelity.
  • Because it is reached via NotFound, it can never shadow a legacy chi route or a registered type.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Clear failures by default. No silent fake fidelity.
  • When passthrough is built, azapi users can unblock themselves for long-tail types with one env var, and its WARN logs show what to register next.
  • About 60 lines when built. No new dependency.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives
docs.text:
• Permissive by default: typos in tests that bypass azapi validation (raw SDK, REST) succeed silently. It hides gaps and invites "works in miniblue, fails in Azure".
  • Validate bodies against bicep-types: a large embedded dataset (tens of MB) or startup cost, against the constraints. azapi already does this client-side.
  • Passthrough via engine middleware (before chi): it would shadow legacy handlers.
  • Fabricated 200 for POST actions: wrong data that looks plausible is worse than a 404.
  • Build passthrough now, in Phase 1: speculative. No user or planned type needs it yet.

docs.title: ADR-0003: Pipeline phases and hooks
docs.text: Status: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
internal/arm is an http.Handler and nothing else. In engine.go:74-119:

  • Validate(id, body) and Defaults(id, body) run before and outside the write lock;
  • they cannot see the stored document;
  • every error becomes 400 (engine.go:87).

That blocks:

  • defaults that must be stable across PUTs (generated URLs, principalIds, createdOn);
  • update rules ("principalId cannot change") and uniqueness checks (409);
  • typed errors (404 parent, 409 conflict);
  • RBAC and policy;
  • in-process callers such as deployments.

docs.title: Transport-independent core
docs.text:
package arm

type Op uint8

const (
    OpGet Op = iota
    OpList
    OpPut
    OpPatch
    OpDelete
    OpAction
)

type Request struct {
    Op         Op
    ID         ID         // instance id; for OpList the parent scope
    Type       *Type
    APIVersion string
    Action     string     // OpAction only
    Query      url.Values
    Principal  Principal
    Body       map[string]any // decoded request (UseNumber)
    Current    map[string]any // stored doc; nil on create
    Doc        map[string]any // proposed doc; hooks mutate this
    Store      Reader
}

type Reader interface { // lock-free reads; backend errors are returned, never swallowed
    Get(id ID) (map[string]any, bool, error)
    Children(parent ID, typeName string) ([]map[string]any, error)
    Under(scope ID, typeName string) ([]map[string]any, error) // subscription or RG wide
}

// Resolve does routing and api-version presence. ok=false means "not ours".
func (e *Engine) Resolve(method, path string, q url.Values) (r *Request, ok bool, err error)
func (e *Engine) Do(ctx context.Context, r *Request) (status int, body any, err error)
func (e *Engine) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) // Resolve, decode, Do, write

The HTTP adapter stays thin, about 40 lines. Deployments and tests call Resolve and Do directly.

docs.title: Phase order
docs.text:
# Phase Runs Failure 1 route Resolve not ours, so fall through 2 api-version Resolve 400 MissingApiVersionParameter or InvalidApiVersionParameter (malformed only, see ADR-0005) 3 decode adapter 400 InvalidRequestContent 4 authorize Authorizer, no lock 403 AuthorizationFailed 5 lock, load Current, scope and parent existence ScopeExists, Reader 404 ResourceGroupNotFound, ParentResourceNotFound, ResourceNotFound 6 shape engine 400 (envelope, name/id mismatch). PATCH merge per Type.Patch. 7 admit Admitter (PUT and PATCH) 403 RequestDisallowedByPolicy 8 validate Hooks.Validate the returned *azerr.Error. A plain error becomes 400 InvalidRequestContent. 9 defaults engine (Provisioned), then Hooks.Defaults none 10 persist, unlock store 500 11 after Hooks.After, no lock logged only

GET, List and DELETE run phases 1, 2, 4, 5 and 10 (DELETE only).

Any Reader or store error in any phase gives 500 InternalServerError. Failures are never treated as "not found" or "no assignments".

Existence checks in phase 5 are deliberately narrow, so that coexistence with legacy types works:

  • Child types (declared via Children): the parent doc must exist in the engine store. Otherwise 404 ParentResourceNotFound. The parent is always an engine type by construction.
  • RG and subscription scope: ScopeExists is called. The server wires the RG check.
  • Extension resources at resource scope (e.g. a roleAssignment on a legacy vault): not existence-checked. The scope may be a legacy resource that the engine cannot see. This is documented as a known deviation until a cross-system resolver is justified.

Authn is not a phase. A small, always-on middleware puts a Principal on ctx (from oid, else sub, read from the unverified bearer). It never fails a request.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
type Hooks struct {
    Validate func(ctx context.Context, r *Request) error
    Defaults func(ctx context.Context, r *Request) error // error only for read failures
    After    func(ctx context.Context, r *Request)
}

Rules, stated in the package doc:

  • Validate and Defaults run under the engine write lock and see Current.
  • They read via r.Store, or via a read-only resolver owned by the same package (e.g. legacy custom role definitions). They never write, and never call Do.
  • Defaults must be idempotent. Generated values (ids, keys, URLs, timestamps) are copied from Current when it is present. armtest checks this (ADR-0005).
  • After runs post-commit, outside the lock. Failures are logged, never returned.

docs.title: Type gains
docs.text:
type PatchMode uint8

const (
    PatchMerge PatchMode = iota // RFC 7386 merge onto Current
    PatchTags                   // only tags may change
    PatchNone                   // 405
)

type ActionFunc func(ctx context.Context, r *Request) (status int, body any, err error)

type Type struct {
    // existing: Name, APIVersions, Scopes, Children, Hooks
    Patch       PatchMode                                           // replaces PatchTags bool
    Provisioned bool                                                // stamps properties.provisioningState=Succeeded
    List        func(ctx context.Context, r *Request) ([]map[string]any, error) // optional filter override
    Actions     map[string]ActionFunc                               // land with first consumer
}
  • Existing registrations with PatchTags: true become Patch: PatchTags.
  • Types relying on today's no-PATCH behaviour set PatchNone explicitly.

docs.title: Seams for RBAC and policy
docs.text:
type Principal struct{ ObjectID, TenantID, AppID string }

func WithPrincipal(ctx context.Context, p Principal) context.Context
func PrincipalFrom(ctx context.Context) Principal

type Authorizer interface {
    Authorize(ctx context.Context, p Principal, action string, scope ID) error
}
type Admitter interface {
    Admit(ctx context.Context, r *Request) error
}

func New(reg *Registry, st *Store, opts ...Option) *Engine
func WithAuthorizer(a Authorizer) Option
func WithAdmitter(a Admitter) Option
func WithScopeExists(f func(ctx context.Context, scope ID) (bool, error)) Option
  • A nil Authorizer or Admitter means allow. A nil ScopeExists means every scope exists.
  • The server wires an RG check backed by the resourcegroups store until RGs move onto the engine.
  • Action strings: {type}/read, {type}/write, {type}/delete, {type}/{action}/action. A list is {type}/read at the parent scope.

docs.title: Shared helpers (not Type fields)
docs.text:
func CheckName(name string, re *regexp.Regexp, min, max int) error // 400 InvalidResourceName
func DefaultIdentity(doc, cur map[string]any, uami IdentityLookup)
func ChildID(parent ID, typeName, name string) ID

// IdentityLookup returns a user-assigned identity's principalId and clientId. Nil is allowed.
type IdentityLookup func(id string) (principalID, clientID string, ok bool)

DefaultIdentity semantics (exact, so implementations cannot drift):

  • No-op when doc.identity is absent, or its type is None. The client's removal stands.
  • SystemAssigned in type: set principalId and tenantId. Copy them from cur.identity if Current also had SystemAssigned, else generate a new UUID and use the default tenant.
  • UserAssigned in type: for each key of userAssignedIdentities, set principalId and clientId from uami(key). Azure echoes the identity resource's own ids, and Terraform configs often cross-reference them. If the lookup is nil or misses, copy from the same key in Current, else generate UUIDs. Whether Azure rejects a missing identity is (verify).
  • Never adds an identity block the client did not send.

The server builds one IdentityLookup over the identity service. It reads legacy keys today and engine docs after wave 2, so callers never change.

docs.title: Headers and preconditions
docs.text:
• If-Match is ignored, and never required (azurerm APIM always sends If-Match: *).
  • If-None-Match: * on an existing resource gives 412 PreconditionFailed.
  • The engine never sends ETags until a type needs them.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One function is the ARM contract. HTTP, deployments and tests all exercise the same code.
  • Hooks can express real ARM rules (immutable fields, 409, stable generated values) without bespoke handlers.
  • Writes are serialised across all engine types by one mutex. That is acceptable for an emulator, and keeps hooks race-free with no per-type locking.
  • Hook authors must not do slow I/O under the lock. This is documented and code-reviewed.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives
docs.text:
• Hooks outside the lock with optimistic retry: more code and subtle bugs, for throughput nobody needs.
  • Authorize under the write lock: a write racing a concurrent role revocation is indistinguishable from one that arrived a moment earlier. Real Azure RBAC is eventually consistent too. Authorizing before the lock keeps reads and writes on one code path.
  • Per-type mutexes: cross-type validation (role definition lookup, parent existence) would need lock ordering.
  • A middleware chain (func(next) Handler) per phase: flexible but opaque ordering. That is the current problem, moved inward.
  • NamePattern, Immutable []string or Unique fields on Type: each one is a one-line hook. Declarative fields grow into a DSL.
  • A separate arm.Error type: duplicates azerr. Extend azerr instead (ADR-0006).
  • An authn phase that rejects requests: a non-goal. Real auth is out of scope, and a missing token resolves to the default principal.

docs.title: ADR-0004: Storage contract
docs.text: Status: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
internal/store has three backends (memory, file, Postgres) behind an interface{} API used at 424 call sites in 47 files. They disagree on what a value is:

  • Memory stores Go values by reference.
  • File wraps memory (file.go:13). It holds live structs until restart, then load (file.go:39) decodes into interface{}, giving maps and float64s, and ignores decode errors.
  • Postgres always returns decoded interface{}.
  • Struct-asserting handlers break after a PERSISTENCE=1 restart, and always on Postgres.
    • They panic at resourcegroups/handler.go:105 and blob/handler.go:568,613,653,755,782.
    • They silently drop records at acr:224, keyvault:574,654, appconfig:119, dbpostgres:264 and blob:212,353.
    • The test suite runs memory only and never restarts, so it cannot see this.
  • Mutating a value after Get changes memory without Set. Save marshals the live map while handlers mutate those values, which is a data race.
  • ListKeysByPrefix (memory.go:177-182) returns all keys for file and Postgres.
  • Set (memory.go:142) swallows errors. SetIfNotExists (:149) is a non-atomic Exists-then-Set.
  • Blob payloads are not persisted. Blob.Content is tagged json:"-" (blob/handler.go:30). Memory holds the live struct, so tests pass, but every blob is empty after a PERSISTENCE=1 restart and on Postgres. Any JSON-encoding store change makes this fail in memory too.
  • A corrupt snapshot starts empty, and autosave then overwrites it (file.go:33-36). Per-value decode errors are ignored (file.go:39).
  • Postgres prefix matching is inconsistent. ListByPrefix (postgres.go:96) and DeleteByPrefix (:143) use unescaped LIKE, while CountByPrefix (:120) escapes. There is no index usable for prefix LIKE.

The engine store (internal/arm/store.go) keeps docs at arm:r:<lower id> as JSON strings, plus a list index as one value per arm:i:<parent>|<type>. That index is a hot row, has no subscription-wide view, and DeleteTree only runs for types with children.

RG delete (resourcegroups/handler.go:141-195):

  • is a hard-coded prefix list;
  • imports aks and vm for cleanup;
  • misses keyvault and arm: keys.

/resources (:215) returns [].

docs.title: 1. Backends are byte KV stores; Store owns encoding
docs.text:
package store

type KV struct {
    Key   string
    Value []byte // JSON
}

type Backend interface {
    Get(key string) ([]byte, bool, error)
    Set(key string, v []byte) error
    SetNX(key string, v []byte) (bool, error) // atomic; Postgres: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
    Delete(key string) (bool, error)
    Scan(prefix string) ([]KV, error) // sorted by key
    DeleteByPrefix(prefix string) (int, error)
    Reset() error
}
  • The current 9-method Backend shrinks to 7. Exists, List, ListByPrefix and CountByPrefix become Store methods derived from Get and Scan.
  • File keeps wrapping memory. Its snapshot becomes a plain copy of map[string][]byte, with no live structs and no race.
  • The snapshot file format is unchanged. The loader already decodes map[string]json.RawMessage (file.go:32), and each RawMessage is now the stored value as is. The schema stamp (§5) is an ordinary key, so it works the same on file and Postgres, with no file envelope.
  • A snapshot that fails to load fails startup. The file is left untouched. Starting empty and autosaving over the user's state is data loss.
  • Store.Set(key string, v any) error marshals and returns an error. Existing statement calls still compile, so there is no churn at the call sites, and it logs on failure. The engine and every migrated handler must check it and return 500.
  • Store.Get(key string) (any, bool) unmarshals fresh on every call, the same as file-after-restart and Postgres today (json.Unmarshal into any). Every backend now behaves identically, so memory-only tests catch persistence bugs. Its signature stays for the 424 legacy call sites; a backend error is logged and reported as a miss.
  • Engine and migrated code read through Store.Lookup(key) ([]byte, bool, error) and Store.Scan, which propagate errors. A backend failure is a 500, never "not found" or "empty list". That matters most for RBAC and policy, where a swallowed scan error would read as "no deny".
  • No persisted type may use json:"-". Blob.Content becomes json:"content" (base64 in JSON, about 33% larger, which is fine at emulator scale). A blob restart test covers upload, copy and block commit. This lands before the byte flip.
  • ListByPrefix, ListKeysByPrefix and CountByPrefix derive from Scan. That fixes finding #3 by construction.
  • Typed access for handlers:
func Decode[T any](v any) (T, error)                  // fast path: v.(T); else JSON round trip
func GetAs[T any](s *Store, key string) (T, bool, error)

Order matters:

  1. Fix Blob.Content and add the restart round-trip test. It passes on current main for everything except blob.
  2. Add Decode and fix the known struct-asserting sites. That works before and after the flip.
  3. Flip memory to bytes.
  4. Fix whatever the test suite then surfaces.

docs.title: 2. Postgres
docs.text:
• key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value JSONB is unchanged. Bytes go in and out as JSONB text, with no interface{} round trip.
  • One likePrefix(s string) string escape helper, used by Scan, DeleteByPrefix and Count.
  • CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS kv_key_prefix ON kv (key text_pattern_ops). The PK btree cannot serve LIKE 'x%' under non-C collations.
  • Scan uses ORDER BY key.
  • Single writer. One miniblue process per database. A shared database across processes is unsupported and documented. The engine mutex is in-process.

docs.title: 3. Engine store
docs.text:
• Drop arm:i: index keys. Leftover keys in existing state are never read, so no schema bump is needed.
  • Docs stay at arm:r:<lower id>, stored as a JSON string. This preserves exact numbers through Postgres JSONB and float64 decoding.

Lists come from a prefix Scan plus a depth filter:

List Prefix Filter Top-level at scope <scope>/providers/<ns>/<type>/ no further / Child <parent>/<childType>/ no further / Subscription-wide, RG-scoped type /subscriptions/<s>/resourcegroups/ parsed type == T, depth 1 /resources in RG /subscriptions/<s>/resourcegroups/<rg>/providers/ top-level only
  • DeleteTree(id) always runs: Delete(id) plus DeleteByPrefix(id + "/"). The / boundary keeps rg from deleting rg2, and armtest checks it.
  • Engine.DeleteScope(scope ID) deletes every engine doc under a scope (DeleteByPrefix(scope + "/")).
  • /resources returns engine resources only. Legacy types appear as they migrate. That is better than [] today.

docs.title: 4. Cascade via scope cleaners
docs.text:
// package resourcegroups
type Cleaner func(sub, rg string)

func New(st *store.Store, eng *arm.Engine, cleaners ...Cleaner) *Handler
  • Each legacy service exports its own cleaner, for example aks.CleanupRG or keyvault.CleanupRG (the latter is added, since it is missing today).
  • The server builds the list.
  • resourcegroups stops importing aks and vm.
  • RG delete runs eng.DeleteScope(rg) and then the cleaners.
  • A migrated type deletes its cleaner in the same PR.

docs.title: 5. State is disposable: a schema stamp, not migrations
docs.text:
Persisted state is test data. It does not need to survive an upgrade that changes its shape, but it must never be silently misread. Misread state is how a migrated type returns 404 and Terraform quietly recreates resources.

// internal/store/schema.go
const SchemaVersion = 1 // bump when the key or value shape of an existing persisted type changes

func CheckSchema(s *Store, location string) error // called once at startup, before serving
  • Empty store: write meta:schema = SchemaVersion.
  • Stamp matches: continue.
  • No stamp on a non-empty store: treat it as version 1. That is state written by current main, which has the same shape. Stamp it and continue.
  • Stamp differs: fail startup, leaving the store untouched. The message names both versions and how to reset, for example: state in ./data/state.json is schema 2; this miniblue needs 3. Delete the file (or TRUNCATE kv on Postgres) and restart. There is no auto-wipe flag.

Bump rules:

  • Moving an existing type onto the engine bumps the version. Its keys change.
  • Adding a new type, or a new field that old readers tolerate, does not.
  • Every bump adds a CHANGELOG line: state reset required: <why>.

Test: one table test covering the empty, matching, unstamped and mismatched cases, asserting that the store is unchanged on mismatch.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• PERSISTENCE and Postgres become as reliable as memory, and the default test run proves it.
  • Shared-map races disappear. The cost is a JSON encode or decode per call. That is negligible at emulator scale, so it is not benchmarked unless a regression shows up.
  • Engine lists get simpler and gain subscription-wide and /resources for free.
  • RG cascade becomes complete and stays decoupled.
  • Upgrades that move a type need a state reset. Startup says so explicitly instead of serving 404s.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives
docs.text:
• Rewrite all 424 call sites to typed repositories now: right in the long term, wrong before expansion. The uniform contract plus Decode[T] gets the safety at a fraction of the cost.
  • Keep the list index and add subscription and type indexes: more keys to keep consistent, plus hot rows, to speed up scans that are already cheap.
  • Postgres-native schema (sub, rg and type columns): backend-specific behaviour and migrations, for no emulator benefit.
  • Store arm: docs as JSONB objects: float64 decoding corrupts large integers and json.Number semantics.
  • RG cascade via global DeleteByPrefix on every service prefix: this is today's approach, and it is exactly what misses keyvault.
  • Lazy, on-read migration of legacy keys: each type would need read fallbacks forever, which defeats the strangler exit.
  • Per-type data migrations (a migrations registry, planned key moves, case-collision detection, fixture tests for each): real code and tests on every migrated type, all to preserve disposable test data. Decision: state does not need to survive shape changes.
  • Raw-byte side keys for blob content: Postgres stores JSONB, so a raw value needs a second column or table. Base64 in JSON keeps one contract on every backend.

docs.title: ADR-0005: Type metadata and the conformance suite
docs.text: Status: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
There are about 25 new types to add, and each one needs the same ARM behaviours to be right:

  • casing;
  • PUT create vs replace;
  • list at the parent scope and subscription-wide;
  • PATCH semantics;
  • cascade;
  • the error envelope;
  • provisioningState.

The engine registers types by hand (registry.go). Register panics on malformed metadata. lookup is private, and there is no Types(). APIVersions currently gates requests the wrong way round: an unknown version gives 400, while a missing version is accepted.

Only tests/arm_policydefinition_test.go exercises the engine, and that one test is bespoke.

docs.title: Hand-written registration, one file per RP
docs.text:
// internal/services/apim/types.go
func Register(reg *arm.Registry) {
    reg.Register(arm.Type{
        Name:        "Microsoft.ApiManagement/service",
        APIVersions: []string{"2024-05-01", "2022-08-01"}, // latest first; metadata
        Scopes:      arm.ScopeResourceGroup,
        Provisioned: true,
        Hooks:       arm.Hooks{Validate: validateService, Defaults: defaultService},
        Children: []arm.Type{
            {Name: "apis", Children: []arm.Type{{Name: "operations"}}},
            // ...
        },
    })
}
  • The server calls each package's Register.
  • Add Registry.Types() []*Type, sorted by name. It is used by armtest coverage and, later, by /providers.

docs.title: api-version is metadata, not a gate
docs.text:
• Missing: 400 MissingApiVersionParameter.
  • Malformed (not YYYY-MM-DD with an optional -preview or similar suffix): 400 InvalidApiVersionParameter.
  • Any well-formed version is accepted. APIVersions feeds /providers output and armtest, and nothing else.

Why: clients (azapi schema validation, the SDKs) already pin versions. Gating rots with every SDK bump, and miniblue serves one shape per type regardless of version.

docs.title: internal/arm/armtest (non-test package)
docs.text:
package armtest

type Sample struct {
    Type    string            // full type name, e.g. "Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/apis"
    Scope   arm.Scope         // zero = first declared scope
    Body    map[string]any    // valid create
    Update  map[string]any    // valid replace, differs from Body
    Invalid map[string]any    // optional; Validate must reject it with 400
    Skip    map[string]string // check name -> reason (reason required)
}

func Run(t *testing.T, h http.Handler, reg *arm.Registry, samples []Sample)
func Coverage(t *testing.T, reg *arm.Registry, samples []Sample) // every registered type has a Sample
  • h is the full server handler, so middleware order, casing and headers are covered.
  • Parents are created from their own Samples. The RG is created with a PUT on the RG endpoint.
  • Names are unique per check, so checks share one server, and t.Parallel() is safe.
  • There is no Options struct. Expectations derive from Type metadata: Patch mode, Provisioned, Children, and Scopes.

Checks:

Check Asserts PutCreate / PutReplace 201 then 200. Replace drops fields absent from Update. id, name and type stay canonical. Get / GetMissing 200 round trip; 404 ResourceNotFound with the envelope UrlCasing Upper-cased path segments resolve to the same resource. Response casing is preserved. List / ListSubscription {"value":[...]} at the parent. Subscription-wide for RG-scoped top-level types. Delete / DeleteMissing 200, then 204 (or 200/204 per type) MissingAPIVersion 400 MissingApiVersionParameter NameIDMismatch 400 BadBody Non-JSON gives 400 InvalidRequestContent. Invalid gives 400. Patch Per mode: merge result, tags-only, or 405 ParentMissing Child PUT without a parent gives 404 ParentResourceNotFound ChildCascade Deleting the parent removes its children RGCascade Deleting the RG removes the resource PrefixSibling Deleting x leaves x2 DefaultsIdempotent PUT the same body twice; the GETs are equal apart from updatedOn-like fields declared in Skip ProvisioningState properties.provisioningState == "Succeeded" when Provisioned ErrorEnvelope Every 4xx has {"error":{"code","message"}} and x-ms-request-id

Where tests live:

  • tests/arm_conformance_test.go calls Run and Coverage with every RP's samples.
  • The samples sit beside it, in tests/armsamples_<rp>_test.go.
  • The engine-level concurrency test stays as a single test in internal/arm.

The cost of a new type is the registration, any hooks, and one Sample of about 15 lines. Bespoke tests are written only for hook logic.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Uniform behaviour is enforced, not reviewed. "Lesser agents" can add types safely.
  • The coverage test fails if a type is registered without a sample.
  • Run time scales linearly with the number of types. Expect well under 1 s for about 60 types in-process.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives
docs.text:
• Codegen from the azure-rest-api-specs repo or bicep-types: large inputs, a build step, and the generated validation is still not behaviour. Hand-written types are about 20 lines each.
  • Loading bicep-types at runtime: tens of MB of data plus startup cost.
  • api-version allow-list gating: rots, has no behavioural payoff, and clients already validate.
  • A strict flag for gating: YAGNI.
  • Per-type hand-written CRUD tests: duplicative, and they drift from each other.
  • An armtest.Options struct: a second source of truth beside Type.

docs.title: ADR-0006: Synchronous LRO and error taxonomy
docs.text: Status: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
LRO. Real ARM returns 201 or 202 plus Azure-AsyncOperation or Location for long-running writes. Clients handle synchronous terminal responses fine:

  • azapi and azcore: a 200 or 201 with no async headers is done.
  • go-azure-sdk (azurerm): a 200 or 201 with provisioningState: Succeeded is done. Its provisioningState poller otherwise waits about 10 s per write, unless the response carries X-Go-Azure-Sdk-Skip-Polling-Delay: true. A bare 202 with no Location is a trap. publicip does exactly that.

Errors. internal/azerr (errors.go) writes {"error":{"code","message"}} through per-status helpers.

  • There is no error type, so the engine and hooks cannot return typed failures.
  • There is no target or details.
  • NotFound says "under resource group" for every scope (errors.go:25).

docs.title: Sync only
docs.text:
Op Status PUT 201 create, 200 replace PATCH 200 DELETE 200 when it existed, 204 when missing Action 200 with a body, 204 without GET, List 200
  • The engine never returns 202 and never sends Azure-AsyncOperation or Location.
  • Provisioned types stamp provisioningState: Succeeded (ADR-0003).
  • AzureHeaders middleware sets X-Go-Azure-Sdk-Skip-Polling-Delay: true on every response. Other clients ignore it. This is the cheapest speed-up available for azurerm suites. Land it in Phase 0.
  • Legacy async flows (RG delete operationresults, KV soft-delete) stay bespoke until they migrate.
  • A future Type.Async is gated on a concrete client that fails without 202. None is known.

docs.title: One error type
docs.text:
package azerr

type Error struct {
    Status  int     `json:"-"`
    Code    string  `json:"code"`
    Message string  `json:"message"`
    Target  string  `json:"target,omitempty"`
    Details []Error `json:"details,omitempty"`
}

func (e *Error) Error() string { return e.Code + ": " + e.Message }

func New(status int, code, format string, args ...any) *Error
func Write(w http.ResponseWriter, err error) // *Error as-is; anything else becomes 500 InternalServerError and is logged
  • The existing helpers (WriteError, NotFound, BadRequest and so on) become one-line wrappers over Write. Legacy call sites are untouched.
  • The engine writes errors only via Write. Hooks return *azerr.Error (ADR-0003 phase 8).
  • NotFound messages are built from the arm.ID, scope-aware: "under resource group 'rg'" only at RG scope (verify exact ARM wording).

docs.title: Taxonomy (engine-emitted)
docs.text:
Status Codes 400 InvalidRequestContent, MissingApiVersionParameter, InvalidApiVersionParameter, InvalidResourceName, InvalidParameter (with target), plus type-specific codes from hooks 403 AuthorizationFailed, RequestDisallowedByPolicy 404 ResourceNotFound, ResourceGroupNotFound, SubscriptionNotFound, ParentResourceNotFound, InvalidResourceType (verify) 405 MethodNotAllowed 409 Conflict, plus type-specific codes (e.g. RoleAssignmentExists) 412 PreconditionFailed 500 InternalServerError

Types add codes in their hooks. There is no central registry of codes.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Deterministic, fast tests. azurerm and azapi both complete without polling.
  • No fake operation-status endpoints to maintain.
  • Hook authors get one obvious way to fail.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives
docs.text:
• Simulated async (202 plus operation status): more code and slower tests, with no client that needs it. A non-goal.
  • Configurable latency: a non-goal. Real LRO timing is out of scope.
  • A separate arm.Error: duplicates azerr and needs mapping both ways.
  • Sentinel errors plus an engine-side mapping table: hooks cannot attach target or type-specific codes.
  • Sending the skip-polling header only on ARM writes: needs path classification for zero benefit.

docs.title: ADR-0007: Migration strategy (strangler)
docs.text: Status: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
There are 37 service directories. Most mix ARM control plane, data plane and provider-level operations. Sizes run from policy (13 lines) to vm (1907). Store access is spread across 424 call sites.

A big-bang move is out (ADR-0001). The risk is a long coexistence period, so it has to be cheap and mechanically safe.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. After gate G1, no new chi ARM routes. The legacy route freeze test enforces this (ADR-0001). New types go on the engine.
  2. Data plane never migrates. blob, queue, table, KV secrets/keys/certs, appconfig KVs, servicebus messaging, ACR registry API, cosmos data, auth and metadata stay chi.
  3. Migration is per type and optional. A type moves when it is touched for fidelity, for RBAC or policy coverage, or as part of its wave.
  4. State changes bump the schema version. Persisted state is disposable test data. It is reset, never migrated, and never silently misread (ADR-0004 §5).

docs.title: Per-type recipe (the PR checklist)
docs.text:
1. Add Register in internal/services/<rp>/types.go: Type, Scopes, Patch mode, Provisioned.
  2. Add an armtest Sample in tests/armsamples_<rp>_test.go.
  3. Port the validation, defaults and actions into hooks. Read through r.Store. Copy generated values from r.Current.
  4. Delete the chi ARM routes and their lines in legacy_arm_routes.txt. Keep the data-plane and provider-level routes.
  5. Bump store.SchemaVersion and add a CHANGELOG line: state reset required: <type> moved to the ARM engine.
  6. Remove the type's prefixes from the package's RG cleaner. Delete the cleaner if it is now empty.
  7. Existing tests/ stay green. Any intentional behaviour change (fidelity fix) is listed in the PR body and the CHANGELOG. A test that PUTs without creating its RG now gets 404 ResourceGroupNotFound: fix the test setup, not the engine.
  8. PR title: refactor(<rp>): serve <type> via arm engine. Behaviour changes go in a separate fix(<rp>): ... commit.

docs.title: Waves
docs.text:
Wave Content Why here 0 Foundation: store contract, CI, azerr, guards, Engine.Do (PLAN phases 0 and 1) Everything else depends on it 1 Slices: roleAssignments, APIM Consumption, policyAssignments Prove hooks, seams and new-type cost 2 Simple leaves: publicip, dns (zones plus record sets), eventgrid, redis, nsg plus rules, identity (userAssignedIdentities ARM), disks Low coupling. They exercise the recipe and migrations. 3 Platform: resourcegroups and subscriptions on the engine, deployments on Do with dependsOn, /providers from the registry Enables ScopeExists without a callback, and in-process deployments 4 Cross-referencing control plane: network (vnets/subnets), networkinterfaces, loadbalancer, appgw, storageaccounts ARM, keyvault ARM, acr ARM, appconfig ARM, dbpostgres, dbmysql, sqldb, cosmosdb ARM, servicebus ARM, aci Need Reader cross-lookups and Actions (listKeys) 5 Heavy: vm, compute, aks, sites, apps, functions Gate G5, below

Gate G5. Migrate only the ARM shell of a wave-5 type when one of these holds:

  • a fidelity bug needs engine behaviour (PATCH, cascade, sub-wide list);
  • or enforcement coverage is requested and the legacy guard (ADR-0008) is not enough.

Otherwise the type stays bespoke. A bespoke type then:

  • registers a scope cleaner;
  • stays in the freeze file;
  • is covered by casemirror.

docs.title: Tracking
docs.text: Progress is the line count of legacy_arm_routes.txt plus the number of cleaners. No separate tracker.

docs.title: Exit
docs.text:
• casemirror.go, the authz catch-all middleware, the RG hard-coded list and the HTTP dispatcher fallback are deleted once their last consumer migrates.
  • If wave 5 stays bespoke, casemirror remains, serving only those routes. That is acceptable.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Coexistence has no deadline and no cliff. Every intermediate state is tested and shippable.
  • The freeze file and the cleaners make the remaining legacy surface explicit.
  • Wave work is mechanical enough for lesser agents to do with the recipe alone.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives
docs.text:
• Migrate everything before adding new types: it delays APIM and the new types for weeks of no-op churn.
  • Never migrate, and add new types only on the engine: RBAC, policy, cascade and sub-wide list would stay split forever. Waves 2 to 4 are cheap with the recipe.
  • Migrate by package rather than by type: the large packages (network, vm) would become unreviewable PRs.
  • A compatibility layer that serves legacy keys through the engine: read fallbacks forever, to preserve disposable data.

docs.title: ADR-0008: RBAC and Policy, the useful minimum
docs.text: Status: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
RBAC today (internal/services/authorization/handler.go):

  • Nine built-in role definitions are synthesised with permissions[] (:30-38). Contributor has empty notActions, so it is the same as Owner.
  • Role assignments are CRUD only, stored at authorization:roleAssignment:<scope as sent>:<name>. The key is case-sensitive.
  • createdOn is regenerated on every PUT (:206), so there is drift.
  • There is no duplicate check, the list is exact-scope only, and a delete of a missing assignment returns 404.
  • There is no enforcement.

Tokens. auth/handler.go:60 gives every client token the same oid/sub (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002). MI tokens (identity/handler.go:~299) carry sub = principalId and no oid. There are two separate JWT builders.

Policy. Only policyDefinitions exists, as an engine type. There are no assignments and no evaluation.

The useful target: let users test "this principal can't do that" and "this policy denies that" locally, without emulating Azure's full semantics.

docs.title: RBAC
docs.text:
Role assignments move onto the engine (Slice 1). roleDefinitions stay in the narrowed authz middleware until a Get-fallback seam for built-ins is justified (gate G3).

Built-ins. Keep them synthesised. Fix Contributor notActions to:

  • Microsoft.Authorization/*/Delete
  • Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write
  • Microsoft.Authorization/elevateAccess/Action

Add User Access Administrator (18d7d88d-d35e-4fb5-a5c3-7773c20a72d9: */read, Microsoft.Authorization/*, Microsoft.Support/*).

Enforcement is off by default. MINIBLUE_RBAC=enforce wires an arm.Authorizer:

// internal/services/authorization/enforce.go
type RoleResolver func(id string, scope arm.ID) (map[string]any, bool, error)

type Enforcer struct {
    Store arm.Reader   // engine roleAssignments
    Roles RoleResolver // built-ins, plus custom roleDefinitions wherever they live today
    Admin string       // MINIBLUE_RBAC_ADMIN, default 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002
}

func (e *Enforcer) Authorize(ctx context.Context, p arm.Principal, action string, scope arm.ID) error

Roles is Handler.ResolveRoleDefinition. Custom role definitions stay at legacy keys until they migrate, and arm.Reader cannot see those keys. Injecting the resolver keeps the Enforcer indifferent to where definitions live. When roleDefinitions migrate, only the resolver body changes.

  1. If p.ObjectID == e.Admin, allow (implicit Owner at /). Default usage keeps working with enforcement on.
  2. Walk scope and then each Parent() up to the tenant. At each level, collect roleAssignments where principalId == p.ObjectID.
  3. Resolve each roleDefinitionId with e.Roles (built-in or custom). An unresolvable definition grants nothing.
  4. Allow if any permission block has an actions match and no notActions match.

  5. Otherwise return 403 AuthorizationFailed:

    The client '{oid}' with object id '{oid}' does not have authorization to perform action '{action}' over scope '{scope}' or the scope is invalid.

    (verify wording)

Any read or resolver error returns 500. It is never treated as "no assignments" (fail closed).

Matching:

  • case-insensitive, where * matches any run of characters including /;
  • it is a custom matcher of about 15 lines, because path.Match stops at /.

Out of scope: dataActions, deny assignments, ABAC conditions, groups, PIM, and data-plane enforcement.

Tokens: one internal/token package replaces both builders.

type Claims struct{ OID, Sub, TID, AppID, Aud string /* ... */ }

func Issue(c Claims) string                 // alg none, as today
func Parse(bearer string) (Claims, bool)    // no signature check
  • Client tokens: oid = uuid.NewSHA1(tenantUUID, client_id). The google/uuid package is already a dependency. The default client miniblue keeps ...0002, so existing users see no change.
  • MI tokens: oid = principalId.
  • CHANGELOG: non-default client ids now get distinct, stable oids.

Legacy guard (optional, not on any gate's critical path). authorization.Guard(a arm.Authorizer, ad arm.Admitter) func(http.Handler) http.Handler applies the same checks to legacy chi ARM routes. It derives the action from the method and from arm.ParseID(path). Build it only if users ask for enforcement on unmigrated types. Until then, enforcement covers engine types only, and the user docs say so. That includes resources created through deployments: the in-process Dispatcher.Put carries ctx (and so the principal) into Engine.Do. The HTTP fallback forwards the original Authorization header, so a Guard, if built later, sees the same principal.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments becomes an engine type at MG, subscription and RG scope. Validate checks that policyDefinitionId resolves (400 PolicyDefinitionNotFound, verify).

Unsupported rules fail closed, at configuration time. A silent "doesn't match" is a false allow, which is the worst outcome for a test tool. policy.Compile(def, params) (Rule, error) turns a definition plus assignment parameters into an evaluable rule. It returns an error for any construct outside the subset below: unknown aliases, operators, functions, value, count, and the denyAction effect.

  • Enforcement on: policyAssignment Validate calls Compile. An unsupported rule gives 400 MinibluePolicyUnsupported, naming the construct. The code is deliberately emulator-specific, so nobody mistakes it for Azure behaviour.
  • Evaluation compiles again, because the definition may have changed since assignment. A compile failure there gives the same 400. It never allows.
  • Enforcement off: assignments are CRUD only and Compile is not called, so any definition can be assigned.

Enforcement is off by default. MINIBLUE_POLICY=enforce wires policy.Admitter, which runs on PUT and PATCH proposed docs (r.Doc):

  1. Collect assignments at the resource's scope and its ancestors. Skip any whose notScopes prefix the resource id.
  2. Compile, then evaluate policyRule.if against r.Doc.
  3. Resolve the effect, which may be [parameters('effect')]:
    • deny: 403 RequestDisallowedByPolicy, with the assignment and definition ids in details. With enforcementMode: DoNotEnforce, deny becomes audit.
    • audit: log one line.
    • disabled: nothing.
    • modify, append, deployIfNotExists, auditIfNotExists and manual never block a request in Azure either. They are treated as disabled and logged once per definition.

Language subset:

Construct Supported Logical allOf, anyOf, not Fields type, name, location, kind, tags, tags['k'], tags.k, identity.type, <type>/sku.name, <type>/sku.tier Operators equals, notEquals, in, notIn, like, notLike, contains, notContains, exists (case-insensitive) Functions [parameters('x')] only
  • Anything outside this table is a Compile error (see above). Nothing evaluates as "missing" or "no match" by accident.
  • value, count and policy set definitions are deferred.

Package layout:

  • internal/services/policy/eval.go (about 200 lines, Compile plus evaluation), with a table-driven test that includes the unsupported cases.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Users can test least-privilege and deny-policy behaviour locally, opt-in, with zero cost when off. A nil Authorizer or Admitter means allow.
  • Distinct oids make multi-principal tests possible.
  • Enforcement covers engine types only. Coverage grows as types migrate, and the optional Guard covers legacy types if users ask for it.
  • Policy users whose definitions use constructs outside the subset get a clear 400 when enforcement is on, never a silent pass.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives
docs.text:
• RBAC on by default: it breaks every existing user whose client id is not the default.
  • Full ARM action catalogue (an operations list per RP): large and unmaintainable. Derived {type}/read|write|delete actions are what built-in roles mostly use.
  • Real token signing and validation: real authn is a non-goal.
  • Heuristic alias mapping (<type>/x to properties.x): right often enough to mislead.
  • Unsupported policy input evaluates as "no match" (fail open): a user would believe a deny policy works when it never fires.
  • Making the legacy Guard a gate prerequisite: it doubles the enforcement surface for types that are about to migrate anyway.
  • modify, append and deployIfNotExists: they mutate requests or create resources. Explicitly out of scope.
  • Policy evaluation on GET (compliance state): not useful without the remediation machinery.

docs.title: Scenario catalogue
docs.text:
Behaviour scenarios harvested from a review of a second Azure emulator, rewritten as real-Azure assertions and mapped to the ARM engine. Each page lists a service's resource types, miniblue's gaps and the scenarios a migration PR should port. Another emulator's behaviour is a prompt, not a spec: where it differs from real Azure, the page asserts real Azure and notes the pitfall.

493 scenario ids: 478 from the review (kept as is, so earlier references still resolve) and 15 marked new. Nothing was run against real Azure. About 450 (verify) marks remain, to be resolved against the REST specs or a single real call before the PR that depends on them.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
A PR that registers or migrates a type:

  1. Open the type's page. Read Types (fit, ADR seams needed) and miniblue gaps.
  2. Port its T1 rows as the armtest Sample and its T2 rows as tests/arm_<x>_test.go, as in tests/arm_policydefinition_test.go. T3 rows become Terraform fixtures only where the page says so.
  3. List the ids ported in the PR description. Resolve each (verify) you touch, or leave it.
  4. Do not port a row marked Dropped, bespoke data plane (unless the PR is about it) or "do not implement".

Ids: G1-T*, G2-T*, G3-T* by service group, APIM-T*, X* for cross-cutting. *-N* is a scenario added during cataloguing. Tiers: T1 engine conformance (armtest, generic), T2 per-resource HTTP test in-process, T3 Terraform acceptance (opt-in, nightly if over about 2 minutes), T4 client smoke (SDK or az), T5 deployments.

Never run long-provisioning resources (API Management and similar, 30 to 60+ minutes) against real Azure from CI or from agents. The emulator answers instantly; the scenarios assert that.

docs.text: Page Content Cross-cutting The engine contract (X1 to X27, the armtest rows), RG, provider, deployment and hierarchy behaviours, client smoke. 52 / 3. Client suites Multi-client smoke pattern (Go SDK, Python SDK, az, PowerShell, Terraform), CA-bundle trust, CI cost classes, ordered adoption backlog. Start here if you only read one page.

docs.title: What the harvest says
docs.text:
• Most types are hooks plus a few shared seams. The seams not yet in an ADR are secret projection, seeded singleton children, a soft-delete path, a NameTaken/ValidateLocation helper, stateful provider registration and $top/nextLink. See the cross-check in Engine lessons.
  • Several real PUTs are 200 or 202 only (Disk, Web API, Cosmos accounts, Storage accounts, Service Bus children). The engine's 201-on-create default needs a per-type override, and whether azurerm tolerates 201 for them is (verify).
  • Typical drift sources azurerm and azapi expose: handlers that drop properties they do not model, Defaults that regenerate GUIDs or keys per PUT, container PUTs that ignore the body (Cosmos, Redis, ACI). Each page lists the existing miniblue instances.
  • Real Azure divergences worth asserting rather than copying: role-assignment duplicates are 409 RoleAssignmentExists; getEntities is POST; a missing delete is 204 or 200, not 404; a bare 202 without a poll URL hangs azurerm; If-Match must never be required (it breaks terraform destroy).
  • Test cost: T1 and T2 are seconds and belong in default CI; Terraform fixtures are opt-in and batched; the API Management and Developer-tier fixtures are nightly at most.

docs.title: API Management: provider notes
docs.text:
How the azurerm provider (and azapi) drive APIM, and what a miniblue response must contain for them to finish. This backs the scenarios in API Management and the hooks in Slice 2; it does not repeat the slice's defaults table or its short client-behaviour list.

Source: the azurerm v5.10.0 and go-azure-sdk read made during the spike, spot-checked against azurerm main for the API resource (If-Match, ;rev= path) and the service resource (deleted-service lookup, purge flag, tenant_access gating). Line-level details drift between releases, so each claim not re-checked is tagged (verify) against the release a fixture pins. Nothing here was run against Azure.

docs.title: azurerm_api_management (service)
docs.text:
Provider timeouts: create, update, delete 3 h; read 5 min.

Step Calls miniblue must Create GET service (expects 404); GET locations/{loc}/deletedservices/{n}; PUT service 404 on the first GET; 404 on the deleted-service GET (404 or 403 is tolerated; a 200 fails the create unless recover_soft_deleted is set); PUT => 201 with provisioningState=Succeeded Create cleanup LIST apis, DELETE each with deleteRevisions=true; LIST products, DELETE each with deleteSubscriptions=true both lists return {"value":[]}, so apis and products must be registered even if nothing is seeded Create, non-Consumption and non-V2 only PUT portalsettings/signin, PUT portalsettings/signup; PUT portalsettings/delegation and PATCH tenant/access only when configured Tier B routes (see below) Update GET service, then PATCH with sku, tags, properties, identity PatchMerge; the PATCH response is 200 (the spec also allows 202, avoid it) Read GET service; GET policies/policy?format=xml (404 tolerated) every field in the next table present or nil-safe Delete GET service, then DELETE; with purge_soft_delete_on_destroy, GET then DELETE on deletedservices/{n} DELETE => 200 existed, 204 missing. Purge mode is unsupported in Slice 2 because the post-delete GET deletedservices must succeed

The PUT body always carries sku{name,capacity}, location, tags, identity and properties{publisherName, publisherEmail, publicNetworkAccess, customProperties, certificates, disableGateway, virtualNetworkType}, plus hostnameConfigurations, additionalLocations, notificationSenderEmail and similar only when configured. azapi and bicep users often omit customProperties, so Defaults must add {}.

docs.title: What Read dereferences
docs.text: Read field Why it must be present properties.customProperties dereferenced without a nil check (verify); must be an object even when the client sent none. Client keys stay verbatim; missing keys read as false gatewayUrl, gatewayRegionalUrl, portalUrl, developerPortalUrl, managementApiUrl, scmUrl exported as attributes; azapi response_export_values reads them too. Exact URL shapes are verify; the provider copies strings publicIPAddresses, privateIPAddresses, notificationSenderEmail, minApiVersion, zones exported; nil-safe, but real Azure returns them hostnameConfigurations handled nil-safe and filtered for defaults; emit only what the client sent identity read back; principalId and tenantId must not change between PUTs (use DefaultIdentity with Current) sku exported as Name_Capacity; Consumption capacity is 0

docs.title: API, operation, product, backend, named value
docs.text:
Resource Create Update Read Delete azurerm_api_management_api (30 min) GET apis/{name};rev={rev} (expects 404), then PUT same path with If-Match: * (non-import path) PUT with If-Match: * (import variant sends none) GET apis/{name};rev=N DELETE with no If-Match; 404 tolerated _api_operation, _product, _backend plain PUT, accepts 200 or 201 plain PUT, no If-Match GET, nil-safe DELETE with no If-Match; product adds deleteSubscriptions=true _named_value PUT, accepts 200, 201 or 202, treated as long-running same GET; does not read value when secret=true DELETE with no If-Match
  • API revision defaults to "1", so the path is always …/apis/{name};rev=1. The name segment is opaque: key on the decoded segment, echo it in id and name. ; is kept raw by some clients and %3B encoded by others.
  • API Read dereferences authenticationSettings.oAuth2 and .openid through a pointer chain (verify). Defaults must return authenticationSettings with both authentication-settings arrays empty. Also default subscriptionKeyParameterNames, type, isCurrent, protocols and subscriptionRequired (values in the slice's hooks table).
  • API body fields azurerm sends: displayName, path, protocols, serviceUrl, subscriptionRequired, apiRevision, apiRevisionDescription, apiVersion, apiVersionDescription, apiVersionSetId, subscriptionKeyParameterNames, authenticationSettings, contact, license, termsOfServiceUrl, type, description, sourceApiId.
  • Named value body: {displayName, value or keyVault, secret, tags}. A child with no provisioningState counts as succeeded.

Status codes the go-azure-sdk accepts:

Operation Accepted service PUT 200, 201 service PATCH 200, 202 service DELETE 200, 202, 204 deleted-service purge 200, 202, 204 child PUT 200, 201 (named value also 202) child DELETE 200, 204 portalsettings/{signin,signup,delegation} PUT 200 only every listSecrets 200

docs.title: Polling and headers
docs.text:
Client path Behaviour go-azure-sdk, 200 or 201 with Azure-AsyncOperation or Location long-running poller, initial wait is Retry-After or 10 s go-azure-sdk, PUT, PATCH or POST returning 200 or 201 with a JSON body provisioningState poller: re-GET after 10 s; Succeeded or absent is done; Failed or Canceled is an error go-azure-sdk, DELETE 200, 201, 202 or 204 with no polling headers poll GET until 404 (10 s initial) azurerm service delete returning 201 or 202 custom poller on Azure-AsyncOperation or Location, needs an absolute URL, 20 s interval (verify) azurerm API PUT whose Location carries an asyncId query parameter custom poller that re-GETs with ?asyncId= until 200 (verify) azapi and azcore 200 or 201 without async headers is complete

So: synchronous 200 or 201 with provisioningState: Succeeded, no Azure-AsyncOperation, no Location, never 202 (ADR-0006). The global X-Go-Azure-Sdk-Skip-Polling-Delay: true header removes the 10 s waits on service and named-value writes. The acceptance runner also sets GO_AZURE_SDK_SKIP_POLLING_DELAY=true, so CI is fast either way.

docs.title: Tier B reads (non-Consumption, non-V2 SKUs)
docs.text:
Read adds these calls, all of which must succeed without a prior PUT. Seed them in code (no stored document needed) once the seeding seam exists.

Call Response azurerm needs GET portalsettings/signin properties.enabled GET portalsettings/signup properties.enabled, termsOfService{enabled, consentRequired} GET portalsettings/delegation properties{url, subscriptions{enabled}, userRegistration{enabled}}; read even when never configured POST portalsettings/delegation/listSecrets validationKey GET tenant/access id, properties{enabled, id}; must succeed with no prior PUT POST tenant/access/listSecrets id, enabled, primaryKey, secondaryKey; the model is dereferenced, so all four fields

tenant_access is rejected by the provider itself for Consumption and V2 SKUs, so Tier A never sees it. Portal-settings PUT returns 200 only; the SDK accepts no 201.

docs.title: azapi
docs.text:
• Create: GET (404 proceeds), PUT (200 or 201), GET read-back. Update: GET, merge, full PUT, GET (no PATCH). Delete tolerates 200, 202, 204 and 404.
  • response_export_values returns whatever the service GET carries, so derived URLs and identity ids must be real strings.
  • Schema validation is client-side, so an unknown type or version never reaches miniblue. Versions to exercise: 2024-05-01 for the service, 2022-08-01 for children, plus one preview such as 2023-05-01-preview to confirm any well-formed version is accepted (ADR-0005).

docs.title: API Management
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks for every Tier A type (service, apis, operations, products, namedValues, backends), passthrough for products/apis, engine-gap for the Tier B singletons and listSecrets. miniblue today: none (no internal/services/apim, no registration, no test, no Terraform fixture). Suggested wave: Slice 2 (PLAN 2.4 and 2.5) for Tier A; Tier B and the follow-on types after G2.

The MVP slice (types, hooks, defaults, acceptance, PRs) is in Slice 2 and is not repeated here. This page holds the full resource table, every APIM-T scenario with its tier, the cost-tier test plan and the pitfalls. Provider call sequences and the defaults azurerm dereferences are in API Management: provider notes.

Gateway runtime is out of scope. No proxying through APIs, no policy execution, no subscription-key validation, no *.azure-api.net host handling. The derived gatewayUrl is a string that does not resolve. Policies are stored as opaque XML. Nothing on this page covers a data plane.

Tiers used below: Tier A is the Consumption SKU path (Consumption_0), Tier B adds what azurerm needs for Developer_1 and above (portal settings, tenant access, listSecrets).

Everything without an azurerm resource (workspaces, portal configs, content types, templates, notifications) is reachable only through azapi and bicep. Those clients can hit any type at any api-version the type lists.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value. There are no existing APIM bugs to cite: the repo has no APIM code.

  • No Microsoft.ApiManagement registration, so every azurerm, azapi and bicep call falls through to the not-found path. Slice 2 closes this for Tier A.
  • Every service GET must carry the fields azurerm dereferences (customProperties, derived URLs, stable identity). That needs Request.Current (ADR-0003) so generated values survive repeated PUTs.
  • azurerm updates the service with PATCH of sku, properties, identity and tags. Needs PatchMerge (PLAN 1.3). azapi azapi_update_resource sends a full PUT instead.
  • No tests/terraform/azurerm/apim_consumption or azapi APIM fixture, and no matrix entry in .github/workflows/acceptance-azurerm.yml.
  • deletedservices is a strict 404 with no route (Slice 2). Soft-delete, purge and recover_soft_deleted have no seam: Hooks has no delete-time hook, so this needs an ADR-0003 amendment or a bespoke route.
  • checkNameAvailability is not served. It is a provider-level route, so it stays a chi route (ADR-0001) and is a later PR.
  • Tier B has no seam: seeded singletons that GET 200 before any PUT, and listSecrets. chi ARM routes are frozen after G1 (ADR-0001), so this needs Type.Actions plus a seed mechanism (ADR amendment).
  • ETag and HEAD: the engine sends no ETags and has no HEAD op (ADR-0003). Optional for azurerm, needed only for the ETag scenarios marked deferred below.
  • Secret masking, paging ($top, $skip, nextLink) and $filter are not available. Documented deviations.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text: Ids are stable. Tier is the test layer (T1 armtest row, T2 tests/arm_apim_test.go httptest or hook unit test, T3 Terraform, T4 client smoke). "Slice 2" in Notes means the scenario is inside the Consumption MVP; everything else is follow-on or deferred.
