docs.title: Cost-tier test plan
docs.text:
Real APIM provisioning is never run from this repo, CI or an agent: Developer, Basic and Standard take 30 to 60+ minutes to create (Premium and multi-region longer, delete and purge also slow), and even Consumption takes minutes. azurerm's own timeouts are 3 h for service create, update and delete and 30 min for children. miniblue answers instantly, so the only cost is the harness.

Tier What runs Where Cost Cadence Default CI armtest Samples for all 7 Slice 2 types (Run, Coverage, ChildCascade, ListSubscription); hook unit tests; httptest scenarios tagged T1 or T2 above tests/armsamples_apim_test.go, internal/services/apim/*_test.go, tests/arm_apim_test.go seconds, in-process, under 3 s for the APIM set every PR Opt-in fixture azurerm apim_consumption; azapi apim_service_api; the negative terraform validate case tests/terraform/azurerm/apim_consumption, tests/terraform/azapi/apim_service_api, one matrix entry each about 1 to 2 min, dominated by terraform init and provider download; run.sh step limit is 600 s (run.sh:107) and the job limit 15 min (acceptance-azurerm.yml:23) on demand; not in default CI (Slice 2) Nightly apim_developer (Developer_1, tenant_access, sign_in); apim_purge once soft-delete exists; latest-provider run same tree longer, more endpoints, higher drift risk scheduled, never PR-blocking Never real-Azure provisioning, VNet, zonal or multi-region, az apim against a live service none 30 to 60+ min and real cost documentation only

Fixture rules:

  • Every APIM fixture sets timeouts { create = "5m" update = "5m" delete = "5m" read = "2m" } on the service and children. A hung or 202-without-status response then fails in minutes instead of waiting out the 3 h provider default. The 10 min step limit and 15 min job limit remain the backstop.
  • run.sh already exports GO_AZURE_SDK_SKIP_POLLING_DELAY=true (run.sh:102) and runs apply, plan -detailed-exitcode (must be 0), a second apply and destroy (run.sh:117). The global skip-polling header (ADR-0006) protects users who run the provider directly.
  • Pin the provider exactly, as existing fixtures do (azurerm = 5.10.0, azapi = 2.13.0), and commit .terraform.lock.hcl: run.sh refuses a fixture without one (run.sh:29).
  • Test data: subscription 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, RG apim-rg, location westeurope, service names apimtest-<n>, publisher Tests and admin@example.test.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Never require If-Match. The spec marks it optional on PUT and required on PATCH and DELETE, but azurerm sends * only on API create and update and sends nothing on any DELETE. Requiring it on update or delete breaks terraform destroy and in-place updates. A stale ETag is 412 on real APIM (verify); ignoring it is the deliberate lenient choice (ADR-0003).
  • Tests that assert rejection of an update PUT without If-Match encode a wrong behaviour. Do not port them.
  • checkNameAvailability for an invalid name is nameAvailable:false, reason:"Invalid". An inverted validity check returning true is wrong.
  • Product state is honoured. published stays published; the default is notPublished. Forcing it breaks azurerm_api_management_product with published = true.
  • Properties live under properties. PATCH merges onto the stored document. Reading fields from the JSON root, or persisting the raw request instead of the merged document, loses data.
  • No async signals. A write response carrying Location with an asyncId query parameter makes azurerm start a custom poller. DELETE returns 200 or 204 only: 201 or 202 routes azurerm to a custom poller that needs an absolute URL. A bare 202 fails with "unexpected status 202 received with no body" (ADR-0006).
  • A malformed Location such as ?asyncCode=…=asyncId=… is worse than none. Emit nothing.
  • Real service GETs are fully populated. gatewayUrl, gatewayRegionalUrl, portalUrl, developerPortalUrl, managementApiUrl, scmUrl, publicIPAddresses, platformVersion and identity are all returned, and azapi response_export_values and azurerm outputs read them. Hard-coding only provisioningState is not enough.
  • createdAtUtc cannot be stable without the stored document. Do not emit it unless it is copied from Current (Slice 2 emits none).
  • Soft-delete. Real DELETE of a service soft-deletes it for a retention window (about 48 h, verify) and keeps the name reserved; deletedservices GET then returns 200. Name uniqueness is DNS-global ({name}.azure-api.net), across subscriptions. miniblue is subscription-local and allows immediate recreate.
  • apis/{id};rev=N is a distinct address per revision. Real APIM also aliases apis/{id} to the current revision. azurerm always uses ;rev=1; CLI and bicep may use the bare name (out of scope in Slice 2).
  • sku.name enum in 2024-05-01 is Developer, Standard, Premium, Basic, Consumption, Isolated, BasicV2, StandardV2. PremiumV2 is not in it. sku.capacity is required (Consumption 0, Developer 1; others verify).
  • Do not seed APIs or products. azurerm lists and deletes them right after create. Real APIM does seed system groups (administrators, developers, guests), a master subscription and admin user 1; add those only when the group and subscription types land.
  • Real lists are {value, count, nextLink}. Clients treat an empty or missing nextLink as done, so returning all items is safe.
  • Secrets are masked on real GET for secret named values, subscription keys and similar fields, and served through listValue or listSecrets (verify per field). Echoing them in clear text is a documented deviation, not Azure behaviour.

docs.title: App Configuration
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks plus engine gaps for the ARM types; data plane bespoke. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/appconfig (chi, no engine). Suggested wave: wave 4 (appconfig ARM, ADR-0007); SPIKE rank 9 (SPIKE).

Real latest stable api-version is 2024-06-01 for the management plane (spec listing, confirmed). Per ADR-0006 the engine is sync only: the real PUT, PATCH, DELETE and purge are long-running operations, but the engine answers 200/201/204 with provisioningState Succeeded and never sends Azure-AsyncOperation. SDK pollers accept that. Scenarios below assert the sync shape.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • No soft-delete: DELETE hard-removes the store and there is no deletedConfigurationStores or purge (internal/services/appconfig/handler.go:231).
  • DELETE returns 202 (handler.go:240). The engine answers 200 or 204, never 202.
  • No PATCH, no regenerateKey, no list-by-subscription.
  • listKeys returns two static keys, miniblue-primary-key and miniblue-secondary-key (handler.go:263-296), not the real four.
  • GET .../replicas always returns an empty list (handler.go:250); no replica PUT, GET or DELETE; no snapshots; no ARM keyValues.
  • PUT defaults a missing location to eastus (handler.go:146-148) and a missing sku to free (handler.go:152). Real Azure requires both.
  • creationDate is hard-coded to 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z (handler.go:164); it must be set once on create and stay stable.
  • No SKU-dependent defaults (softDeleteRetentionInDays, enablePurgeProtection, revision retention).
  • Data plane: the ETag is "etag-" + key (handler.go:102), so it does not change when the value changes. getKeyValue reads the stored value with a struct type-assert (handler.go:119), the persistence-roundtrip bug class from the spike findings.
  • Data plane: DELETE always returns 204 (handler.go:130); no /keys, /labels, /revisions, lock, snapshots or null-label (%00) handling.
  • Existing tests: tests/appconfig_test.go, tests/appconfigarm_test.go. No azurerm or azapi fixture for azurerm_app_configuration.
  • website/docs/services/parity.md:59 says "No labels, no feature flags". Labels work through the label query parameter, so the line is stale.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Real PATCH, DELETE and purge are long-running operations. The engine is sync; assert 200 or 204, not 202.
  • Real location and sku are required on PUT. Defaulting them hides client bugs and masks a real 400.
  • listKeys returns four keys (two read-write, two read-only). Two static keys breaks clients that pick a read-only connection string.
  • Soft-delete retention and purge protection apply to non-Free SKUs only; Free stores have neither. Purging a protected store is 409, and purge protection cannot be turned off.
  • The data-plane DELETE answers 200 or 204, and an ETag that does not change on write breaks conditional requests.
  • A replica endpoint is derived from the store and replica names; replicas are not available on Free or Developer.
  • Naive store error codes (StoreNotFound, ReplicaNotFound) would diverge; real Azure uses ResourceNotFound and ParentResourceNotFound.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • No list-by-subscription for serverfarms or sites; lists are RG only (internal/services/sites/handler.go:55, :191-192).
  • Site PUT returns 200 on both branches (handler.go:156-158) and serverfarms PUT returns 200 on both (serverfarms.go:127-129). That matches the spec; keep it if these types ever move.
  • Site defaults: kind defaults to functionapp (handler.go:109) and location to eastus. Real clients send kind; a missing kind should not imply a function app. The response drops hostNameSslStates, availabilityState and siteConfig.
  • Sites are stored under func:{sub}:{rg}:{name} keys (handler.go:92), plus func:{sub}:{name} used for name checks (handler.go:96). The prefix is a leftover of the functions code, not a real concept.
  • internal/services/functions/handler.go:35 defines the same Microsoft.Web/sites routes as sites/handler.go:55, but nothing imports that package, so sites is the only live handler. Remove or merge the dead copy before any migration.
  • serverfarms:
    • The route is registered as serverFarms and responses return type Microsoft.Web/serverFarms (serverfarms.go:36, :93). The real, canonical type is Microsoft.Web/serverfarms.
    • The SKU tier is derived from a non-spec properties.skuName (serverfarms.go:69-72). The real SKU is the top-level sku object (name, tier, size, family, capacity).
    • No restartSites, no PATCH.
  • config/web supports GET and PUT only; no PATCH (spec has PATCH). Sites config routes otherwise cover appsettings, azurestorageaccounts, authsettings, authsettingsV2, backup, logs, metadata, connectionstrings, pushsettings, slotConfigNames, publishingcredentials and the FTP and SCM policies.
  • checknameavailability handles type Microsoft.Web/sites only (handler.go:219) and scans one subscription.
  • No publishxml, no webAppStacks, no Kudu endpoints.
  • Tests: tests/functions_test.go only; there is no dedicated App Service test and no azurerm or azapi fixture for azurerm_service_plan or the web app resources.
  • website/docs/services/parity.md:79 lists Azure App Service as not implemented, which is stale.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Spec create status is 200 or 202 for serverfarms, sites and slots. An engine that returns 201 on create can be rejected by SDK clients that check expected status codes (the go-azure-sdk webapps CreateOrUpdate accepts only 200 and 202), so a migrated type needs a per-type create-status override or must stay bespoke. The engine's 201-on-create default is therefore wrong for this provider ((verify) against the ADR-0003 hook set).
  • A plan PUT is a full replace. Merging omitted properties masks client bugs.
  • The SKU is the top-level sku object, not a properties field. reserved distinguishes Linux plans.
  • restartSites is 204 with no body, not 200.
  • publishingcredentials/list and appsettings/list are POSTs; real Azure has no GET on config/appsettings.
  • Site names are global ({name}.azurewebsites.net); a per-subscription scan cannot report names taken in other subscriptions.
  • Do not key sites under another service's prefix. Kind decides the experience (app, app,linux, functionapp); echo what the client sent.
  • Real DELETE of a missing site or slot can be 404 per the spec, whereas the engine rule for DELETE is 200 or 204.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks for roleAssignments; hooks plus engine gaps for roleDefinitions; bespoke for RBAC enforcement (per type below). miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/authorization (bespoke Dispatch behind a middleware). Suggested wave: roleAssignments in Phase 2 slice 2.1 (PLAN), design in slice 1; roleDefinitions at gate G3 (ADR-0008); enforcement at slice 2.3 (opt-in).

Real latest stable api-version is 2022-04-01 for both types (spec confirmed; some role-definition paths also appear in a 2022-05-01 preview). The validation, defaults, list override and removal design for roleAssignments lives in slice 1; this page only lists the scenarios that slice must satisfy and does not repeat its rules.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value. Bugs carry file:line in internal/services/authorization/handler.go.

  • Role assignment PUT regenerates createdOn and updatedOn on every call (:206-207), and there is no validation beyond "properties present". GUID name, principalId, roleDefinitionId resolution, immutable fields and duplicates are all unchecked; the fix is slice 1.
  • No duplicate detection: a second assignment for the same principal, role and scope is accepted.
  • The storage key is authorization:roleAssignment:<scope as sent>:<name> (:169), so it is case-sensitive.
  • DELETE of a missing assignment returns 404; real ARM returns 204. DELETE of an existing one returns 200 with the body, which matches the spec (200 or 204).
  • Contributor is seeded with actions ["*"] and empty notActions (:31, :369), so it equals Owner. ADR-0008 specifies the correct notActions and adds User Access Administrator.
  • Tenant-level GET /providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/{id} is rejected: parseAuthorizationPath returns not-ok when the marker is at index 0 (:102-104). Only 9 built-ins are seeded (:29-38).
  • Role definition list handles only $filter=roleName eq '...' (:316-319); no atScopeAndBelow, no type eq filter and no paging.
  • Role definition PUT on a built-in id returns 400 and custom DELETE returns 204 or 404 (:343). Real DELETE of an existing definition returns 200 with the body (spec: 200 or 204).
  • Management-group and nested-resource scopes are served by the generic path parse in the middleware (:45-53), but nothing in the tests exercises them (verify).
  • No enforcement of any kind; the opt-in design is in ADR-0008.
  • Tests: internal/services/authorization/handler_test.go, internal/server/authorization_test.go. Terraform: tests/terraform/azurerm/identity-rbac covers azurerm_role_assignment; no azapi fixture.

Same name and same content is idempotent (200). docs.title: Enforcement (deferred)
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G1-T58 RBAC scope inheritance on ARM calls With MINIBLUE_RBAC=enforce: Reader at subscription => GET of a resource below it 200, PUT 403 AuthorizationFailed; an assignment at RG A grants nothing in sibling RG B (403); an assignment above applies to scopes below T2 Deferred to slice 2.3 (ADR-0008). Covers engine types only; data-plane enforcement and management-group propagation are out of scope until MG parents are modelled (verify).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Real Azure returns 409 RoleAssignmentExists on a duplicate; asserting 400 RoleAssignmentAlreadyExists would be wrong.
  • Assignment names must be GUIDs. Real Azure rejects other names with 400 on the ARM call itself, not only in a client tool.
  • The 2022-04-01 role-definition property is type (BuiltInRole or CustomRole); there is no roleType.
  • The role-definition PUT spec documents 201 only. A strict SDK client can reject a 200 on update.
  • Paging uses nextLink; do not invent a hasMore field.
  • A role definition is addressed by its GUID name; roleName is a property and is matched by $filter, not by the URL.
  • DELETE of a missing role assignment is 204, not 404.
  • Contributor must not be able to write or delete role assignments (notActions includes Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write and */Delete); seeding it as * hides the difference between Contributor and Owner.
  • Role assignments are extension resources: they can sit under any resource id, so the engine must accept arbitrary parent scopes without an existence check.

docs.title: Client suites
docs.text:
Engine fit: not applicable (test infrastructure). miniblue today: Terraform suites only (one azapi fixture, six azurerm fixtures). No Azure SDK suite, no scripted az suite, no PowerShell suite. Suggested wave: SDK and az smoke after PLAN 1.5 (armtest) so the two layers do not overlap.

Each client class exercises something an in-process httptest cannot: real credential and discovery flows, real LRO pollers, real id parsing and casing logic in the client, and the TLS trust path. This page defines the multi-client smoke pattern, the trust setup per client, how CI should wire it, and the order to build it in. The scenarios themselves are the client smoke rows on cross-cutting scenarios.

docs.title: Suite pattern
docs.text:
One small scenario per client, the same shape everywhere: create an RG, tag it, read it back, list, check existence, create one engine-served resource (a policy definition today), run one deployment, delete, assert 404. Keep each suite under the cost rule below. Breadth belongs in tests/ httptest and armtest, not here.

Suite Client and runtime Scenario Isolation Verdict for miniblue Terraform (azurerm, azapi) Terraform 1.16.6; azurerm = 5.10.0, azapi 2.13.0 apply, plan shows no drift, second apply no-op, destroy (azurerm); apply, mangled-case GETs, destroy, 404 (azapi) RG names inside the fixture; one fresh miniblue per fixture Exists. Add the negative fixture, a plugin cache and a nightly latest-provider job Go SDK armresources (and armpolicy or armauthorization) in a separate module tests/sdk/go RG create, get, list, update tags, exists, delete; policy definition CRUD through the LRO poller; ids canonical-cased; 404 after delete Unique RG name per test Adopt first. Only client class that exercises Go poller and id-casing logic directly Python SDK pytest with azure-mgmt-resource and azure-mgmt-authorization RG, tags, deployment, policy definition via begin_*().result() Unique RG name per test Adopt second; cheap once the Go suite exists az CLI mcr.microsoft.com/azure-cli:<version> container, scripted cloud register, login, az group create/show/exists/list/delete, az policy definition create/show/delete, az deployment group create Unique RG name per run Adopt third; feasibility spike first PowerShell pwsh 7.4 with the Az modules same shape as az Saved context restored per process Later or optional; only if PowerShell users are a target Node @azure/arm-* none planned Skip. No ARM suite is needed; data-plane clients are out of scope here

Isolation today is one hard-coded subscription (the all-zeros GUID). Until a multi-subscription model exists, every test uses a unique RG name and cleans it up.

docs.title: Harness pattern
docs.text: Step Pattern miniblue today Action Start the emulator a fresh process or image per suite, private ports, in-memory state tests/terraform/azurerm/run.sh starts the binary in stub mode (MINIBLUE_DISABLE_DOCKER=1), on private ports, with PERSISTENCE and DATABASE_URL ignored, and refuses to run if the port is already taken Reuse for SDK and az jobs. Test the shipped image in at least one job (e2e.yml already builds it) TLS a throwaway certificate generated per run LOCAL_AZURE_CERT_DIR points the child at a temp dir; the CA bundle is built from system roots plus the run's cert Keep generating per run. Never commit keys or certificates Trust append the cert to every CA store the client reads SSL_CERT_FILE only (Go, Terraform) Add the per-client rows in the next section Endpoint discovery clients get their endpoints from configuration, not from DNS tricks azurerm: ARM_METADATA_HOSTNAME=localhost:<tls port>; azapi: provider endpoint variables Add a cloud.json template for az and reuse it for the scripted scenario Auth a fake credential for SDKs, a service principal login for az and Terraform miniblue's token endpoint returns a mock JWT for any client (internal/services/auth/handler.go:71-95); ARM_CLIENT_ID/ARM_CLIENT_SECRET are placeholders A fake TokenCredential is enough for SDKs. Any bearer is accepted Polling skip artificial poll delays GO_AZURE_SDK_SKIP_POLLING_DELAY=true in run.sh; the header equivalent lands with PLAN 0.8 Keep both until the header is on every response Speed initialise providers once, reuse -lockfile=readonly, init per fixture, no cache Add TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR plus an actions/cache step

docs.title: Trust per client
docs.text:
SSL trust is where suites break first. Each client reads a different store, and several variables replace the system roots instead of adding to them.

Client Store it reads What to set Notes Go SDK Go system roots, or a transport you pass SSL_CERT_FILE (Linux, macOS), or give the client a Transport with an explicit root pool Go on Windows ignores SSL_CERT_FILE (documented in the acceptance guide). A custom transport works everywhere and needs no environment Terraform providers (Go) same as Go SSL_CERT_FILE pointing at system roots plus the miniblue cert The variable replaces the system roots, so build a combined bundle. run.sh does this for the provider registry Python SDK requests or certifi REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or SSL_CERT_FILE on a combined bundle; azure-core also accepts a per-client verify path (verify) A bundle must include public roots if the same process talks to anything else az CLI the certifi bundle inside the az Python append the cert to the certifi bundle, set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, set AZURE_CORE_INSTANCE_DISCOVERY=false The OS trust store is not read. Instance discovery would otherwise try to reach the real Microsoft endpoints PowerShell (.NET) OS store; on Linux, OpenSSL paths on Linux, SSL_CERT_FILE or SSL_CERT_DIR (verify); on Windows, import into the user store Do not rely on Connect-AzAccount skipping validation Node bundled roots NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS Adds to the bundled roots. Only relevant if a Node suite is ever built curl (probes, helper scripts) system bundle --cacert <file> run.sh pins the probe to the run's own certificate so it cannot reach another instance

Both the Go SDK and the Python SDK refuse to send a bearer token over plain HTTP, so every SDK suite targets the TLS port (default 4567), not the HTTP port.

docs.text: Client Wiring miniblue endpoint it depends on Go SDK arm.ClientOptions with a custom Cloud configuration (authority host plus the ARM endpoint and audience) and a fake TokenCredential https://localhost:<tls> for ARM; no token call is made with a fake credential Python SDK base_url and credential_scopes on the management client, plus a credential class that returns a fixed token ARM only az az cloud register --cloud-config @cloud.json (ARM, AAD, Graph and the service suffixes), az cloud set, then a login GET /metadata/endpoints, GET /metadata/instance, POST /{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token, /oauth2/token, the openid configuration and /common/discovery/instance routes. All are registered today (internal/services/auth/handler.go:24-41; the metadata handler serves the other two) PowerShell Add-AzEnvironment (ARM URL, AAD authority, suffixes) then Connect-AzAccount; Save-AzContext once so each later process restores it same as az Terraform provider environment from run.sh (ARM_METADATA_HOSTNAME, ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, ARM_TENANT_ID, ARM_CLIENT_ID, ARM_CLIENT_SECRET, ARM_RESOURCE_PROVIDER_REGISTRATIONS=none) metadata, token, ARM

docs.text:
Two guides contradict these suites and need an update in the PR that proves otherwise. Do not change them speculatively.

Page Current claim Consequence website/docs/guides/azure-cli.md (line 97) native az uses MSAL and cannot be reliably emulated; use azlocal The az suite is a feasibility spike first. If it passes, rewrite the section; if not, record the failure and drop the item website/docs/guides/sdk.md (lines 3 and 199-206) official SDKs enforce HTTPS and real credentials, so use plain HTTP The SDK suites show how to use them over the TLS port with a fake credential. Add a section then website/docs/guides/acceptance-tests.md documents SSL_CERT_FILE only Add the per-client trust table above once a second client lands

docs.title: CI wiring
docs.text:
Current workflows, checked in the worktree:

Workflow Jobs and triggers Notes ci.yml vet, lint, test, build, docker; push to main and PRs to main The test job runs go test -v ./tests/... (ci.yml:47). internal/... is not run and there is no race detector (PLAN 0.1) acceptance.yml one job, the azapi policy definition fixture; 15 minute cap; cancels superseded runs The only azapi job. Uploads the log on failure acceptance-azurerm.yml matrix azurerm / <fixture> over network, storage, identity-rbac, keyvault, compute, examples/terraform; fail-fast: false; 15 minutes each Builds the binary from source, then ACC_SETUP_SYSTEM=1 ./tests/terraform/azurerm/run.sh <fixture> e2e.yml builds the Docker image; curl and Python smoke plus the azlocal CLI; push, PR and manual The only job that tests the shipped image aks-e2e.yml real-backend AKS run; path-filtered on AKS code, push to main and manual The precedent for expensive, gated suites Aspect Pattern miniblue today Adopt Build once, test many one job builds the image or binary and exports it; every suite loads it each workflow builds its own Optional. Do it when three or more suites need the binary Path filter a changed-files filter decides which suites run; a core change runs all ci.yml, acceptance*.yml run on every PR; only aks-e2e.yml and docs.yml filter paths Add when the matrix passes about ten jobs. Core paths (internal/arm, internal/server, internal/store) always run everything Client matrix several az versions and provider versions, non-blocking single pinned versions, no matrix Add an az version matrix (fail-fast: false, non-blocking) with the az suite. Add a latest-provider job to the nightly Nightly a scheduled full run on unpinned versions no schedule trigger in any workflow Add one nightly workflow for drift and the slow suites Manual runs workflow_dispatch on expensive suites e2e.yml and aks-e2e.yml have it; the acceptance workflows do not Add to every new suite that misses the PR budget Provider cache cache the plugin directory none TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR and actions/cache; serialise init if a cache is shared between parallel fixtures Reporting publish test results and coverage raw logs; acceptance.yml uploads the log on failure Low priority: gotestsum --junitfile plus a coverage upload Unit tests the same pipeline runs unit and integration tests internal/... not run PLAN 0.1

docs.title: Cost rule
docs.text:
Anything expected to take more than about 2 minutes is nightly or opt-in (schedule or workflow_dispatch), not per PR. The figures below are budget classes, not measurements; measure each suite when it lands and move it if it exceeds its class.

Class Budget Runs Suites PR, blocking under about 2 minutes each every PR go test ./... with -race, Go SDK smoke, Python SDK smoke, existing azurerm and azapi fixtures (each fixture is its own job) PR, non-blocking under about 2 minutes each every PR, fail-fast: false az version matrix once stable Nightly over 2 minutes scheduled, plus manual latest-provider drift (azurerm and azapi unpinned), PowerShell, any combined cross-service fixture, az against older versions Opt-in any workflow_dispatch or path filter real-backend suites (AKS style), anything needing a real cloud

Never run any suite against real Azure. No suite needs a subscription, a login or a credit.

docs.title: Adoption backlog
docs.text:
Ordered. Effort: XS under half a day, S about a day, M two to four days, L engine work.

# Item Effort Depends on Why A1 go test ./... with -race in ci.yml XS none (PLAN 0.1) engine, store, id and deployments tests are unguarded in CI A2 Go SDK smoke in tests/sdk/go: own module, no replace, custom transport or SSL_CERT_FILE, fake credential M A1 exercises the LRO poller and id casing in Go; Terraform's Go provider shares the same SDK base A3 Python SDK smoke: azure-mgmt-resource, azure-mgmt-authorization, base_url, fake credential M A2 cheap once A2 exists; begin_*().result() covers polling A4 az scripted scenario plus cloud.json and a three-version matrix; feasibility spike first, then update azure-cli.md M A1 the most common local-dev client; catches discovery and metadata drift A5 Negative Terraform fixture: invalid name fails apply and the message is asserted S a name-validation hook on at least one type locks the CheckName hooks end to end A6 TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR cache and a nightly latest-provider job S none speed and early drift detection A7 Path filter on the acceptance workflows S matrix over about ten jobs cost A8 Subscription-per-suite isolation L multi-subscription model (no PLAN row) removes unique-name discipline Later PowerShell suite; test-result reporting; build-once artefact shared by suites; batching azapi fixtures into one job S to M each demand each azapi fixture is a full CI job today

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Go on Windows ignores SSL_CERT_FILE. Run the shell harness on Linux or WSL2, or pass an explicit transport in SDK tests.
  • SSL_CERT_FILE replaces the system roots. Concatenate the public roots and the miniblue cert, or provider downloads fail.
  • az ignores the OS trust store and needs the cert in its certifi bundle. Without AZURE_CORE_INSTANCE_DISCOVERY=false it tries the real discovery endpoints.
  • SDKs refuse bearer tokens over HTTP. Point them at the TLS port.
  • A shared provider plugin cache fails with "text file busy" if two terraform init runs share it. Serialise init, or copy an initialised workspace per test.
  • Terraform lock files must carry hashes for every developer platform (linux_amd64, darwin_arm64, windows_amd64), or -lockfile=readonly fails locally.
  • Pollers need terminal responses or a valid Location. A bare 202 stalls them; see the cross-cutting pitfalls.
  • Do not copy committed key material from other projects. A per-run certificate removes the risk and the rotation chore.
  • Real Azure is never a dependency, even as an oracle. Verify uncertain behaviour against the REST specs and provider source.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text:
Engine fit: bespoke (virtualMachines), hooks (availabilitySets), passthrough (SKU and size catalogue). miniblue today: hand-written services internal/services/vm (rich) and internal/services/compute (catalogue only). Suggested wave: virtualMachines stay bespoke (PLAN wave 5 / G5); availabilitySets as a new type after G2.

Paths below are relative to /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.Compute unless stated. Spec facts come from Microsoft.Compute/Compute ComputeRP.json (read at 2025-04-01; newer stable directories exist, the newest listed is 2026-04-01).

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • No availabilitySets routes or store prefix; no code under internal/ references availabilitySet. VM PUT neither validates properties.availabilitySet.id nor records membership, so azurerm_availability_set and VMs that join a set cannot work.
  • Microsoft.Compute/skus entries carry only vCPUs, MemoryGB and MaxDataDiskCount (compute/handler.go:58, :63); there is no PremiumIO capability. The catalogue has two sizes (compute/handler.go:35, :43).
  • DELETE of a missing VM returns 404 (vm/handler.go:340-342); real Azure returns 204. DELETE of an existing VM returns 204 (vm/handler.go:365), which clients accept.
  • VM PUT already checks the resource group and returns 404 ResourceGroupNotFound (vm/handler.go:174); PATCH merges with mergePatch (vm/arm.go:67).
  • The RG cascade list has vm:, vmsvc: and vmext: only; availability sets need a prefix or DeleteTree.

docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T112 PATCH changes hardwareProfile.vmSize and tags; list; delete PATCH virtualMachines/{v} with a new vmSize and tags => 200, GET returns both; list by RG and by subscription include the VM; DELETE => 200 or 204, GET after => 404 T2 Mostly covered by existing tests; check the vmSize PATCH. Real PATCH may be 200 or 202 (verify) G3-T113 A VM joins an availability set by id; the set tracks its members PUT virtualMachines/{v} with properties.availabilitySet.id of a missing set => 404 (code (verify)); with an existing set => 200 or 201 and GET availabilitySets/{n} lists the VM under properties.virtualMachines; DELETE the VM => it is gone from the list T2 Depends on the availability set lifecycle row. Cross-resource write, so the VM handler stays bespoke. virtualMachines is a list of sub-resource ids in the spec G3-T120 A multi-resource create in dependency order succeeds RG, then vnet and subnet, public IP, NSG, NIC, then VM, each => 2xx; GET VM => provisioningState Succeeded T2/T4 The az vm create command itself needs the az CLI; use its call order as the httptest sequence

docs.title: Availability sets
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T115 Availability set lifecycle PUT availabilitySets/{n} => 200 (create and update); body has platformFaultDomainCount, platformUpdateDomainCount, sku.name; GET; PATCH tags => 200; DELETE => 200; list by RG and by subscription; missing RG => 404 ResourceGroupNotFound T1/T2 Spec lists only 200 for PUT, while the engine answers 201 on create (ADR 0006); whether azurerm's azurerm_availability_set accepts 201 is (verify). sku.name is Aligned for managed disks (verify). Missing in miniblue G3-T116 Delete of a missing availability set DELETE availabilitySets/{n} missing => 204; existing => 200 T1/T2 Spec: DELETE 200/204 G3-T117 GET availabilitySets/{n}/vmSizes lists sizes available for new VMs in the set GET => 200 {"value":[...]} with name, numberOfCores, memoryInMB, maxDataDiskCount; an empty set returns every catalogue size; a set with member VMs returns only the sizes of the members' size family T2 Family filtering is an approximation of the real hardware-cluster rule (verify) G3-T118 Availability sets deploy from an ARM template; the set lists its members deployment with an availability set and VMs referencing it => set GET lists the VMs; azurerm_availability_set applies and destroys T2/T3 The template case depends on deployment dispatch (see the deployments page). Add the Terraform case to azurerm/compute

docs.title: Catalogue
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T119 The SKU list is non-empty and exposes a premium storage capability GET /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.Compute/skus => 200, non-empty; at least one size has capability PremiumIO set to True T2 Existing catalogue test covers non-empty; add the PremiumIO capability

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Missing resources are the generic ResourceNotFound; do not mint per-type codes (a VM-specific or availability-set-specific not-found code is not a real ARM code (verify)).
  • DELETE of a missing availability set or VM is 204, not 404.
  • Availability set PUT is 200 in the spec even on create; see the note on the lifecycle row.
  • properties.virtualMachines on a set is maintained by the platform from VM availabilitySet.id; clients never write it, so a PUT of the set must not overwrite the member list.
  • A VM cannot reference an availability set that does not exist; the id comparison is case-insensitive (verify).
  • vmSizes for a set is a subset of the size catalogue, not a copy of it.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
• No tests of any kind (see above).
  • buildResponse (internal/services/aci/handler.go:265-355) drops tags, restartPolicy, resources and dnsNameLabel from the stored input. azurerm refresh would show drift.
  • Routes cover only list-by-RG, PUT, GET and DELETE (handler.go:40-44). Missing: list by subscription, PATCH, start / stop / restart, container logs, RG-existence check on PUT.
  • ipAddress.ip is hard-coded to 127.0.0.1 (handler.go:318), and the default location is eastus (handler.go:270).
  • The internal _containerID is written into the API response (handler.go:350).
  • DELETE returns 404 for a missing group (handler.go:237-251); real allows 200/202/204 and treats a missing group as 204 (verify).
  • PUT returns 201 on create and 200 on replace (handler.go:208-210), which matches the spec and ADR-0006.
  • Docker side effects (dockerRun, handler.go:74) have no hook in Hooks{Validate, Defaults} (verify). Stub mode is the testable baseline.

Error code for a missing field (verify) G1-T70 PUT with a public IP, dnsNameLabel and port 80/TCP ipAddress.type=Public, dnsNameLabel echoed, ports echoed, ip non-empty, fqdn derived from the label T2 Spec requires ipAddress.ports and type; dnsNameLabel, fqdn, ip are optional. type enum values and fqdn format (verify). Covered end to end by the T3 row below G1-T71 PUT with tags, then GET Tags are returned unchanged T2 Dropped by miniblue today (handler.go:265-355) G1-T72 GET a missing group; PUT into a missing RG GET => 404 ResourceNotFound; PUT => 404 ResourceGroupNotFound T1 Generic engine checks G1-T73 List by RG and list by subscription Both 200 and contain the group T1 Sub-wide list is engine behaviour (ADR-0003). GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups G1-T74 PUT the same group again with a change PUT => 200 (replace); GET shows the change; PATCH with tags only => 200 T2 Real ACI rejects updates to some immutable properties (verify); assert only on a mutable field such as tags. PATCH is tags-only in the spec G1-T75 POST start, stop, restart; same on a missing group Each => 204 with no body (spec: start 202/204, stop 204, restart 204); missing group => 404 ResourceNotFound T2 Type.Actions; matches the ADR-0006 "204 without body" action form. Do not assert instance state transitions (verify) G1-T76 DELETE a group, then GET DELETE => 200, 202 or 204; GET => 404 ResourceNotFound; DELETE of a missing group => 204 (verify) T1 Sync engine returns 200 or 204 G1-T78 azurerm_container_group x3: no public IP + Always, public IP + dns_name_label + OnFailure, tagged apply then refresh => clean plan; ip_address_type, dns_name_label, restart_policy, os_type and tags echoed T3 New fixture under tests/terraform/azurerm/. azurerm refresh sensitivity to ipAddress when no IP is requested (verify)

docs.title: containers/logs
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G1-T77 GET containerGroups/{g}/containers/{c}/logs 200 with {"content": "<text>"}; tail limits to the last N lines; timestamps=true prefixes each line T2 Bespoke. Assert the JSON shape, not a placeholder string. Content in stub mode is implementation-defined

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• tags, restartPolicy, resources and dnsNameLabel must round-trip, otherwise azurerm shows a diff on every refresh.
  • Do not hard-code ipAddress.ip. A public group returns a real-looking address and an fqdn built from dnsNameLabel.
  • start, stop and restart return 204, not 200 with a body.
  • Logs are {"content": "..."}, not a bare string.
  • DELETE is idempotent: a missing group is not a 404.
  • In the 2026-07-01 spec location is optional on the group (it is a proxy resource there); older versions treat it as required (verify). Do not assert a 400 on a missing location.
  • Never leak internal fields (for example the Docker container id) into the response.
  • PUT is a full replace. PATCH changes tags only.
  • Create is an LRO in the spec (200/201); the sync engine relies on SDK pollers accepting a terminal 201 (verify).
  • Docker-backed runs are nondeterministic in CI. Write acceptance tests against the stub-mode shape.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
• checkNameAvailability never reports AlreadyExists: internal/services/acr/handler.go:224 type-asserts item.(Registry), but stored values are maps. Existing bug.
  • buildRegistryResponse (handler.go:63) drops tags and identity, echoes sku.tier = sku.name (handler.go:96), hard-codes adminUserEnabled=false (handler.go:101) and a constant creationDate of 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z (handler.go:102), and defaults location to eastus (handler.go:68).
  • PUT (handler.go:126) ignores a body decode error and does no name or location validation. Responses are 201 on create and 200 on replace (handler.go:140-142); DELETE returns 202 (handler.go:168) and 404 for a missing registry.
  • Missing: PATCH, listCredentials, generateCredentials, regenerateCredential, listUsages, tasks, runs, tokens, list by subscription, RG-existence check.
  • replications is a stub that returns an empty list (handler.go:48, ListReplications at handler.go:196).
  • Data-plane stubs live under /acr/{registry}/v2/... (handler.go:53-56: manifests and tags/list only). No blob upload, no _catalog, no token exchange.
  • Existing coverage: tests/acr_test.go (TestACRRegistry, TestACRRegistryARMPolicyAndRoleAssignmentMode). No azurerm or azapi ACR fixture.

docs.title: registries
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G1-T79 PUT a Standard registry PUT => 201 (spec 200/201); loginServer ends .azurecr.io and contains the name; adminUserEnabled=false; sku.name=Standard, sku.tier=Standard; provisioningState=Succeeded; publicNetworkAccess=Enabled; zoneRedundancy=Disabled; networkRuleBypassOptions=AzureServices; creationDate is a current RFC 3339 timestamp T2 Hooks.Defaults. sku is required, tier is read-only. A domain-name-label scope may add a hash suffix to loginServer; assert "contains name" (verify) G1-T80 PUT with a name shorter than 5, longer than 50, or non-alphanumeric 400 with an error code (verify) T2 Hooks.Validate. Name rule from the spec: 5-50 characters, ^[a-zA-Z0-9]*$. Real code is likely InvalidParameter (verify); do not assert a bespoke code G1-T81 PUT without location; PUT into a missing RG missing location => 400 LocationRequired (verify); missing RG => 404 ResourceGroupNotFound T1/T2 RG check is generic (T1). Location is required on TrackedResource; never default it G1-T82 PATCH adminUserEnabled true, then false PATCH => 200 and GET reflects the flag. With the flag on, listCredentials returns a username equal to the registry name and two passwords; with it off the passwords are not available T2 PatchMode merge. Passwords never appear on GET. Spec lists PATCH as 200/201 (LRO) G1-T83 PUT a Premium registry with a SystemAssigned identity sku.name and sku.tier are Premium; identity.type=SystemAssigned with principalId and tenantId present T2 DefaultIdentity seam. Today identity is dropped (handler.go:63) G1-T84 GET a missing registry 404 ResourceNotFound T1 Generic G1-T85 List by RG, list by subscription, DELETE Lists contain the registry; DELETE => 200, 202 or 204; GET after => 404 ResourceNotFound T1 Sync engine returns 200 or 204 G1-T86 POST listCredentials with admin enabled, with admin disabled, then after enabling Enabled: 200 with username and passwords (password, password2, each with a value). Disabled: error with a code (verify). Works again after PATCH enables it T2 Type.Actions. Azurerm reads these when admin_enabled is set (verify), which makes this the first consumer that lets the seam land G1-T87 POST generateCredentials (all passwords, or one by name); missing registry 200 (spec 200/202) with username and passwords[] (one entry when a name is given); missing registry => 404 ResourceNotFound T2 Real input is tokenId, expiry and name (password1 or password2), and the credentials belong to a registry token, not the admin user. Needs a registries/tokens type before it can be ported (verify) G1-T88 POST regenerateCredential with name = password or password2 200 with a body in the listCredentials shape (verify); only the named password changes; the other is stable; admin disabled => error with a code (verify) T2 Type.Actions. The old value must stop matching G1-T89 GET listUsages by sku 200 value[] with name, limit, currentValue, unit. Documented limits: Basic storage 10 GiB / webhooks 2; Standard 100 GiB / 10; Premium 500 GiB / 500 T2 Spec shape verified. Limit values, unit string and which usage names appear (verify) G1-T97 azurerm_container_registry (Standard, admin_enabled=true) and an azapi basic registry apply then refresh => clean plan; login_server contains the name; admin_enabled echoed T3 New fixtures tests/terraform/azurerm/container_registry and tests/terraform/azapi/container_registry_basic. Provider read calls beyond GET (verify)

docs.title: tasks and runs
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G1-T92 Tasks: PUT, GET, PATCH (status), DELETE, list; PUT without a task type CRUD as for any child; missing task type => 400 BadRequest (verify) T2 Spec for tasks was not checked (verify). May need Type.Actions for listDetails (verify) G1-T93 Runs: POST scheduleRun, GET and list runs, PATCH isArchiveEnabled, POST listLogSasUrl scheduleRun yields a run whose status reaches Succeeded in the sync model; GET and list return it; PATCH persists isArchiveEnabled; listLogSasUrl => logLink T2 Bespoke. Real runs move through Queued, Running, Succeeded; the sync form returns a terminal state (verify). The source also lists a plain run operation (verify)

docs.title: Data plane (bespoke)
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G1-T95 OCI distribution API: /v2/ auth challenge and token exchange; blob upload (initiate, patch, complete); manifest PUT, GET, HEAD, DELETE; _catalog; tags/list with n and last pagination; blob DELETE Challenge => 401 with WWW-Authenticate; manifest and blob DELETE => 202; unknown manifest => 404; tags/list pages by n and last T2 Bespoke, never migrates (ADR-0007). Real Azure serves this on {name}.azurecr.io; miniblue serves a path form /acr/{registry}/v2/.... Exact status codes per the OCI spec (verify)

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• location is required on the registry. Real ARM returns 400 LocationRequired (verify); do not default it to the RG location.
  • Names are 5-50 alphanumerics and globally unique. The real error code for an invalid name on PUT is unconfirmed (verify); RegistryNameInvalid is not a known real code.
  • A missing registry is 404 ResourceNotFound, not a service-specific code such as ContainerRegistryNotFound. A missing replication is likewise ResourceNotFound.
  • sku.tier is read-only and derived from sku.name (Classic, Basic, Standard, Premium).
  • Passwords come only from listCredentials, regenerateCredential and generateCredentials, never from GET. regenerateCredential changes only the named password.
  • generateCredentials takes a token id, so it is not the admin-user flow.
  • PUT is a full replace and must keep tags, identity and sku. creationDate is the real creation time.
  • PATCH and PUT are LROs in the spec (200/201). The sync engine relies on SDK pollers accepting a terminal response (verify).
  • checkNameAvailability is a POST at subscription scope, with {nameAvailable, reason, message} in the response. AlreadyExists must come from stored registries, not from a type assertion that never matches.
  • The error code for listCredentials with admin disabled is unconfirmed (verify). Bespoke upper-case codes are not ARM style.
  • Replications are a Premium feature (verify).

docs.title: Cosmos DB
docs.text: Engine fit: hooks for Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts and its SQL children (defaults, derived locations, parent checks), engine-gap for key actions (Type.Actions), the name-check HEAD and the create status, bespoke for the data plane and the SQL query engine. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/cosmosdb (ARM plus a miniblue-specific data plane). Suggested wave: PLAN wave 4 (ARM only; data planes never migrate).

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
• Container PUT (internal/services/cosmosdb/handler.go:452-479) ignores the body and hard-codes partitionKey.paths to ["/id"] (handler.go:469). An azurerm container with /pk drifts on every plan. Existing bug.
  • CreateOrUpdateSQLDatabase (handler.go:389-409) ignores the body and does no parent-account check. Database and container PUT return 200, DELETE returns 202 (handler.go:435, handler.go:507) or 404 for a missing resource.
  • regenerateKey (handler.go:376) validates nothing and returns the same static keys (accountKeysResponse, handler.go:338), so no key ever changes.
  • throughputSettings exists only for tables (handler.go:54-56, handler.go:584-603), not for sqlDatabases or containers.
  • Missing: HEAD databaseAccountNames, PATCH on accounts, list by subscription, RG-existence check, echo of disableLocalAuth.
  • Account PUT returns 200 always (handler.go:291), which matches the spec but conflicts with the ADR-0006 "201 on create" rule. Account DELETE returns 202 (handler.go:317).
  • documentEndpoint is fixed to https://{name}.documents.azure.com:443/ (handler.go:239).
  • Data plane is served at a miniblue path, /cosmosdb/{account}/dbs/{db}/colls/{coll}/docs (handler.go:64), not on the account endpoint host. ReplaceDocument (handler.go:118) upserts instead of returning 404 and can panic on a nil document; document DELETE returns 204 even when missing (handler.go:139); QueryDocuments (handler.go:142) returns every document with no SQL; there is no If-Match / 412, no PATCH, no /dbs or /colls CRUD, no pkranges.
  • Existing coverage: tests/cosmosdb_test.go (3 document tests), tests/cosmosdbarm_test.go (12 ARM tests), internal/services/cosmosdb/handler_test.go. No azurerm Cosmos fixture.

docs.title: databaseAccounts
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G1-T98 PUT an account: kind=GlobalDocumentDB, Session consistency, databaseAccountOfferType=Standard, one location PUT => 200 (spec: 200 only, LRO; no 201); kind, databaseAccountOfferType=Standard, consistencyPolicy, documentEndpoint=https://{name}.documents.azure.com:443/, provisioningState=Succeeded T2 Spec requires properties.locations and databaseAccountOfferType; error code on omission (verify). Name is 3-50 characters, ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*. Needs a per-type create-status override. The endpoint host should follow miniblue's configured host (verify) G1-T99 Derived fields on a created account writeLocations and readLocations computed from locations (failoverPriority 0 is the write region), each with id, locationName, documentEndpoint, provisioningState; failoverPolicies derived; backupPolicy Periodic with 240 minutes interval and 8 hours retention; publicNetworkAccess=Enabled T2 Hooks.Defaults. backupStorageRedundancy default (verify). Property list from the spec: readLocations, writeLocations, failoverPolicies, backupPolicy, publicNetworkAccess G1-T100 disableLocalAuth default and explicit true Default reads back false; true is stored and echoed on GET T2 Property exists in the spec. Not echoed by miniblue today. Behaviour of the data plane when true is dropped (see Dropped) G1-T101 PATCH tags, GET, DELETE, GET again PATCH => 200 with new tags and other properties intact; GET => 200; DELETE => 200 or 204 in the sync engine (spec 202/204); GET after => 404 ResourceNotFound (verify) T2 PatchMode merge. The account-specific code DatabaseAccountNotFound is not an ARM code; exact real code for a missing account (verify) G1-T102 List by RG and by subscription Both 200 and contain the account T1 Sub-wide list is engine behaviour (ADR-0003) G1-T103 POST listKeys, POST/GET readonlykeys, POST listConnectionStrings, POST regenerateKey with keyKind; an invalid keyKind listKeys => primaryMasterKey, secondaryMasterKey; readonlykeys => primaryReadonlyMasterKey, secondaryReadonlyMasterKey; listConnectionStrings => connectionStrings[]; regenerateKey (spec 200/202; 200 in the sync engine) changes only the chosen key; invalid keyKind => 400 InvalidKeyKind (verify) T2 Type.Actions lands with the first consumer of this scenario. keyKind values: primary, secondary, primaryReadonly, secondaryReadonly (spec enum). Key format is base64 (verify). Stable between calls until regenerated G1-T104 HEAD /providers/Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccountNames/{name} for a free and a used name Free => 404; used => 200; no body either way T2 Spec: HEAD returns 200 or 404 only. The reason string AlreadyExists does not apply to a HEAD

docs.title: sqlDatabases

Needs the account, key, database and container rows first. Provider read calls (keys, connection strings, throughput) (verify)

docs.title: Data plane (bespoke)
docs.text:
The data plane keeps its own routes and never migrates to the engine (ADR-0007). Real clients talk to the account endpoint host and authenticate with a signed master key or a bearer token; miniblue exposes a path form and no auth. Every row is tier T2 only and tagged bespoke.

ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G1-T111 GET / on the account endpoint 200 with account properties: writable and readable locations and consistency policy T2 bespoke; shape (verify) G1-T112 /dbs: create, read, list, delete Create => 201; read => 200; list contains it; delete => 204 then 404 T2 bespoke. Success codes per the Cosmos REST API docs (verify) G1-T113 /colls: create, read, replace, delete, list; cross-plane visibility 201; 200; replace => 200; delete => 204; a database or container made through ARM is visible on the data plane, and the reverse T2 bespoke. Needs the ARM and data-plane stores to share state G1-T114 Documents: create; duplicate id; missing id or missing partition key; read; replace; delete; stale If-Match Create => 201; duplicate => 409; missing id or partition key => 400; read => 200; replace => 200 (404 if the document is absent, never an upsert); delete => 204 then 404; stale If-Match => 412 PreconditionFailed T2 bespoke. Replace and delete on a missing document are 404 (verify) G1-T115 List documents; PATCH operations List contains the created items; a PATCH with an operation changes only the targeted field T2 bespoke. Operation set (set, replace, add, remove, incr) (verify) G1-T116 SQL query: SELECT *, WHERE with equality, >, IN, IS_DEFINED, parameterised queries Only matching documents returned T2 bespoke; needs a SQL parser. Query is a POST with the query content type and x-ms-documentdb-isquery (verify) G1-T117 SQL query: field projection, SELECT VALUE, ORDER BY ascending and descending, COUNT Results have the requested shape and order T2 bespoke G1-T118 SQL query pagination with a continuation token Walking every page yields each document exactly once T2 bespoke; x-ms-continuation and x-ms-max-item-count (verify) G1-T119 SQL query: GROUP BY with COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX; ORDER BY on an aggregate or group field; empty collection One row per group; an empty collection yields an empty result T2 bespoke G1-T120 TTL expiry on documents An expired document is no longer readable T2 bespoke; test the purge function as a unit. Real expiry is lazy and approximate, so assert eventual absence G1-T121 GET .../colls/{c}/pkranges 200 with at least one partition key range T2 bespoke; SDKs call it before cross-partition queries. Response shape (verify)

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Account PUT is 200 only in the spec, even on create, and the account DELETE is 202 or 204. The ADR-0006 201-on-create rule would be wrong for this type.
  • Missing resources are 404 ResourceNotFound or ParentResourceNotFound. Service-specific codes (DatabaseAccountNotFound, SqlDatabaseNotFound) are not ARM codes.
  • Database and container PUT bodies carry properties.resource. Echo it. A constant partition key makes azurerm detect drift and force a replace.
  • throughputSettings PUT takes throughput or autoscaleSettings, never both. GET on a resource without dedicated throughput can be 404 (verify).
  • listKeys is a POST. readonlykeys accepts GET and POST. Static keys make regenerateKey untestable; the chosen key must change and the others must not.
  • regenerateKey is a spec LRO (200/202). The sync engine returns 200.
  • HEAD on databaseAccountNames returns no body: 404 means the name is free.
  • Account kind can only be set at creation. PATCH merges and does not change location.
  • Document replace is not an upsert, and DELETE on a missing document is 404.
  • Data-plane auth (master-key HMAC, RBAC) is separate from ARM auth and is not modelled here.

docs.title: Dropped
docs.text: ID Reason G1-T109 ARM template deployment of an account populating locations needs Deployments. Not portable. G1-T122 disableLocalAuth=true giving 401 on data-plane key auth, and RBAC-based data-plane auth. Not portable until miniblue models identities (Authorizer seam).

docs.title: Cross-cutting scenarios
docs.text:
Engine fit: the first block is the generic engine contract (armtest rows, per type). Resource groups, providers, subscriptions and deployments are bespoke handlers today and stay out of the engine until PLAN 3.x. miniblue today: the engine serves one type (policyDefinitions); everything else is hand-written under internal/services/*. Suggested wave: engine contract with PLAN 1.5, the rest as the PLAN row named in each Notes cell.

This page holds the scenarios that are not owned by one service: behaviour every ARM type shares, plus resource groups, subscriptions, providers, deployments and client smoke. Per-service scenarios live on the service pages in this catalogue. Ids keep the numbering of the spike so ADR and PLAN references resolve.

Codes and statuses not marked (verify) come from the ARM contract as understood during the spike and from ADR-0003, ADR-0005 and ADR-0006. None was re-checked against the live service. Treat every code as provisional until a conformance test pins it.

docs.title: How to read the tables
docs.text:
Column Meaning Behaviour Real Azure behaviour, not what miniblue does today Expect verb path => status, key body facts, error code Tier T1 conformance (armtest row, generic), T2 per-resource httptest in tests/, T3 Terraform acceptance, T4 client smoke (SDK, az) Notes armtest check name (ADR-0005), PLAN row, miniblue status. file:line is cited only where checked in the worktree

Related: ADR-0003 pipeline, ADR-0005 conformance suite, ADR-0006 sync and errors, PLAN.

docs.title: armtest additions beyond ADR-0005
docs.text:
ADR-0005 defines Sample, Run and Coverage and the check list. Nothing here replaces it. The scenarios below need these extra checks, which derive from the same Type metadata and need no Options struct. Propose them as an ADR-0005 amendment or as extra checks in PLAN 1.5.

Proposed check Asserts Derives from WrongMethod POST or PUT on a collection, and an unsupported verb on an item, give 405 MethodNotAllowed with the envelope Type.Patch (PatchNone also gives 405 on PATCH) MalformedAPIVersion api-version=latest gives 400 InvalidApiVersionParameter; a well-formed unknown date is accepted none (ADR-0005 states the rule but lists only the missing case) ScopeSurvivesRGDelete A type whose only scope is subscription survives deletion of an RG Type.Scopes ResponseHeaders x-ms-request-id and x-ms-correlation-request-id on success and on error (ErrorEnvelope asserts the request id on 4xx only) none UnknownRoute An unregistered type or an unrouted path gives a JSON 404 envelope with an ARM code ADR-0002 (code is open, see the unknown route row)

Two ADR-0005 checks need a precise reading. UrlCasing says response casing is preserved: read it as canonical keywords plus the name casing of the creating PUT (ADR-0003). List asserts {"value":[...]} only, because paging is not planned.

docs.title: Engine contract (armtest)
docs.text:
Rules from ADR-0003 and ADR-0006 that apply to every row: api-version is always required, parent and RG existence is always checked, responses are canonical-cased, writes are synchronous.

ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes X1 PUT a new resource at each scope the type allows PUT {id} => 201; id, name, type are server-owned; submitted properties echoed T1 armtest PutCreate X2 PUT an existing resource with a different body PUT {id} => 200; full replace, properties missing from the body are gone T1 armtest PutReplace. Server-owned fields (keys, creation time) must survive via Request.Current; the check cannot see them, so types that own such fields add a T2 X3 GET an existing and a missing resource GET {id} => 200, same document as the PUT; missing => 404 ResourceNotFound with the envelope T1 armtest Get, GetMissing X4 GET with a mangled-case path GET {MANGLED id} => 200; id keeps the canonical segment keywords and the name casing of the creating PUT T1 armtest UrlCasing. Engine types are canonical-only (ADR-0003). Legacy handlers still mirror the client casing (tests/casesensitivity_test.go) until migrated. The azapi policy definition acceptance already covers it end to end X5 List a collection: empty, N items, siblings only GET {collection} => 200 {"value":[...]} in a stable order; no leak across parents or across name prefixes; nextLink absent T1 armtest List, ListSubscription, PrefixSibling. Paging is deferred (no PLAN row; see engine lessons). Real RPs add nextLink only when paging; (verify) per RP X6 DELETE an existing, then a missing resource DELETE {id} => 200 when it existed, then 204 with an empty body; GET => 404 T1 armtest Delete, DeleteMissing. Real RPs vary between 200, 202 and 204; sync-only (ADR-0006) fixes 200 and 204 X7 Unsupported or malformed api-version api-version=latest => 400 InvalidApiVersionParameter T1 Real ARM also rejects a well-formed version the type does not support (verify); miniblue deliberately accepts any well-formed version and treats APIVersions as metadata (ADR-0005). Needs the MalformedAPIVersion check above X8 Missing api-version any /subscriptions/... call without api-version => 400 MissingApiVersionParameter T1 armtest MissingAPIVersion. Always strict (PLAN 1.4). Legacy routes only echo x-ms-api-version today (internal/server/middleware.go:46), so they still accept a missing version X9 Body name or id differs from the URL PUT => 400 InvalidRequestContent (verify) T1 armtest NameIDMismatch X10 Malformed JSON, non-object body, empty body PUT => 400 JSON envelope InvalidRequestContent; never 500, never text/plain T1 armtest BadBody X11 PATCH per PatchMode PatchMerge: 200, RFC 7386 merge (null deletes); PatchTags: 200, tags replaced, {} clears, no tags => 400; PatchNone: 405; missing resource => 404 T1/T2 armtest Patch. Mode comes from Type.Patch (PLAN 1.3). Types with PATCH-specific hooks add a T2 X12 Delete a parent children GET => 404; child list empty; recreating the parent starts empty T1 armtest ChildCascade X13 Delete an RG that holds an engine type at RG scope DELETE rg => 200/202; resource GET => 404; RG-wide and subscription-wide lists empty T1/T2 armtest RGCascade. miniblue defect today: RG delete walks a hard-coded legacy prefix list. Fixed by scope cleaners (PLAN 0.6) and Engine.DeleteScope (PLAN 1.2) X14 Delete an RG while a subscription-scope type has resources resource GET => 200; subscription-wide list unchanged T2 Gap in ADR-0005: no check. Propose ScopeSurvivesRGDelete. Guards over-eager cascade when DeleteScope lands X15 Unsupported verb POST or PUT on a collection, POST on an item without a registered action => 405 MethodNotAllowed T1 Gap in ADR-0005. Propose WrongMethod. Real ARM also sends an Allow header (verify) X16 Every non-2xx response JSON {"error":{"code","message"}}, application/json; target and details where validation names a field T1/T2 armtest ErrorEnvelope. target/details arrive with azerr.Error (PLAN 0.7) X17 Correlation headers every response carries x-ms-request-id and x-ms-correlation-request-id T2 Gap in ADR-0005 (ErrorEnvelope checks the request id on 4xx only). Both headers are set by AzureHeaders (internal/server/middleware.go:32-33) X18 Unknown route or unregistered type GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.Nope/things?api-version=... => 404 JSON envelope with an ARM code, not EndpointNotFound T2 ADR-0002 fixes a strict 404. The code is InvalidResourceType or NoRegisteredProviderFound (verify); pick one in the PLAN row that implements ADR-0002 and pin it here X19 Parallel PUT, PATCH, DELETE on one id no 5xx, no torn documents, under -race T2 Stays one test in internal/arm (ADR-0005). Only meaningful once CI runs the race detector (PLAN 0.1) X20 Tags lifecycle create with tags, read back via GET and list, update, clear with {}; tags preserved verbatim T3 azurerm fixture with tags on RG and one engine type. Per-service legacy coverage is in tests/tags_test.go X21 provisioningState on synchronous types PUT and GET => properties.provisioningState == "Succeeded" T1 armtest ProvisioningState, gated by Type.Provisioned. Real LRO types may show Creating, Updating, Deleting first; not modelled (ADR-0006)

docs.title: Resource groups
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes X23 RG delete is long-running DELETE rg => 202 with Location pointing at operationresults; polling => 200 T2 Pins today's legacy behaviour (internal/services/resourcegroups/handler.go:221-223 serves operationresults). PLAN 3.3 makes RG delete sync 200 and drops operationresults (ADR-0006); update this row in that PR. Deliberate deviation from real ARM X24 PUT an existing RG with a different location PUT rg => 409 InvalidResourceGroupLocation T2 miniblue accepts and overwrites the location today (handler.go:71-91 never compares) X25 PUT an RG without location, or with an invalid one missing => 400; invalid => 400 LocationNotAvailableForResourceGroup (verify) T2 Missing location is rejected today with a generic 400 (handler.go:66-69); the code is not asserted anywhere. Invalid locations are not validated X26 HEAD an RG HEAD rg => 204 when it exists, 404 when missing, no body T2 Exists (route registered in handler.go, r.Head). Assert both legs X27 List the resources in an RG GET rg/resources after creating one engine and one legacy resource => both listed with id, name, type, location, tags; $filter=resourceType eq '...' narrows T2 Returns [] unconditionally today (handler.go:215-217). Engine-backed at PLAN 3.3. ADR-0004 lists engine types only and has no $filter: gap. azurerm checks this list before deleting an RG (prevent_deletion_if_contains_resources, on by default) (verify) X28 DELETE a missing RG DELETE rg => 404 ResourceGroupNotFound T2 Exists, but returns 404 ResourceNotFound with a generic "under resource group" message today (handler.go:146-149, via azerr.NotFound). Fix the code, and the same for RG GET. Tests that assert the status only miss it

docs.title: Parents, names, locations, ETags
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes X29 PUT under a missing subscription, RG or parent resource missing RG => 404 ResourceGroupNotFound; missing subscription => 404 SubscriptionNotFound; missing parent => 404 ParentResourceNotFound (some RPs ResourceNotFound) (verify) T1/T3 armtest ParentMissing. Always on for engine types (ADR-0003). Subscription existence is not checkable until a multi-subscription model exists; GET /subscriptions/{id} accepts any id today. T3: a Terraform apply into a missing RG fails with the message surfaced X30 Invalid resource name PUT => 400 (InvalidResourceName or an RP-specific code (verify)); terraform apply exits non-zero and prints the message T3 Negative azurerm fixture. Rules per type in Validate through CheckName (ADR-0003); ADR-0003 rejects declarative name patterns on Type. Backlog item for the fixture is on the client suites page X31 checkNameAvailability POST /subscriptions/{s}/providers/{ns}/checkNameAvailability {name,type} => 200 {nameAvailable:true} for an unused name; after create => false, reason: AlreadyExists; invalid name => false, reason: Invalid T2 Provider-level chi route, not an engine action (ADR-0001). Some RPs use a locations/{l} variant (verify). Needs a store lookup by global name; there is no helper yet (see engine lessons) X32 PUT a regional resource with an unsupported location PUT => 400 LocationNotAvailableForResourceType T2 Via a Validate hook. No shared location helper exists; propose one (engine lessons). Global types have no location and are exempt X33 Optimistic concurrency If-Match mismatch => 412 PreconditionFailed; If-None-Match: * on an existing resource => 412; a type that requires If-Match and gets none => 400 MissingIfMatchHeader (verify) T2 Deferred until a type needs ETags. ADR-0003: the engine ignores If-Match, never requires it, and enforces only If-None-Match: *. Never require If-Match on a path azurerm deletes without it

docs.title: Providers
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes X34 List providers GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers => 200, 10 or more namespaces each with namespace, registrationState, registrationPolicy; GET /providers (tenant) => same shape T2 miniblue serves 17 fixed namespaces, all Registered (internal/services/subscriptions/handler.go:94-112) and has no tenant /providers route. docs.title: Subscriptions and tenants
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes X37 Subscription list and get list => 200; get known => 200 with state: Enabled, subscriptionId, tenantId; get unknown => 404 SubscriptionNotFound; malformed id => 400 InvalidSubscriptionId (verify) T2 GetSubscription echoes any id as Enabled (handler.go:44-50), so the unknown and malformed legs fail today. Defining which ids are "known" is a model decision tied to the multi-subscription work in the lifecycle row below X38 Tenants GET /tenants => 200, value[].tenantId T2 Exists (handler.go:52-63). Assert the shape X39 Subscription lifecycle and locations GET /subscriptions/{s}/locations => 200, non-empty; subscription create, cancel (state: Disabled), enable (Enabled), tags set, update and clear T2 Deferred: needs a multi-subscription model, which no PLAN row schedules.
