docs.title: Deployments
docs.text:
Bespoke handler. Today it serves RG scope only: list, PUT, GET, DELETE (internal/services/deployments/handler.go:40-52), synchronous, with no validate, cancel, export, HEAD, operations or other scopes. Real PUT is asynchronous (accepted, then running, then terminal); the sync deviation returns the terminal state at once (ADR-0006). Sequencing: PLAN 3.1 and 3.2, plus the deployments wave (T5) in SPIKE.

ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes X40 Create, show, list, delete at RG, subscription, management group and tenant scope PUT, GET, list, DELETE succeed at each scope; subscription-scope ids contain no /resourceGroups/ T2 Only RG scope exists today. Scope paths: /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/{n}, /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/{mg}/providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/{n}, /providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/{n} X41 Validate POST .../deployments/{n}/validate: valid template => 200 properties.provisioningState: Succeeded (also at tenant scope); structurally invalid template => 400 InvalidTemplate (verify) T2 No validate route today X42 Cancel completed deployment => 409 DeploymentCannotBeCancelled; nonexistent => 404 at RG, subscription and MG scope; running => Canceled T2 Under sync-only deployments a running state is unreachable, so the running leg is deferred. 404 code DeploymentNotFound (verify) X44 Export POST .../exportTemplate => 200 with the submitted template; nonexistent => 404; HEAD .../deployments/{n} => 204 when present (tenant scope too), 404 when absent T2 No export or HEAD route today X45 Outputs literal, parameter-derived and tenant().tenantId outputs resolve; reference() on a Key Vault resolves properties.vaultUri; reference() on an unsupported type fails the deployment T2 Only parameters() and variables() evaluate today. Do not emit a null output for an unresolvable reference() X46 Nested templates a template with a nested deployment resource creates an RG, the nested deployment and a resource in it; a subscription-scope deployment containing an RG resource creates the RG T2 Needs subscription-scope deployments (first row of this group) and in-process dispatch (PLAN 3.1) X47 Failure a failing resource gives a terminal Failed deployment with properties.error (code, message, details); a failing nested deployment is Failed too T2 miniblue already stores Failed plus the error; assert the nested case X48 Deployment operations GET .../deployments/{n}/operations lists one per resource with provisioningOperation, provisioningState, targetResource; GET .../operations/{id} returns one; unknown deployment or operation => 404 (MG and tenant scope too) T2 No operations route today. Field names (verify) X49 Deployment of an engine-registered type the resource appears via the engine GET with a canonical id and the same document a direct PUT produces T2 In-process Dispatcher.Put (PLAN 3.1); legacy types go over the HTTP fallback with the original Authorization header. Template resources without apiVersion default to 2023-01-01 (handler.go:188), so engine types must accept that version

docs.title: Client smoke and hierarchy
docs.text:
Pattern, trust and CI wiring for these rows are on client suites.

ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes X51 Azure SDK for Go, armresources RG create, get, list, update tags, exists, delete; policy definition CRUD with the LRO poller; ids canonical-cased; 404 after delete T4 New suite tests/sdk/go (own module). Pollers must finish against sync responses X52 Azure SDK for Python, azure-mgmt-resource RG, tags, deployment via begin_*().result() T4 New pytest module; base_url, credential_scopes, fake credential X53 az CLI scripted scenario cloud register, login, az group create/show/exists/list/delete, az policy definition create/show/delete, az deployment group create T4 New script plus a CLI version matrix. Feasibility first: the current guide says native az is not supported X54 Terraform negative fixture apply with an invalid name exits non-zero and the output contains the emulator's message T3 New azurerm fixture; pairs with the name validation row. Must assert the message, not only the exit code X55 Terraform combined fixture one fixture spanning RG, network, storage, Key Vault, identity; plan after apply shows no drift; second apply is a no-op T3 Partly covered by the examples/terraform and network, storage, keyvault, identity-rbac fixtures in acceptance-azurerm.yml. Add the cross-service fixture only if cross-type references need coverage

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Malformed JSON is 400 InvalidRequestContent as JSON. A 500 with text/plain breaks every SDK error parser.
  • Never map an unknown error code to 500. A client fault with an unmapped code hides the real cause; return the declared status.
  • Missing api-version is 400. Accepting it hides client bugs that real ARM rejects.
  • A duplicate role assignment is 409 RoleAssignmentExists. Asserting 400 would be wrong.
  • Per-service not-found codes (VirtualNetworkNotFound, SubnetNotFound, VMNotFound) are not ARM. Use ResourceNotFound, and ParentResourceNotFound for a missing parent (verify).
  • 404 messages name the right scope. "Under resource group" is wrong for subscription-scope resources.
  • If-Match must never be required on routes azurerm deletes without it. A required header breaks terraform destroy.
  • A bare 202 with no Location sends azurerm into its own poller (about 20 s) or stalls it. Return a terminal 200 or 201.
  • reference() on an unsupported type fails the deployment in real ARM. A null output with a Succeeded deployment is wrong.
  • A running deployment is unobservable in a sync engine. Do not write a cancel-while-running test until deployments are async.
  • Unrouted requests are not EndpointNotFound. Real ARM uses InvalidResourceType or NoRegisteredProviderFound (verify).
  • GET on an unknown provider namespace must not report Registered.
  • A HEAD 404 has no body. Assert the status only.
  • Single-subscription harnesses force unique RG names per test. Do not assume subscription isolation.
  • Never commit private keys or certificates for client trust. Generate them per run.

docs.title: Dropped
docs.text: ID Reason X22 Opt-in long-running operations are out of scope: ADR-0006 makes the engine sync-only (no 202, no Azure-AsyncOperation, no Location). A future async type is gated on a client that fails without 202; none is known. The SDK smoke rows cover poller behaviour against sync responses X43 What-if needs asynchronous deployments (real contract is 202 plus polling) and a diff engine. Out of scope per ADR-0006 and the deployments wave (T5) in SPIKE X50 Management groups are a service in their own right (root group, subscription placement, descendants). Belongs on a management-group page; only the generic parent-existence rule applies to this page

docs.title: Deployments and ResourceManager
docs.text:
Engine fit: bespoke for deployments and their actions (validate, cancel, exportTemplate, operations); hooks-style engine dispatch for the resources inside a template. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/deployments (resource group scope only, synchronous). Suggested wave: PLAN 3.1 (refactor(deployments): dispatch in-process via Engine.Do) and PLAN 3.2 (feat(deployments): order resources by dependsOn); extra scopes and actions after G3.

Deployments stay bespoke because they are an orchestrator, not a stored resource with a schema. They stop calling the router through a recorder and call Engine.Do instead, with an HTTP fallback for legacy types that forwards the original Authorization header (PLAN 3.1). The page also holds the resource group exportTemplate action, which is the other ResourceManager operation, and the shared resource id helper test.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Resource type api-versions seen (real latest (verify)) Scopes Children Non-CRUD ops Engine fit Needs (ADR seams) Value Effort Microsoft.Resources/deployments spec repo: 2024-11-01, 2025-03-01, 2025-04-01, 2026-06-01 (latest (verify)) RG, subscription, management group, tenant operations POST validate (200/202/400), POST cancel (204), POST exportTemplate (200), POST whatIf (200/202), HEAD (204/404); DELETE (202/204) bespoke Engine.Do in-process dispatch (PLAN 3.1), topo sort (PLAN 3.2), ChildID, template expression evaluator H L deployments/operations same same four scopes none list, GET by operationId bespoke per-resource operation records written during dispatch M S Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups exportTemplate resources spec 2025-04-01 (verify) RG none POST /subscriptions/{s}/resourcegroups/{rg}/exportTemplate (200/202) bespoke enumerate every resource in the RG (needs the /resources list from PLAN 3.3) M M

Real facts confirmed in the REST spec (api-version 2025-04-01):

  • Deployment name is 1 to 64 characters matching ^[-\w\._\(\)]+$.
  • mode is Incremental or Complete. Complete deletes resources in the group that are not in the template.
  • provisioningState enum: NotSpecified, Accepted, Running, Ready, Creating, Created, Deleting, Deleted, Canceled, Failed, Succeeded, Updating.
  • Cancel is allowed only while the state is Accepted or Running; afterwards the state is Canceled and resources are left partially deployed.
  • Deleting a deployment removes its operations. A running deployment cannot be deleted.
  • Deployment what-if change types: Create, Delete, Ignore, Deploy, NoChange, Modify, Unsupported.
  • Management group and tenant scopes use /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/{groupId}/providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/{n} and /providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/{n}. Operations list and GET exist at all four scopes in the spec.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • Resources dispatch through an in-memory router, not the engine. handler.go:211-223 builds an httptest request per resource. Nested ids are built ad hoc and dependsOn is ignored (index finding 11). PLAN 3.1 replaces this with Engine.Do.
  • Missing apiVersion silently defaults to 2023-01-01 (handler.go:188). Real Azure rejects the template. PLAN 3.1 returns 400 InvalidTemplate (verify).
  • No ordering. Resources deploy in template order; dependsOn, copy and condition are ignored. PLAN 3.2 adds a topo sort; a cycle gives 400.
  • Outputs are always {} (handler.go:124). Expression support is limited to a whole-string [parameters('x')] or [variables('x')] (template.go); no function calls, concatenation, reference(), resourceGroup() or tenant().
  • Resource group scope only. Routes: list, PUT, GET, DELETE (with a duplicate case-variant set). No subscription, management group or tenant scope; no HEAD; no validate, cancel, whatIf, exportTemplate or operations.
  • Failure shape is thin. A dispatch failure sets the deployment to Failed with error code DeploymentFailed; nested errors are not surfaced in error.details.
  • No template validation. A missing template is a 400, but there is no check for the $schema, contentVersion and resources members.
  • DELETE returns 204 and does not remove operations (there are none). Deployments are not removed when their resource group is deleted (see Resource groups).
  • Existing coverage: internal/services/deployments/handler_test.go (TestSimpleDeploymentDispatchesEachResource, TestParameterAndVariableSubstitution, TestDispatcherFailureMarksDeploymentFailed, TestGetDelete).

docs.title: Validate, cancel and DELETE
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T23 Validate a valid template succeeds. Validate {"hello":"world"} (no $schema, contentVersion, resources) fails. POST .../deployments/{n}/validate => 200, properties.provisioningState=Succeeded; invalid => 400 InvalidTemplate (verify) T2 The spec lists 400 for validate. Sync only: no 202. Validate runs the same checks as PUT without dispatching. G3-T24 Cancel a deployment that has already finished fails. Cancel an unknown deployment fails. POST .../cancel => 409 DeploymentCannotBeCancelled (verify); unknown => 404 DeploymentNotFound (verify) T2 The spec only documents 204 for cancel; both error codes are unconfirmed. With sync dispatch every deployment is already terminal, so 409 is the normal outcome. G3-N1 new: PUT, GET, HEAD, list and DELETE at resource group scope. DELETE then GET and HEAD report not found. PUT => 201 then 200; GET => 200; HEAD => 204 then 404; DELETE => 200 or 204 (spec 202/204; sync); GET missing => 404 DeploymentNotFound (verify) T2 Missing from the source. HEAD is absent today. Accept 200 or 204 on DELETE until a decision is recorded; do not return 202.

docs.title: Export template
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T26 Export the template of a finished deployment returns the original template. Unknown deployment fails. POST .../deployments/{n}/exportTemplate => 200, body template equals the submitted template; unknown => 404 DeploymentNotFound (verify) T2 Needs the deployment record to keep the submitted template. G3-T27 Resource group export. An empty RG exports resources=[] plus $schema. With several resources, resources:["*"] exports all and a specific resource id exports just that one. POST /subscriptions/{s}/resourcegroups/{rg}/exportTemplate => 200, template.resources per request T2 Bespoke. Depends on listing every resource in the RG (PLAN 3.3). Real Azure may add an error member for resources it could not export (verify). Spec also allows 202; stay 200. G3-T28 Export options change the output: IncludeParameterDefaultValue, IncludeComments (adds a description in metadata), SkipResourceNameParameterization (literal names), SkipAllParameterization (no parameters). Managed identity name and location are parameterized by default. POST exportTemplate with options => 200 with the matching shape T2 Option names and the identity parameterization are (verify) against the export request model. Low priority.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T29 Subscription scope: create and list deployments at subscription scope. A template containing a Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups resource creates that RG. PUT /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/{n} => 200 or 201; GET list => 200; the RG then exists T2 The spec allows 200 and 201. Subscription, management group and tenant deployments take a location in the body (verify). G3-T31 Tenant scope: create returns the tenant-scoped id; GET; DELETE (no content); HEAD existence 204; validate Succeeded; list with no deployments returns an empty array. PUT /providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/{n} => 200 or 201; GET => 200; DELETE => 200 or 204; HEAD => 204; list => 200, value=[] T2 Low value for an emulator. A tenant id has an empty namespace (ID.IsTenant()), so the id parses already.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T32 Operations of a deployment: one entry per deployed resource; an empty template gives none; GET by operation id returns it; unknown deployment and unknown operation fail. Repeat at all four scopes. GET .../deployments/{n}/operations => 200; GET .../operations/{id} => 200; unknown deployment or operation => 404 (verify) code T2 Bespoke records written during dispatch. Operation body fields (provisioningOperation, provisioningState, targetResource) are (verify). Management group scope needs a management group concept (see Dropped).

docs.title: Template evaluation and outputs
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T33 Outputs: a literal output, an output taken from a parameter, and tenant() used as a parameter default returns the default tenant id. GET deployment => 200, properties.outputs.<n>={type,value} T2 Needs an expression evaluator beyond today's whole-string substitution (handler.go:124 returns {}). Default tenant is ...0001 in miniblue. G3-T34 reference() of a Key Vault in the same template resolves properties.vaultUri in an output. GET deployment => 200, output equals the vault's vaultUri T2 reference() is read through Engine.Do GET (or the HTTP fallback for a legacy type). A reference() to a resource that does not exist fails the deployment in real Azure, not a null output (verify); see Pitfalls. G3-T35 Nested deployment (a Microsoft.Resources/deployments resource) at subscription scope provisions its inner resources. When an inner step fails, the nested deployment is Failed and the outer deployment reaches a terminal state (Failed) with the error carried in error.details. GET outer and nested => 200; states Succeeded or Failed as above T2 Nested ids come from ChildID. Inner failure shape (DeploymentFailed wrapper) (verify). G3-T37 A template containing Microsoft.Sql/servers deploys and the server can then be read. PUT deployment => 200 or 201; GET .../Microsoft.Sql/servers/{n} => 200 T2 Cross-type dispatch test for the SQL page. Runs over the HTTP fallback until SQL migrates.

docs.title: Dispatch and ordering (PLAN 3.1, 3.2)
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-N2 new: dependsOn orders deployment: resource B that depends on A (by resource id or by name) is created after A, across an engine type and a legacy type. Template order does not matter. PUT deployment => 200 or 201; creation order A then B; both GET => 200 T2 Acceptance for PLAN Gate G3 (dependsOn across an engine type and a legacy type). Observe order through the deployment's operations or resource creation timestamps (verify). G3-N3 new: a dependsOn cycle is rejected before anything is deployed. PUT deployment => 400 InvalidTemplate (verify) T2 PLAN 3.2. No resource may be created. G3-N4 new: a template resource without apiVersion is rejected. PUT deployment => 400 InvalidTemplate (verify) T2 PLAN 3.1. Replaces today's silent 2023-01-01 default. G3-N5 new: template-only keys never reach the stored resource: apiVersion, type, dependsOn, condition, copy, comments, scope are stripped before dispatch. GET deployed resource => 200, body has none of those keys T2 PLAN 3.1.

docs.title: Shared resource id helper
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T55 Build a resource id from a scope, a multi-level type and its names. Microsoft.ServiceBus/namespaces/topics/subscriptions/rules with name ns/topic/sub/rule gives the full id. A top-level type gives the short form. An empty (tenant) scope gives /providers/.... A type with a different number of segments than the name is not silently joined. unit: chaining arm.ChildID from the scope through each level yields the full id, and arm.ParseID of the result round-trips to the same string; mismatched segment counts are rejected (verify) against the ChildID contract T1 Unit test in internal/arm/*_test.go, not an HTTP scenario. arm.ParseID exists; the builder lands in PLAN 1.4 (ChildID). Used by deployments for PUT and outputResources.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A deployment with a missing apiVersion on a resource, or a dependsOn cycle, fails validation before any resource is created. Defaulting the version hides template bugs that real Azure surfaces.
  • Real Azure PUT on a deployment is long-running; a synchronous emulator returns the terminal body at once with 200 or 201. Do not return 202 or a Running state: clients poll forever if the poll URL is never completed.
  • reference() of a resource that does not exist, or whose type the template engine cannot read, fails the deployment. Resolving it to null and succeeding hides real template errors.
  • Cancel works only on Accepted or Running deployments and returns 204. A synchronous emulator has no running deployments, so cancel of a finished one is a conflict, not a no-op.
  • Deleting a resource group removes its deployments and their operations. Leaving them behind makes a recreated group show stale history.
  • A deployment name is limited to 64 characters of [-\w._()]; resource names inside the template follow their own type's rules.
  • dependsOn entries are either resource ids or bare resource names; both forms resolve to the same node.
  • Nested deployments take their own scope and apiVersion; inner ids must be built from the inner scope, not the outer one.
  • What-if is a long-running diff operation; it needs the async machinery that ADR-0006 deliberately leaves out.

docs.title: Dropped
docs.text: ID Reason G3-T25 Cancelling a running deployment needs asynchronous orchestration. Sync-only dispatch (ADR-0006) never leaves a deployment in Running, so there is nothing to cancel. Revisit if deployments become async. G3-T30 Management group scope. Management groups are not modelled and Microsoft.Management is out of scope; listing for an unknown group cannot be asserted without that store. G3-T36 What-if is a long-running operation (200/202) with a bespoke diff engine (Create, NoChange, Modify, Delete). Out of scope for the ARM foundation per SPIKE section 0; needs async (ADR-0006).

docs.title: Disk
docs.text: Engine fit: hooks for Microsoft.Compute/disks CRUD (defaults and derived diskState), engine-gap for the beginGetAccess / endGetAccess actions (Type.Actions) and the PUT create status, bespoke for the diskOperations poll route and the disk-SAS data plane. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/disks. Suggested wave: PLAN wave 2.

docs.text: Resource type api-versions seen (real latest (verify)) Scopes Children Non-CRUD ops Engine fit Needs (ADR seams) Value Effort Microsoft.Compute/disks 2024-03-02, 2025-01-02, 2026-03-02 (latest in spec) RG; list by RG and by subscription none PATCH; POST beginGetAccess, endGetAccess hooks + engine-gap Hooks.Defaults (diskState, timeCreated, uniqueId, access defaults, sku tier), Hooks.Validate (name, size), PatchMode merge, Type.Actions, per-type create-status override M S Microsoft.Compute/locations/diskOperations/{id} same subscription + location (verify) none GET (poll) bespoke none (chi route); only needed if beginGetAccess stays asynchronous M S Disk SAS data plane /disk-sas/{id} n/a (data plane) host/path routed by miniblue none HEAD, PUT range, GET range bespoke none (data planes never migrate, ADR-0007) L M

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
• No RG-existence check: CreateOrUpdate (internal/services/disks/handler.go:229) writes into any RG. Real: 404 ResourceGroupNotFound.
  • beginGetAccess (handler.go:316-327) answers synchronously with a fake accessSAS. No 202 + Location, no diskOperations route, no ActiveSAS state, no 409 on a second grant. endGetAccess (handler.go:330) does not change diskState.
  • No /disk-sas data plane (HEAD / range PUT / range GET).
  • Defaults that real ARM does not apply: location falls back to eastus (handler.go:138). Real ARM rejects a missing location with 400 LocationRequired (verify). SKU falls back to Standard_LRS (handler.go:152) (verify against real default).
  • PUT always returns 200 (handler.go:248), which matches the spec but conflicts with the ADR-0006 "201 on create" rule (see Pitfalls).
  • DELETE returns 204 for a missing disk and 202 on success (handler.go:297, handler.go:300). Real allows 200/202/204; the engine would return 200 or 204 per ADR-0006.
  • Existing coverage: tests/disks_test.go (TestManagedDiskLifecyclePatchAccessAndLists, TestManagedDiskUploadStateAndResourceGroupCascade) and azurerm_managed_disk in tests/terraform/azurerm/compute/main.tf.

docs.title: disks
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G1-T59 PUT an Empty 32 GB Premium_LRS disk with a location PUT => 200 (spec lists 200/202, never 201); body has diskState=Unattached, provisioningState=Succeeded, timeCreated, uniqueId, publicNetworkAccess=Enabled, networkAccessPolicy=AllowAll, sku.name=Premium_LRS, sku.tier=Premium, diskSizeGB=32 T2 Hooks.Defaults. Needs a per-type create-status override vs the ADR-0006 201 rule. Access-policy defaults and sku.tier value (verify) G1-T60 PUT a disk into an RG that does not exist PUT => 404 ResourceGroupNotFound T1 Generic engine check, no disk-specific code G1-T61 GET, list by RG, list by subscription, DELETE, GET again GET => 200; both lists contain the disk; DELETE => 200, 202 or 204; GET after => 404 ResourceNotFound; DELETE of a missing disk => 204 (verify) T1 Assert the code only, not the message text. Sync engine returns 200 or 204 on delete G1-T62 PATCH tags and diskSizeGB; PATCH a missing disk PATCH => 200 (spec 200/202), tags merged and diskSizeGB persisted; missing => 404 ResourceNotFound T2 PatchMode merge. Real rejects shrinking diskSizeGB and resizing an attached disk without deallocation (verify) G1-T63 POST beginGetAccess with access=Read and durationInSeconds Real: 202 + Location, poll to a final body with accessSAS. Engine (sync-only): POST => 200 with accessSAS; then GET disk => diskState=ActiveSAS T2/T4 Engine-gap: Type.Actions. Sync-only ADR means no 202. Add a T4 SDK poller run to prove an SDK poller completes on a sync 200 (verify). Never assert the SAS token value G1-T64 Poll the diskOperations/{id} URL returned by beginGetAccess GET => 200 status=InProgress then status=Succeeded with properties.output.accessSAS; unknown id => 404 T2 Bespoke. Only needed if the async form is kept; conflicts with sync-only ADR-0006. Assert the terminal shape, not the in-progress timing G1-T65 beginGetAccess on a disk that already has an active SAS 409 with an error code (verify) T2 Needs diskState tracked across calls. Code unconfirmed G1-T66 POST endGetAccess Real: LRO. Engine: POST => 204 (no body); diskState returns to Unattached; the SAS URL stops working T2 Type.Actions. "SAS stops working" depends on the T67 route (verify) G1-T68 azurerm_managed_disk, Premium_LRS, Empty, 32 GB terraform apply then refresh => clean plan; storage_account_type echoed T3 tests/terraform/azurerm/compute already has the resource; extend assertions

docs.title: Data plane (bespoke)
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G1-T67 Disk SAS endpoint: HEAD, ranged PUT, ranged GET HEAD => 200 with Content-Length = disk size; PUT with a Range/x-ms-range uploads bytes; GET with a range returns those bytes T2 Bespoke, low priority, stays a chi route. Exact headers real Azure uses on the SAS host (verify)

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Disk PUT is 200 or 202 only in the spec; there is no 201. Generated SDK clients check the expected status set, so an engine 201 on create can fail the poller (verify). Needs a per-type override or an ADR-0006 note.
  • DELETE is async in the spec (200/202/204). A missing disk is 204, not 404.
  • PUT is a full replace. managedBy, managedByExtended, diskState, sku.tier, timeCreated and uniqueId are server-owned; ignore them on input.
  • location is required on a tracked resource. Do not default it to the RG location.
  • Disk name: letters, digits, _ and -, up to 80 characters.
  • SKU names in the spec: Standard_LRS, Premium_LRS, StandardSSD_LRS, UltraSSD_LRS, Premium_ZRS, StandardSSD_ZRS, PremiumV2_LRS.
  • beginGetAccess and endGetAccess are LROs with a Location header in the spec. A sync 200 or 204 relies on SDK pollers treating a terminal initial response as done.
  • A fake SAS must be ephemeral and never asserted verbatim.

docs.title: Engine lessons
docs.text:
Engine fit: design guidance for the shared engine helpers and the porting workflow (not a service). miniblue today: the engine serves policyDefinitions only; armtest and the legacy route freeze file do not exist yet. Suggested wave: PLAN 1.4 and 1.5 for the helpers, Phase 4 for the recipe.

This page turns the design lessons about shared ARM helpers into decisions for miniblue's engine. It does three things: states each lesson with the real Azure behaviour behind it, restates the porting recipe and test skeleton in current ADR vocabulary, and cross-checks every lesson against the ADRs and the PLAN so the gaps are visible. It proposes amendments and PLAN rows; it edits neither.

Authoritative sources: ADR-0003 pipeline and hooks, ADR-0005 conformance, ADR-0006 sync and errors, ADR-0007 migration, PLAN. Scenarios that exercise these lessons are on cross-cutting scenarios.

Statements marked (verify) were not checked against the REST specs or provider source.

docs.title: Name validation
docs.text:
Lesson Detail Validate on PUT, not only in checkNameAvailability A helper that checks names only in the availability call lets invalid names through the create path. Real ARM rejects on PUT with 400 The rule is per type There is no universal name rule. Put the regex and length in the type's Validate hook through CheckName(name, re, min, max) (400 InvalidResourceName, ADR-0003). Declarative name fields on Type were rejected in ADR-0003 Share the rule with the name check The provider-level checkNameAvailability route and the PUT hook must use one regex per type, or the two drift Error code varies by RP InvalidResourceName is the default; some RPs use their own code (verify). Pin the code per type in its Sample (Invalid)

Constraints to confirm before asserting, all (verify):

Type Constraint Storage account 3 to 24 characters, lowercase letters and digits, globally unique SQL server 1 to 63 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, globally unique Service Bus namespace 6 to 50 characters, letters, digits and hyphens, starts with a letter, globally unique Virtual network, subnet 2 to 64 characters API Management service per Slice 2 (CheckName with 1 to 50)

docs.title: Id parsing
docs.text: Lesson Detail Parse structurally, not positionally Position-based parsing breaks on extension resources, names equal to a keyword (providers) and mixed-case segments. arm.ParseID is the structural parser; keep it Build ids from one helper Nested ids come from ChildID(parent, typeName, name) for both the PUT response and outputResources (ADR-0001, PLAN 1.4). A builder pairs each type segment with a name segment and handles the tenant-level empty scope Name casing is frozen at create Lookups are case-insensitive; the response keeps canonical keywords and the creating PUT's name casing (ADR-0003) Opaque names Some names carry characters such as ;rev= (APIM). Treat the segment as opaque after decoding; an encoded / inside a name is still open (SPIKE)

docs.title: Error taxonomy
docs.text:
One envelope everywhere: {"error":{"code","message","target"?,"details"?}} as application/json through azerr.Error (ADR-0006, PLAN 0.7). Never default an unmapped code to 500, and never invent per-service not-found codes.

Status Codes in use or planned When 400 InvalidRequestContent, MissingApiVersionParameter, InvalidApiVersionParameter, InvalidResourceName, InvalidParameter bad body, bad or missing api-version, bad name, hook validation 403 AuthorizationFailed, RequestDisallowedByPolicy RBAC or policy enforcement (ADR-0008) 404 ResourceNotFound, ResourceGroupNotFound, SubscriptionNotFound, ParentResourceNotFound, InvalidResourceType (verify) missing resource, RG, subscription, parent, unregistered type 405 MethodNotAllowed unsupported verb, PatchNone types 409 Conflict and type-specific codes such as RoleAssignmentExists; InvalidResourceGroupLocation; MissingSubscriptionRegistration duplicates, immutable-field changes, unregistered provider 412 PreconditionFailed If-None-Match: * on an existing resource 500 InternalServerError store or reader failure (never treated as not found)

Rules that follow:

  • Missing parent is ParentResourceNotFound, not a per-service code (VirtualNetworkNotFound, SubnetNotFound) (verify).
  • 404 messages are scope-aware: "under resource group" only at RG scope.
  • Hooks return *azerr.Error; a plain error becomes 400 InvalidRequestContent (ADR-0003 phase 8).
  • Any Reader or store failure is 500, so an outage never looks like an empty list.

docs.title: List and paging
docs.text: Lesson Detail Shape {"value":[...]} with nextLink only when the RP pages. Engine lists are sorted and prefix-safe (deleting x leaves x2) Scope variants Parent list, RG-wide and subscription-wide lists for the same type; Reader.Under serves the last two (ADR-0003, PLAN 1.2) Paging is deferred Clients that list follow nextLink if present, so omitting it is safe until a list is large. $top, $skip and $filter are RP-specific; add per type when a client needs them Generic resource list GET .../resourceGroups/{rg}/resources aggregates across types. It is [] today and becomes engine-backed at PLAN 3.3; $filter=resourceType eq is not planned

docs.title: Secrets handling
docs.text: Lesson Detail Never echo secrets on GET Admin passwords, keys, connection strings and similar fields are accepted on PUT and are never returned by GET. Keys come back only from a POST action (listKeys, listSecrets) The engine stores what the client sent There is no redaction step, so a typed model with a password field echoes it on GET. This is a documented deviation today, not Azure behaviour A Defaults hook cannot fix it Defaults output is persisted; stripping there loses the value an action later needs Needed seam Keep secrets in the stored document and project them out of GET, list and PUT responses; actions read the stored value. Declare the paths per type (the SPIKE called it SecretPaths). Requires an ADR-0003 amendment Some secrets are masked, not removed Named values and similar fields return a masked or empty value on GET (verify) per type

docs.title: Soft-delete
docs.text: Lesson Detail Behaviour Key Vault, App Configuration and API Management keep a deleted resource in a per-location deleted... collection. A recreate with the same name conflicts until purge. Purge of a purge-protected item is 409 Conflict (verify) Engine today DELETE hard-removes. Hooks never write (ADR-0003), so a hook cannot move a document into a deleted collection Needed seam A write-capable delete path, or a second registered type for the deleted collection plus an engine-owned move. Decide before the first soft-delete type migrates Interim Legacy soft-delete flows stay bespoke (ADR-0006, ADR-0007). purge_soft_delete_on_destroy is documented unsupported for APIM; the deleted-service GET is a strict 404

docs.title: POST actions
docs.text: Lesson Detail Instance actions are engine-owned listKeys, regenerateKey, listSecrets belong in Type.Actions, which lands with its first consumer (ADR-0001, ADR-0003, PLAN Phase 4). Authorisation strings follow {type}/{action}/action Provider-level operations stay chi routes checkNameAvailability, operationResults, locations/*, operations, deletedservices (exempt from the freeze file, ADR-0001) Subscription and deployment actions are not engine actions subscription cancel and enable, deployment validate, cancel, exportTemplate and what-if stay bespoke Unregistered action paths Fall through today; with ADR-0002 they become a strict 404

docs.title: Other helper lessons
docs.text: Concern Lesson Today Server-owned fields Keys, creation times, generated GUIDs and URLs must survive a replacing PUT. Copy from Current in Defaults; Defaults must be idempotent Covered by ADR-0003 and the DefaultsIdempotent check Global name uniqueness DNS-global names (storage, SQL server, Service Bus, Key Vault, ACR, APIM) conflict across RGs and subscriptions: 409 (storage uses StorageAccountAlreadyTaken (verify)) No helper. A hook can scan with Reader.Under, but a cross-subscription check needs a store-wide lookup Location location is required on regional types (400) and must be in the type's list (400 LocationNotAvailableForResourceType); global types have no location No helper. Each type would hand-roll it Tags Replace on PUT, default {}, PATCH per PatchMode. Limits of 50 tags, name up to 512, value up to 256 (verify) Modes covered; limits not enforced Singleton and default children default, current, $Default, RootManageSharedAccessKey exist or are auto-created, so GET is 200 before any PUT No seed mechanism (APIM Tier B needs one) Provider registration A per-subscription state; PUT under an unregistered namespace is 409 MissingSubscriptionRegistration; az auto-registers and retries Only the namespace list is derived from the registry (PLAN 3.4); no state, no gate Cross-resource side effects NIC and private endpoint IP allocation against a subnet, availability set membership, subscription creation seeding RBAC Out of engine scope: hooks are read-only. These stay bespoke ETag Optional per RP; mismatched If-Match is 412. Never require If-Match where azurerm deletes without it Engine ignores If-Match, sends no ETags

docs.title: Porting recipe
docs.text:
ADR-0007 holds the per-type checklist and is authoritative. The table below is the full mechanical sequence, with the steps ADR-0007 does not spell out marked "extra".

# Step Where Notes 1 Classify fit: passthrough, hooks, engine-gap, bespoke. If a gap needs an engine change, land it first with an internal/arm unit test and an ADR amendment internal/arm/* Gate G4: no new Type fields outside an ADR amendment 2 Register(reg *arm.Registry): one arm.Type per top-level type; children via Children internal/services/<rp>/types.go Name must be Namespace/type with one slash; a malformed, duplicate or incomplete type panics (internal/arm/registry.go:46-61) 3 Mount before the engine, gated by the service filter internal/server/server.go:178-181 if serviceEnabled("<svc>", allowed) { <pkg>.Register(armTypes) } precedes arm.NewEngine (extra) 4 Append the service name for /health internal/server/server.go:267-268 Extra. The /health list is built from the same filter 5 Delete the chi ARM routes and their lines in legacy_arm_routes.txt; keep data-plane and provider-level routes the old handler, freeze file Freeze file lands with PLAN 1.6; it does not exist yet. Engine shadows chi, so legacy state would dangle 6 Provider-level chi routes for checkNameAvailability and similar beside Register Exempt from the freeze file. Share the name rule with the hook 7 Add an armtest Sample tests/armsamples_<rp>_test.go One Sample of about 15 lines; Skip needs a reason (ADR-0005) 8 Port validation, defaults and actions into hooks; read through r.Store; copy generated values from r.Current hooks.go Hooks never write and never call Do 9 Bespoke tests for hook logic and coexistence tests/arm_<name>_test.go See the skeleton below 10 Remove the type's prefixes from the package's RG cleaner the package cleaner Delete the cleaner if it is empty 11 Bump store.SchemaVersion and add a CHANGELOG line state reset required: <type> moved to the ARM engine internal/store, CHANGELOG.md ADR-0004 and ADR-0007 12 Add the namespace to the provider list only if clients enumerate it internal/services/subscriptions/handler.go Optional; Microsoft.Authorization is already absent and policy works. PLAN 3.4 derives it later (extra) 13 Docs: services parity table and overview, a service page, mkdocs.yml nav, README service counts, CHANGELOG website/docs/services/* Extra. The contributing guide still documents the hand-written pattern (verify); add the engine recipe in the first porting PR 14 Terraform acceptance when the type is reachable from azurerm or azapi azapi: tests/terraform/azapi/<case>/{main.tf,run.sh} plus a job in acceptance.yml; azurerm: tests/terraform/azurerm/<fixture>/main.tf, a committed .terraform.lock.hcl (linux_amd64, darwin_arm64, windows_amd64) and a matrix entry in acceptance-azurerm.yml Extra. run.sh asserts apply, no drift, a no-op second apply, destroy. Linux or WSL2 only 15 Behaviour changes in a separate fix(<rp>) commit; PR title refactor(<rp>): serve <type> via arm engine git ADR-0007

A test that PUTs without creating its RG now gets 404 ResourceGroupNotFound. Fix the test setup, not the engine.

docs.title: Integration-test skeleton
docs.text:
After ADR-0005 the generic behaviour moves into the armtest Sample, so the bespoke file shrinks to what a Sample cannot say. Helpers already in tests/helpers_test.go: setupServer, doRequest, expectStatus, decodeJSON, decodeError. tests/arm_policydefinition_test.go is the worked example (five tests).

Test (file tests/arm_<name>_test.go) Asserts Covered by armtest instead TestArm<Thing>_Lifecycle PUT 201 then 200, mangled-case GET, list, DELETE 200 then 204, GET 404 PutCreate, PutReplace, Get, UrlCasing, List, Delete TestArm<Thing>_RequestValidation the type's own Validate codes (typed 400, 409) generic checks: MissingAPIVersion, NameIDMismatch, BadBody TestArm<Thing>_ScopeOnly a type registered at one scope falls through at the other scopes none; keep TestArm<Thing>_ComputedFieldsStable specific computed fields (ids, keys, endpoints) stable across a second PUT, no azurerm drift DefaultsIdempotent (generic) TestArm<Thing>_CoexistsWithHandWritten a hand-written neighbour on the same subscription still answers none; keep TestArm<Thing>_ServiceFilterAndReset SERVICES excluding the service leaves the type unmounted; /_miniblue/reset empties it none; keep TestArm<Thing>_CascadeOnResourceGroupDelete RG delete removes the resource RGCascade TestArm<Thing>_Actions listKeys and similar: status, body shape, case-mangled path none; keep once Type.Actions exists 
// Signatures only; bodies follow tests/arm_policydefinition_test.go.
func TestArmThing_RequestValidation(t *testing.T)    // hook codes only
func TestArmThing_ScopeOnly(t *testing.T)            // falls through at other scopes
func TestArmThing_CoexistsWithHandWritten(t *testing.T)
func TestArmThing_ServiceFilterAndReset(t *testing.T)
func TestArmThing_Actions(t *testing.T)              // after Type.Actions

docs.title: Migration notes
docs.text:
Wave order and gates are in PLAN Phase 4 and ADR-0007. Keep these in view:

Item Note Stays bespoke data planes always; keyvault, network (inline plus child sync), storageaccounts (PUT must return 200 (verify)), vm, aci, aks, sites, dbpostgres unless a fidelity or enforcement need arises (ADR-0007 gates G4, G5) Casing Legacy handlers mirror client casing; engine types return canonical casing. A move is a listed behaviour change Middleware order The engine must stay ahead of authorisation middleware so extension scopes resolve State Moving a type changes the key space; bump SchemaVersion Drift Idempotent Defaults is the guard against azurerm plan drift; the acceptance fixture proves it Cost Each migrated type adds one Sample (fast) and, if reachable, one Terraform job (slow). Batch azapi fixtures if the count grows

docs.title: ADR cross-check
docs.text:
"Covered" cites the ADR or PLAN row that already decides the lesson. "Gap" is a proposal, not a decision: an ADR amendment or a PLAN row for the owners to accept.

Lesson Already covered by Gap (proposal) Typed errors with target and details; generic codes ADR-0006, PLAN 0.7 none Code for an unrouted request ADR-0002 (strict 404, code open) pin InvalidResourceType or NoRegisteredProviderFound (verify) in the PLAN row that implements ADR-0002 Missing and malformed api-version ADR-0005, ADR-0006, PLAN 1.4 MalformedAPIVersion check is not in the ADR-0005 list; add it Name validation per type in hooks ADR-0003 (CheckName), PLAN 1.4 negative Terraform fixture for name errors (see client suites); share one rule between the hook and the availability route Id parsing and builder arm.ParseID; ChildID in ADR-0003 and PLAN 1.4 extend the id tests with builder cases (tenant-level scope, unpaired segments) RG and parent existence ADR-0003 phase 5 subscription existence needs a "known subscription" model; no PLAN row Server-owned fields, stable defaults ADR-0003 (Current, idempotent Defaults), ADR-0005 DefaultsIdempotent none Sub-wide list, prefix safety ADR-0004, PLAN 1.2 none Paging and nextLink none (SPIKE "Later") PLAN row feat(arm): $top and nextLink for lists, triggered by the first type whose list needs it RG /resources PLAN 3.3 $filter=resourceType eq is not covered; add to 3.3 or drop RG cascade ADR-0004, PLAN 0.6 and 1.2 ScopeSurvivesRGDelete check Secrets never echoed none (SPIKE "Later", SecretPaths) ADR-0003 amendment: declared secret paths projected out of responses; PLAN row feat(arm): secret path projection before the first secret-bearing type (SQL, APIM named values) Soft-delete and purge ADR-0006 and ADR-0007 keep legacy flows bespoke; APIM deletedservices is a strict 404 ADR amendment for a write-capable delete path or deleted-collection type, before App Configuration or Key Vault migrates POST instance actions ADR-0001, ADR-0003 (Type.Actions with first consumer), PLAN Phase 4 none checkNameAvailability ADR-0001 (provider-level chi route) shared name-taken helper (next row) Global-name uniqueness none helper arm.NameTaken(...) over a store-wide lookup, used by Validate and the availability route; PLAN row Location validation none helper arm.ValidateLocation(allowed...) added to the ADR-0003 helper list Tags limits none optional; verify limits first, then a shared Validate helper provisioningState ADR-0003 Provisioned, ADR-0005 ProvisioningState none Singleton and auto-created children none (SPIKE "Later"; APIM page notes the need) ADR amendment for a seed mechanism; PLAN row before APIM Tier B Provider registration state and 409 gate PLAN 3.4 (derive the list only) PLAN row: stored per-subscription state, unregister, tenant /providers, optional 409 gate default off Cross-resource side effects ADR-0003 (hooks are read-only), ADR-0007 (wave 4 optional) none; state explicitly that these stay bespoke Sync only, no LRO ADR-0006 none ETag and If-Match ADR-0003 (ignored, never required) opt-in ETag type flag only when a type needs it Deployments beyond RG-scope CRUD ADR-0001, PLAN 3.1 and 3.2 validate, exportTemplate, cancel, HEAD, subscription, management group and tenant scope, operations have no PLAN row (T5 in the SPIKE); what-if is out of scope Conformance additions ADR-0005 (16 checks) WrongMethod, ResponseHeaders, UnknownRoute, ScopeSurvivesRGDelete; see cross-cutting

docs.title: Proposed PLAN rows
docs.text:
Proposals only. Sizes are estimates; the PLAN owners decide numbering and dependencies.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A name rule enforced only in checkNameAvailability lets invalid names reach the store.
  • A per-service not-found code is not ARM. Use ResourceNotFound and ParentResourceNotFound.
  • Mapping an unknown error code to 500 turns client faults into server faults in every SDK.
  • Echoing a secret on GET is not Azure behaviour, even when the typed model makes it free.
  • A hook that writes under the engine lock breaks the ordering guarantees in ADR-0003. Needs that require writes need a seam, not a workaround.
  • Requiring If-Match breaks terraform destroy, which deletes without it.
  • Defaults that regenerate keys, GUIDs or timestamps on every PUT cause azurerm plan drift.
  • A bare 202 with no Location stalls the azurerm poller. Return a terminal status.
  • Moving a type without bumping SchemaVersion leaves dangling legacy state that is silently misread.

docs.title: Event Grid
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks for topics, namespaces and systemTopics; passthrough child for eventSubscriptions (plus a second, extension-scoped form); bespoke for the data plane and delivery. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/eventgrid (topics only, plus an accept-only publish route). Suggested wave: migration wave 2 (PLAN Phase 4, migrate-only, low value); namespaces, systemTopics and eventSubscriptions are new types after G2.

Control plane and data plane are separate. The data plane section covers only publish and a minimal webhook delivery; push-delivery retries, dead-lettering and pull delivery are out of scope.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Latest stable api-version is 2025-02-15 (confirmed in the REST spec repo); previews run up to 2026-06-15-preview. azurerm and azapi pins were not checked (verify). APIVersions is metadata only (ADR-0005), so any well-formed version is accepted.

Name rules from Learn: topics and domains 3 to 50 alphanumerics and hyphens, event subscriptions 3 to 64 alphanumerics and hyphens.

Resource type api-versions seen (real latest (verify)) Scopes Children Non-CRUD ops Engine fit Needs (ADR seams) Value Effort Microsoft.EventGrid/topics 2025-02-15 RG eventSubscriptions POST listKeys; POST regenerateKey body {keyName}; list by subscription and by RG hooks Type.Actions (listKeys, regenerateKey); Reader.Under for the subscription-wide list; PatchMode merge; Hooks.Defaults for endpoint, provisioningState, inputSchema, publicNetworkAccess M S Microsoft.EventGrid/namespaces 2025-02-15 RG namespace topics and their event subscriptions (not in the source scenarios) POST listKeys; POST regenerateKey body {keyName}; list by subscription and by RG hooks same as topics; sku is Standard with capacity 1 to 20 (spec) M S Microsoft.EventGrid/systemTopics 2025-02-15 RG eventSubscriptions list by subscription and by RG hooks Hooks.Validate (source and topicType required, verify); identity supported L S topics/eventSubscriptions, systemTopics/eventSubscriptions 2025-02-15 child of topics or systemTopics none GET {parent}/eventSubscriptions list; POST getFullUrl; POST getDeliveryAttributes passthrough Children; Type.Actions for both POSTs M S for CRUD, L with delivery Microsoft.EventGrid/eventSubscriptions (extension form) 2025-02-15 subscription, RG and resource scope: {scope}/providers/Microsoft.EventGrid/eventSubscriptions/{n} none POST getFullUrl; POST getDeliveryAttributes; global, regional and per-topic-type lists engine-gap a ScopeResource type; ADR-0003 does not existence-check extension resources at resource scope M S Data plane: POST /api/events on the topic endpoint not versioned through ARM (verify) per topic endpoint none event and CloudEvent schemas; validation-event handshake for webhook destinations bespoke background delivery worker; reads the stored subscription M M

PUT, PATCH and DELETE are long-running in the real spec (topics: PUT 201 only, PATCH 200 or 201, DELETE 202 or 204). miniblue is sync (ADR-0006): PUT 201 on create and 200 on replace, PATCH 200, DELETE 200 or 204.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value. Line numbers refer to internal/services/eventgrid/handler.go.

  • No eventSubscriptions in either form, so Bicep, Terraform and the SDK cannot create a subscription. No getFullUrl or getDeliveryAttributes.
  • No namespaces or systemTopics.
  • Topics have no PATCH, no subscription-wide list (the list route is RG-scoped only, lines 35-43) and no regenerateKey.
  • listKeys returns two fixed strings (lines 115-116), so rotation can never be observed.
  • DELETE returns a bare 202 with no Location or Azure-AsyncOperation header (line 96) and 404 when the topic is missing. ADR-0006 wants 200, or 204 when missing.
  • PUT ignores body decode errors (line 56), so a null or malformed body creates a topic. No location or name check.
  • The data plane route is POST /eventgrid/{topicName}/events (line 43). It only decodes a JSON array (line 120), never checks the topic exists, never delivers, and enforces no size limit.
  • The topic endpoint is hard-coded to https://<name>.eastus-1.eventgrid.azure.net/api/events (line 61). That host does not resolve locally, so an SDK publisher built from the ARM response cannot reach miniblue.
  • Store keys are case-sensitive concatenations (topicKey, eg:topic: prefix), so two spellings of the same id become two topics. Moving to the engine fixes this.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text: {t} is a topic name, {p} is the path /subscriptions/{s}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.EventGrid. Codes and statuses follow ADR-0006 (sync).

docs.title: topics
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T34 Creating a topic returns its endpoint and a succeeded state. PUT {p}/topics/{t} body {location} => 201; properties.endpoint is https://{t}.{region}-1.eventgrid.azure.net/api/events; properties.provisioningState is Succeeded; a second PUT => 200 T2 Flag: the spec lists only 201 for PUT (LRO). 200 on replace is the ADR-0006 sync rule. Defaults (verify): inputSchema EventGridSchema, publicNetworkAccess Enabled, minimumTlsVersionAllowed 1.2. G2-T35 Reading a topic returns what was created. GET {p}/topics/{t} => 200, same body as the PUT response T1/T2 G2-T36 Reading a missing topic. GET {p}/topics/{t} => 404 ResourceNotFound T1 Generic ARM not-found, covered by the armtest row once the type migrates. G2-T37 PATCH replaces the tags. PATCH {p}/topics/{t} body {tags} => 200; tags are the new set; properties unchanged T2 Spec marks PATCH as LRO (200 or 201); sync 200 here. PatchMode merge also covers the patchable properties (publicNetworkAccess, inboundIpRules, disableLocalAuth; verify the update model). G2-T38 A deleted topic is gone. DELETE {p}/topics/{t} => 200; GET => 404; DELETE again => 204 T1/T2 Flag: real DELETE is an LRO (202 or 204). Sync with no async headers. Tests against real Azure accept 202 or 204 and poll. G2-T39 Listing by resource group. GET {p}/topics => 200 {value:[...]} containing the created topic T1 G2-T40 Listing by subscription. GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.EventGrid/topics => 200 {value:[...]} including topics from other resource groups T1/T2 Needs Reader.Under; ADR-0005 makes subscription-wide list part of the generic row for RG-scoped top-level types. G2-T41 listKeys returns two non-empty keys. POST {p}/topics/{t}/listKeys => 200 {key1, key2}; the values are stable across calls; missing topic => 404 T2 Fixed placeholder strings today; generate random base64 keys at create time. G2-T42 regenerateKey rotates only the named key. POST {p}/topics/{t}/regenerateKey body {"keyName":"key1"} => 200 {key1, key2}; key1 changed, key2 unchanged; keyName is required T2 Spec marks it 200 or 202 (LRO); sync 200 here. An unknown keyName is a 400 (verify code).

docs.title: namespaces
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T43 Namespaces follow the same lifecycle as topics. PUT 201 then 200, GET 200, missing GET 404, PATCH tags 200, DELETE 200, list by RG and by subscription 200 for {p}/namespaces/{n} T1/T2 Mirrors G2-T34 to G2-T40. sku defaults to Standard; capacity range is 1 to 20 (spec). Properties include topicsConfiguration, isZoneRedundant, publicNetworkAccess, minimumTlsVersionAllowed. G2-T44 Namespaces have listKeys and regenerateKey. POST {p}/namespaces/{n}/listKeys => 200 {key1, key2}; POST .../regenerateKey body {keyName} => 200 and the named key changes T2 Same shape as topics (spec confirms key1, key2, required keyName).

docs.title: systemTopics
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T45 System topics follow the same lifecycle. CRUD, PATCH, list by RG and by subscription for {p}/systemTopics/{n}; properties.source and properties.topicType are required on create, a missing one => 400 T2 Mirrors G2-T34 to G2-T40. Required-ness of source and topicType is inferred (verify). Properties include provisioningState, metricResourceId; the resource supports identity.

docs.title: eventSubscriptions
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T46 Event subscriptions have a full lifecycle under a topic. PUT {p}/topics/{t}/eventSubscriptions/{e} => 201 then 200; GET 200; PATCH 200; GET {p}/topics/{t}/eventSubscriptions => 200 {value:[...]}; DELETE => 200 then GET => 404; missing topic => 404 ParentResourceNotFound T2/T3 Serve both forms: the child path above and {scope}/providers/Microsoft.EventGrid/eventSubscriptions/{e} at subscription, RG and resource scope (the extension form, spec PUT 201). Which form azurerm and Bicep use is (verify). Name 3 to 64 alphanumerics and hyphens. In real Azure a webhook destination is validated at create (see G2-T48). G2-T47 getFullUrl and getDeliveryAttributes are POST actions on a subscription. POST .../eventSubscriptions/{e}/getFullUrl => 200 {endpointUrl}; POST .../getDeliveryAttributes => 200 {value:[{name, type, properties{value, isSecret}}]} T2 Response shapes are inferred (verify). Both are Type.Actions on the child and the extension form.

docs.title: Data plane (bespoke)
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T48 Publishing to a topic endpoint delivers to a webhook subscription after a validation handshake. POST /api/events with an event array => 200; a subscription whose destination is a local webhook first receives a Microsoft.EventGrid.SubscriptionValidationEvent carrying a validationCode, the endpoint answers with validationResponse, then the published event arrives T2 Bespoke delivery worker; the test starts its own webhook with httptest.NewServer. Real Azure requires a valid aeg-sas-key or AAD token (401 otherwise, verify); decide whether miniblue checks it. Retries and dead-lettering are out of scope. G2-T49 A very large batch of small events. POST /api/events with more than 5000 events => 400 (verify) T2 Not confirmed: Learn documents no per-batch event count, only the 1 MB array limit (G2-T50). Do not implement until confirmed. G2-T50 An oversized payload is rejected. POST /api/events with a body over 1 MB, single event or array => 413 T2 Limit is 1 MB per request per Learn; the exact error body is (verify).

docs.title: Template deployment
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T51 A template can create a topic with event subscription children. deployment with Microsoft.EventGrid/topics and Microsoft.EventGrid/topics/eventSubscriptions succeeds; both resources exist afterwards T2 Cross-owner: depends on the deployments dispatch (PLAN 3.1, ChildID for nested ids) and on eventSubscriptions being registered. See deployments.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T52 Bad create requests are rejected. PUT {p}/topics/{t} with a null body, an empty body or no location => 400 (LocationRequired for a missing location, verify); a name outside 3 to 50 alphanumerics and hyphens => 400 InvalidResourceName (verify code) T1/T2 Body validation and CheckName (ADR-0003). Today decode errors are ignored (handler.go:56). The source's "missing name" case has no equivalent: an empty name segment is a different route.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Topic PUT is spec'd as 201 only, and DELETE is 202 or 204; both are long-running. miniblue returns 201 or 200 and 200 or 204 (ADR-0006). A 202 with no operation header leaves pollers without a status URL, so do not keep today's bare 202.
  • Event subscriptions are extension resources in real clients. Serving only the child-of-topic form misses {scope}/providers/Microsoft.EventGrid/eventSubscriptions/{n} (verify which form azurerm and Bicep use). Resource-scope extension resources are not existence-checked by the engine (ADR-0003).
  • Webhook destinations are validated during create. Real Azure fails the PUT when the endpoint does not answer the validation event (verify), so a subscription must not be marked Succeeded while the handshake is pending.
  • regenerateKey is the Event Grid spelling with body {keyName} and key1/key2 in the response. Event Hubs and Service Bus use regenerateKeys with keyType. Do not share one handler.
  • Static keys hide rotation bugs. Rotate only the named key and leave the other untouched.
  • The publish limit is 1 MB per request, with 413 above it. A per-batch event count of 5000 is not documented (verify).
  • inputSchema (EventGridSchema, CloudEventSchemaV1_0, CustomEventSchema) decides the shape the data plane must accept; a topic created for CloudEvents rejects the Event Grid schema in real Azure (verify).
  • Real publish endpoints are regional DNS names that do not resolve locally. Return an endpoint that reaches miniblue, or SDK publishers cannot be tested.
  • Tag PATCH replaces the whole tag set rather than merging keys (verify).
  • Ids are case-insensitive. Normalise on lookup and return canonical casing.

docs.title: Dropped
docs.text: ID Reason G2-T53 Wrappers (CLI and MCP tools) over the same REST calls; not portable and no new behaviour.

docs.title: Event Hubs
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks for namespaces, passthrough child for eventhubs and authorizationRules (with a POST action for the keys), passthrough singleton for networkRuleSets/default, bespoke for the AMQP and Kafka data planes (out of scope). miniblue today: none (no internal/services package, no registration for Microsoft.EventHub). Suggested wave: new types after G2 (SPIKE rank 5).

The data plane is out of scope. No AMQP listener, no Kafka endpoint, no message storage. The serviceBusEndpoint string is derived and does not resolve. The control plane is enough for azurerm, azapi and Bicep to plan, apply and destroy.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Latest stable api-version is 2026-01-01 (confirmed in the REST spec repo). Other stable versions: 2014-09-01, 2015-08-01, 2017-04-01, 2021-11-01, 2024-01-01; previews run to 2026-07-01-preview. azurerm imports the 2024-01-01 clients for namespaces, network rule sets and namespace authorization rules (provider source, verify per release). APIVersions is metadata only (ADR-0005), so any well-formed version is accepted.

Name rules from Learn:

  • Namespace: 6 to 50 characters, alphanumerics and hyphens, starts with a letter, ends with a letter or number, globally unique.
  • Eventhub: 1 to 256 characters of alphanumerics, periods, hyphens and underscores, starting and ending alphanumeric.
  • Authorization rule: 1 to 50 characters, same character set, starting and ending alphanumeric.
Resource type api-versions seen (real latest (verify)) Scopes Children Non-CRUD ops Engine fit Needs (ADR seams) Value Effort Microsoft.EventHub/namespaces 2026-01-01, 2024-01-01 RG eventhubs, authorizationRules, networkRuleSets list by subscription and by RG; POST /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.EventHub/checkNameAvailability (no source scenario) hooks Hooks.Defaults (provisioningState, status, createdAt, updatedAt, serviceBusEndpoint, metricId); PatchMode merge (real PATCH exists); a create-time hook that seeds the default authorization rule; Reader.Under for the subscription list; global name uniqueness H S namespaces/eventhubs 2026-01-01, 2024-01-01 child of namespaces authorizationRules, consumergroups (no source scenario) list by namespace passthrough parent existence (built into the engine, ADR-0003); partitionCount 1 to 32, messageRetentionInDays 1 to 7 per the spec description (verify) H S namespaces/authorizationRules 2026-01-01, 2024-01-01 child of namespaces none POST listKeys; POST regenerateKeys body {keyType, key?} passthrough Type.Actions; key generation; seed RootManageSharedAccessKey on namespace create (verify) M S namespaces/eventhubs/authorizationRules 2026-01-01, 2024-01-01 child of eventhubs none POST listKeys; POST regenerateKeys passthrough same as namespace rules L S namespaces/networkRuleSets/default 2026-01-01, 2024-01-01 child of namespaces; singleton none GET .../networkRuleSets list passthrough Hooks.Validate (name must be default); a GET that succeeds before any PUT L S AMQP and Kafka data plane not ARM per namespace endpoint none produce and consume bespoke, out of scope an AMQP 1.0 listener; message store M L

Spec status codes: namespace PUT is 200, 201 or 202 (LRO); eventhub PUT is 200 only; rule PUT is 200; DELETE is 200 or 204 (namespace also 202); listKeys and regenerateKeys are 200. miniblue is sync (ADR-0006): PUT 201 on create and 200 on replace, DELETE 200 or 204.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
• No Event Hubs support at all. Microsoft.EventHub is not registered and no handler exists, so any azurerm_eventhub* or Bicep deployment fails on the first namespace PUT.
  • azurerm's namespace read calls GET networkRuleSets/default and listKeys on the default RootManageSharedAccessKey rule (provider source, namespace resource read path). A namespace that does not seed both makes the read fail even when PUT succeeds (verify the exact failure).
  • Global namespace-name uniqueness has no precedent in the engine. Decide the behaviour (see Pitfalls).

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text: {p} is /subscriptions/{s}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.EventHub. Statuses follow ADR-0006 (sync).

docs.title: namespaces
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T54 Terraform azurerm creates and destroys a namespace. azurerm_eventhub_namespace apply then destroy => both succeed with no drift on a second plan T3 Apply path: namespace PUT, read (GET namespace, GET networkRuleSets/default, listKeys on RootManageSharedAccessKey), destroy DELETE then a poll until GET => 404. Needs sku and defaults. Pins 2024-01-01 (verify per release). G2-T55 Terraform azapi creates and destroys a namespace. azapi_resource of type Microsoft.EventHub/namespaces@<version> apply then destroy => both succeed T3 azapi sends the body as written and reads back the PUT response. Works at any well-formed api-version because APIVersions is metadata only. G2-T58 A namespace can be created, read and updated. PUT {p}/namespaces/{n} body {location, sku{name, capacity}} => 201; GET => 200; PUT again or PATCH with changed properties => 200 and the new values on GET T2 Properties to round-trip: tags, sku, isAutoInflateEnabled, maximumThroughputUnits, kafkaEnabled, minimumTlsVersion, publicNetworkAccess. sku.name is required (Basic, Standard or Premium); capacity range per the spec description (0 to 20 for Basic and Standard, 0 to 10 for Premium; verify). PATCH exists in the real API and runs in merge mode.

docs.title: eventhubs
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T56 Terraform creates and destroys an event hub with both providers. azurerm_eventhub and an azapi_resource of Microsoft.EventHub/namespaces/eventhubs apply then destroy => both succeed T3 Needs partitionCount and messageRetentionInDays (spec 1 to 7, verify) round-tripped, and the server-set partitionIds, status, createdAt, updatedAt. Flag: the spec lists only 200 for the eventhub PUT; the engine returns 201 on create (ADR-0006). Clients accept both (verify with the pinned azurerm version). G2-T57 az eventhubs eventhub works end to end. create => the hub exists; show => 200; list => contains every hub in the namespace; delete => gone, list no longer has it T2/T4 The REST equivalent is PUT, GET, GET {p}/namespaces/{n}/eventhubs and DELETE => 200 then 204 on repeat. No data-plane call is involved. G2-T62 Eventhub operations under a namespace that does not exist fail with a not-found. PUT {p}/namespaces/{n}/eventhubs/{h} with no namespace => 404 ParentResourceNotFound; GET of a missing hub in an existing namespace => 404 ResourceNotFound T1/T2 Asserted codes are the generic ARM ones from the engine (ADR-0003). Real Event Hubs may answer ResourceNotFound for a missing namespace (verify); azurerm treats any 404 as absent, so assert 404 and accept either code if real-Azure parity matters. Flag: per-service not-found codes are not asserted.

docs.title: networkRuleSets and authorizationRules
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T59 networkRuleSets exists only as default. PUT {p}/namespaces/{n}/networkRuleSets/default => 200; GET returns trustedServiceAccessEnabled, defaultAction (Allow or Deny), virtualNetworkRules, ipRules, publicNetworkAccess (Enabled, Disabled or SecuredByPerimeter); any other name => 404 T2 In the spec the path is the literal default, so other names have no route; the exact error code is (verify). GET before any PUT should return a default set (Allow, empty rules; verify) because azurerm reads it unconditionally. GET .../networkRuleSets lists the single default. G2-T60 listKeys on an authorization rule returns the keys and connection strings. POST {p}/namespaces/{n}/authorizationRules/{r}/listKeys => 200 {primaryConnectionString, secondaryConnectionString, aliasPrimaryConnectionString, aliasSecondaryConnectionString, primaryKey, secondaryKey, keyName}; keyName equals {r}; keys are base64 256-bit values; missing rule or namespace => 404 T2 Shape confirmed against the spec; the connection-string format Endpoint=sb://{n}.servicebus.windows.net/;SharedAccessKeyName={r};SharedAccessKey={key} is (verify). Alias fields are empty without geo-disaster recovery (verify). The rule PUT requires properties.rights (Manage, Send, Listen); Manage alone being invalid is (verify). regenerateKeys takes {keyType: PrimaryKey or SecondaryKey, key?} (keyType required) and changes only that key. Namespace create seeds RootManageSharedAccessKey with all three rights (verify); azurerm depends on it.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Namespace names are DNS labels and unique across Azure. A duplicate name in another resource group or subscription conflicts in real Azure. Decide whether miniblue enforces uniqueness (cheap to do with Reader.Under in a single-tenant store) and note it in the PR.
  • The eventhub PUT is 200 in the spec, not 201. A test that asserts 201 on real Azure fails; accept 200 or 201.
  • Namespace PUT is an LRO (200, 201 or 202) in real Azure. miniblue is sync (ADR-0006); SDK pollers accept the synchronous result.
  • The key-rotation action is regenerateKeys with keyType, unlike Event Grid's regenerateKey with keyName. listKeys returns six string fields plus keyName, not just two keys.
  • Keys are 256-bit base64 values. Generate them randomly at rule create, keep them stable until regenerated, and keep primary and secondary distinct.
  • RootManageSharedAccessKey exists on every real namespace. Without it, azurerm's read fails or drifts (verify).
  • networkRuleSets/default is a singleton that exists before any PUT. A 404 on first GET breaks azurerm's read. publicNetworkAccess appears on both the namespace and the rule set.
  • Invented service-specific not-found codes are wrong; ARM clients key off ResourceNotFound and ParentResourceNotFound.
  • Partition count and retention are constrained: partitionCount is 1 to 32 and cannot change after create on Basic and Standard (verify); retention is 1 to 7 days per the spec description (verify).
  • Ids are case-insensitive. Normalise on lookup and return canonical casing.

docs.title: Dropped
docs.text: ID Reason G2-T61 AMQP producer and consumer round trip: data plane, out of scope (no AMQP listener).

docs.title: Insights (Application Insights)
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks for components; bespoke for currentbillingfeatures and for the ingestion and query data planes. miniblue today: none (no internal/services/insights; Microsoft.Insights is not in supportedProviders, internal/services/subscriptions/handler.go:94-112). Suggested wave: new type after G2, shipped in the same PR as Log Analytics.

Common azurerm modules create a Log Analytics workspace and a workspace-based azurerm_application_insights that points at it (workspace_id). Treat the two pages as one deliverable: components without workspaces fails the first terraform apply of most modules.

Scope: the ARM control plane (components, currentbillingfeatures) plus a small bespoke data plane (telemetry ingestion and query). Alerts, workbooks, web tests, eventtypes and API keys are out of scope and have no scenario ids.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Resource type api-versions seen (real latest (verify)) Scopes Children Non-CRUD ops Engine fit Needs (ADR seams) Value Effort Microsoft.Insights/components 2020-02-02, 2015-05-01 (spec dirs; latest stable (verify)) RG; list by subscription currentbillingfeatures none hooks Defaults with Request.Current (stable AppId, InstrumentationKey, ConnectionString), ListSubscription (PLAN 1.2), PatchMode tags (real PATCH is a tags update (verify)), RG existence, Provisioned H S components/currentbillingfeatures 2015-05-01 singleton under a component (no name segment (verify)) none none bespoke parent existence (ParentResourceNotFound) L S Ingestion POST /v2/track, /v2.1/track (data plane) n/a host from the component's IngestionEndpoint none batch envelope bespoke none (not ARM, stays chi) M M Query POST /v1/apps/{appId or ikey}/query (data plane) v1 host from the component's endpoint none KQL subset bespoke none (not ARM, stays chi) M L

Property names on components are PascalCase in this provider (Application_Type, Flow_Type, Request_Source, WorkspaceResourceId, InstrumentationKey, ConnectionString, AppId, RetentionInDays, IngestionMode) (verify). Engine responses are canonical-cased (ADR-0005), so pin the casing in Sample and check azapi round trips.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
• No service at all: no components, no currentbillingfeatures, no data plane. Everything below is greenfield.
  • Microsoft.Insights and Microsoft.OperationalInsights are missing from supportedProviders (internal/services/subscriptions/handler.go:94-112), so provider list and register calls do not show them. Whether azurerm's registration check reads this list is (verify).
  • Stable generated values (AppId, InstrumentationKey) need either derivation from the resource id or Request.Current copy-forward in a Defaults hook. Regenerating per PUT breaks cached connection strings.
  • ConnectionString endpoint hosts must point at miniblue, otherwise SDKs ship telemetry out of the emulator.
  • List by subscription depends on the engine seam in PLAN 1.2.
  • Ingestion and KQL query are not started. Query is the expensive part: scope to take, where, count first.

docs.title: components
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T63 Create, read, delete a component. PUT components/{n} => 201 with properties; GET => 200; DELETE => 200; GET after => 404 ResourceNotFound. A second DELETE => 204 (verify). T1 Generic lifecycle; the real DELETE is documented as 200 or 204 (verify). G2-T64 A new component exposes a GUID instrumentation key and a connection string built from it. GET => 200; InstrumentationKey is a GUID; ConnectionString starts InstrumentationKey={key}; and carries IngestionEndpoint= and LiveEndpoint=; AppId is a GUID. T2 Endpoint hosts must be miniblue's. Keys stay identical across later PUT and PATCH. G2-T65 List by resource group returns every component created in it. GET .../resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.Insights/components => 200, all created names present, none from other groups. T1 G2-T66 List by subscription returns all components. GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.Insights/components => 200, all created names present. T1 Needs ListSubscription (PLAN 1.2). G2-T67 Update tags with PATCH. PATCH components/{n} body {tags} => 200; next GET shows the new tags; other properties unchanged. T1 PatchTags (verify). G2-T68 Deploy a component with a workspace link through an ARM deployment. Deployment succeeds; GET components/{n} => WorkspaceResourceId equals the template value (case preserved). T2 Goes through the deployments service. Depends on Log Analytics workspaces existing. G2-T73 azurerm create and destroy a workspace-based azurerm_application_insights. Apply and destroy succeed; application_type as set; instrumentation_key populated; connection_string contains the key; daily_data_cap_in_gb persisted. T3 Needs T69 and T71. New fixture: no Insights fixture exists today. Pair with the workspace fixture.

docs.title: currentbillingfeatures
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T69 Default billing features for a new component. GET components/{n}/currentbillingfeatures => 200; plan list contains Basic; DataVolumeCap present. T2 Response is a flat object, not under properties (verify). G2-T70 Switch the plan list to include the Enterprise plan. PUT with CurrentBillingFeatures including Application Insights Enterprise => 200; next GET lists it. T2 (verify): the retention limit that triggers this is unclear (30 versus 90 days in the notes). Treat the retention link as unconfirmed and assert only the persisted plan list. G2-T71 Set a daily data cap. PUT body with DataVolumeCap.Cap => 200; next GET returns the same cap. T2 azurerm reads this for daily_data_cap_in_gb. G2-T72 Billing features for a missing component. GET or PUT => 404 ResourceNotFound. T2 The engine rule for a missing parent is ParentResourceNotFound; which code this provider returns is (verify).

docs.title: Data plane (bespoke)
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T74 Post telemetry items (request, trace, exception, event, metric, dependency, and a batch). POST /v2/track and /v2.1/track => 200 with {itemsReceived, itemsAccepted, errors}; unknown instrumentation key => 401 (verify). T2 bespoke Real ingestion answers 206 on partial success (verify). The 401 for an unknown key is unconfirmed. G2-T75 Query ingested telemetry. POST /v1/apps/{key}/query => 200 with tables[0].name == "PrimaryResult"; take, where, count return the ingested rows. T2 bespoke Start with take, where, summarize count. Defer bin, join, ago, between. An unknown table is a 400 query error in real Azure (verify), not an empty result.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• AppId, InstrumentationKey and ConnectionString are stable for the life of the component. Real Azure never changes them on update.
  • The retention default differs by product: components default to 90 days, Log Analytics workspaces to 30. Copying one default to the other is wrong (verify).
  • A missing or malformed api-version is 400; any well-formed version is accepted. Do not return 400 for an api-version the spec does not list.
  • Real ARM PUT on an existing resource returns 200, not 201. Asserting 201 on update would be wrong.
  • A query on a table that does not exist is an error in real Azure (verify). An emulator may choose to return an empty table, but the doc assertion is the error.
  • currentbillingfeatures has no resource name segment in its path (verify); engine-registered child types assume {parent}/{type}/{name}.
  • Telemetry ingestion with a partial failure is a 206, and the envelope's errors carry per-item index and statusCode (verify).

docs.title: Key Vault
docs.text:
Engine fit: hand-written control plane today (vaults, access policies, deleted vaults); could move to hooks plus CheckName as an optional ARM shell. The keys and certificates data plane is bespoke and the biggest data-plane gap; secrets stay on chi. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/keyvault (vaults, accessPolicies, deletedVaults, and a secrets-only data plane). Suggested wave: wave 4 for the ARM shell (optional; PLAN phase 4); keys and certificates are not an engine job (data planes never migrate, ADR-0007).

The control plane is already close to complete. The scenarios below mostly tighten it (name validation, RG check, delete status codes, recover mode) and then add the two missing data planes. Keys and certificates are the large work: they are standalone chi routes backed by Go crypto/* and crypto/x509, with no ARM involvement.

docs.text:
