Spec facts used below (confirmed in the 2026-05-15 management-plane spec): create requires location and properties; properties requires tenantId and sku; enableSoftDelete defaults to true and cannot be turned off; softDeleteRetentionInDays is 7 to 90, default 90; createMode is recover or default; checkNameAvailability takes name and type (both required) and its reason is AccountNameInvalid or AlreadyExists; PUT and DELETE on a vault list 200 and 201 (create) or 200 and 204 (delete).

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • Keys data plane is absent. No create, get, list, versions, delete, recover, purge, rotation policy, rng, encrypt, decrypt, wrap or unwrap routes (internal/services/keyvault/handler.go:33-74 is the route table).
  • Certificates data plane is absent (create, import, pending, merge, versions, policy).
  • Secrets data plane is partial. Set, get, get by version, list, delete, deletedsecrets get and purge exist. Missing: list versions, update attributes, backup and restore, recover, and deleted list (handler.go:33-74).
  • Persistence bug for secrets. Secrets are stored as a Go struct and read back with a type assertion (handler.go:574, handler.go:654); after a restart or on a Postgres store the assertion fails and data is dropped. Store plain JSON-shaped maps.
  • Vault PUT does no name validation and no RG-exists check (CreateOrUpdateVault, handler.go:280-302). vaultNamePattern (handler.go:456) and validVaultName (handler.go:458, also rejects --) are only used by CheckNameAvailability (handler.go:462).
  • No createMode=recover on PUT, although deleted-vault list, get and purge exist. Purge is DELETE => 204 (handler.go:523) and POST .../purge => 202 (handler.go:530); sync-only (ADR-0006) wants 200 for the POST form.
  • Faked async headers. setOperationHeaders (handler.go:273) and the 200-with-headers DELETE (handler.go:336) emulate an LRO. Sync-only drops them.
  • DELETE of a missing vault returns 404 (handler.go:336); the spec lists 200 or 204, so 204 is expected (verify).
  • Vault PATCH exists (handler.go:304), as do access policy updates (handler.go:390, add, remove, replace; invalid operation is 400) and subscription list (handler.go:380).
  • Existing coverage: tests/keyvault_test.go (TestKeyVaultCRUD, TestKeyVaultDataPlaneVaultAzureNetHostCRUD, TestKeyVaultARMVaultCRUDAndAccessPolicies) and an azurerm fixture at tests/terraform/azurerm/keyvault/main.tf. No keys or certificates tests.

docs.title: Vaults (control plane)

PUT vaults/{n} with 2 chars, a leading digit, a trailing -, --, more than 24 chars, or an illegal char => 400 VaultNameNotValid (verify); a-b1 => 201. T2 Hooks.Validate. The error code is (verify). G2-T86 Name availability. POST checkNameAvailability {name, type} => 200: existing vault nameAvailable:false, reason:AlreadyExists; invalid name false with AccountNameInvalid; soft-deleted name false with AlreadyExists (verify); free name true. G2-T88 Create with each security option and tags. PUT => 201; GET reflects enabledForDeployment, enabledForDiskEncryption, enabledForTemplateDeployment, enableRbacAuthorization, premium sku, softDeleteRetentionInDays, tags. Missing tenantId or sku => 400 (verify). T2 Retention cannot be changed after create (verify). Defaults: soft delete on, retention 90. G2-T89 Get, list and delete. GET => 200; missing => 404 ResourceNotFound; list by RG and by subscription include all; DELETE existing => 200; DELETE missing => 204 (verify). T1 The spec lists 200 or 204 for delete, never 404. G2-T90 Update each property with PATCH. PATCH vaults/{n} => 200; each property from T88 changes; others unchanged. T2 PatchMerge. Array handling for accessPolicies under PATCH is (verify). G2-T91 Deleted vault lifecycle. After DELETE, GET locations/{l}/deletedVaults/{n} => 200 and list includes it; POST .../purge => 200 and the entry is gone; PUT with createMode=recover => 200 or 201 and the vault is readable again. docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T93 Deleted secrets. GET /deletedsecrets => 200, value: [] when empty and all deleted names otherwise; POST /deletedsecrets/{n}/recover => 200 and GET /secrets/{n} works again and the deleted list no longer holds it; DELETE /deletedsecrets/{n} (purge) => 204 and it is gone. T2 bespoke List and recover are missing today. G2-N12 new: secret versions and attribute updates. A second PUT /secrets/{n} creates a new version; GET /secrets/{n}/versions lists both; PATCH /secrets/{n}/{version} updates attributes without creating a version. T2 bespoke new. Also fixes the persistence shape (handler.go:574).

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T94 Create RSA and EC keys. POST /keys/{n}/create {kty: RSA} or {kty: EC, crv} => 200 bundle with key.kid, kty, n and e (RSA) or crv, x, y (EC); a requested key_size is honoured. T2 bespoke Go crypto/rsa and crypto/ecdsa. Supported sizes and curves (verify). G2-T95 Delete then recover a key. DELETE /keys/{n} => 200 with recoveryId; POST /deletedkeys/{n}/recover => 200; GET /keys/{n} => 200; the name is absent from GET /deletedkeys after recovery. T2 bespoke A deleted key reads as 404 KeyNotFound (verify). G2-T96 Rotation policy round trip. PUT /keys/{n}/rotationpolicy with lifetimeActions and attributes.expiryTime => 200; GET returns the same. T2 bespoke Default policy when none is set (verify). G2-T97 Random bytes. POST /rng {count} => 200; value is base64url of count bytes. T2 bespoke Real support may be limited to Managed HSM (verify). Do not build without confirming. G2-T98 Encrypt and decrypt. POST /keys/{n}/{v}/encrypt and .../decrypt with RSA-OAEP-256 and RSA1_5 => 200; decrypting the ciphertext returns the original. T2 bespoke Payloads are base64url without padding. The version segment may be optional (verify). G2-T99 Wrap and unwrap. POST .../wrapkey and .../unwrapkey with RSA-OAEP-256 => 200; round trip returns the original key bytes. T2 bespoke

docs.title: Certificates
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T101 Create or import a certificate. POST /certificates/{n}/create => 202 with an in-progress operation; GET /certificates/{n}/pending => status then completed; GET /certificates/{n} => 200 with id, kid, sid, x5t, cer; versions list; pending can be deleted; merge completes an externally signed request. T2 bespoke Go crypto/x509 self-signed. Create answering 202 is (verify). G2-T102 azurerm azurerm_key_vault_certificate. Apply and destroy succeed; secret_id contains the name; thumbprint and version are non-empty. T3 Needs T101. New fixture.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A DELETE on a missing resource is never 404 in ARM. Use 204.
  • PUT on a vault: 201 on create, 200 on replace. The spec marks create as long-running; sync-only returns the final state with no async headers.
  • Vault names are globally unique (they form the host {name}.vault.azure.net), and soft-deleted names still count as taken.
  • enableSoftDelete cannot be turned off, and enablePurgeProtection cannot be turned off once on. Real Azure leaves purge protection unset unless requested, while miniblue writes false (handler.go:218) (verify).
  • Do not persist data-plane objects as Go structs; round trips through a JSON-backed store lose them.
  • Key and certificate payloads use base64url without padding.
  • Real Azure does not return a name-check reason outside AccountNameInvalid and AlreadyExists.
  • A data-plane host is the vault host, not the ARM host; tests must resolve {name}.vault.azure.net to miniblue.
  • Access policy changes go through PUT .../accessPolicies/{add|remove|replace} (200 or 201 in the spec); no other verb is defined for them.

docs.title: Dropped
docs.text: ID Reason G2-T100 Key release returns an attestation-bound token. Needs an attestation service; out of scope. G2-T104 Data-plane authorization (RBAC versus access policy enforcement). miniblue has no authorization enforcement; the Authorizer seam is metadata only.

docs.title: Load Balancer
docs.text:
Engine fit: passthrough (all Microsoft.Network/loadBalancers types). miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/loadbalancer, already a superset of what the engine needs (full CRUD, three child types, list by subscription). Suggested wave: wave 4 (PLAN phase 4). Until then only the small additions below are worth doing.

miniblue is ahead of the source inventory here. The source scenarios are mostly covered by tests/loadbalancer_test.go (lifecycle, not found, defaults, multiple, and per-child lifecycle, defaults and not found for pools, probes and rules). This page records the remainder.

docs.title: Types
docs.text: Resource type api-versions seen (real latest (verify)) Scopes Children Non-CRUD ops Engine fit Needs (ADR seams) Value Effort Microsoft.Network/loadBalancers up to 2026-03-01 in the Network spec dir; tests use 2023-09-01 RG; list by subscription backendAddressPools, probes, loadBalancingRules (all present); frontendIPConfigurations (read-only, derived from properties), inboundNatRules, inboundNatPools, outboundRules (not present) none in scope passthrough PatchMode tags (real PATCH is a tags update (verify)), ListSubscription (PLAN 1.2), Request.Current for stable resourceGuid, RG existence L S loadBalancers/{backendAddressPools,probes,loadBalancingRules} same child none none passthrough parent existence (ParentResourceNotFound) L S

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value. Only the first group is worth doing before the wave 4 migration.

  • No PATCH on a load balancer (internal/services/loadbalancer/handler.go:23-57, route table). Real PATCH updates tags only.
  • resourceGuid is regenerated on every PUT (handler.go:156; children at handler.go:188, handler.go:219, handler.go:238). It must stay stable for the life of the resource.
  • DELETE returns a bare 202 with no operation headers (handler.go:311). A client that polls the LRO has nothing to follow. Sync-only (ADR-0006) wants 200 when it existed and 204 when it did not. The existing TestLoadBalancerDeleteNotFound asserts 404 for a missing load balancer and will flip to 204.
  • Default location is eastus (handler.go:131-134) instead of requiring location or taking it from the resource group.
  • Default sku is Standard / Regional when none is sent (handler.go:136-139); real Azure applies Basic when the field is omitted on older versions (verify).
  • No RG-exists check on PUT.
  • Inline arrays on the load balancer body (backendAddressPools, probes, loadBalancingRules) and the child routes are not kept in sync, so a rule added through the child route is invisible in the parent GET.
  • No azurerm or azapi fixture for a load balancer (tests/terraform/azurerm/network/main.tf has none).

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T106 Create, get, delete, list by RG, list by subscription, update tags. PUT => 201 on create, 200 on replace; GET => 200; PATCH {tags} => 200 and tags persist on the next GET; list by subscription includes every load balancer; DELETE => 200 then GET => 404 ResourceNotFound. T2 Extend tests/loadbalancer_test.go. New work is PATCH and the DELETE status. List by subscription already exists (handler.go:57). G2-T107 azurerm and azapi create a basic-SKU load balancer. Apply and destroy succeed; sku Basic; tags preserved across a no-op re-apply. T3 New fixture; none exists today. Which child reads azurerm issues after create is (verify). G2-T108 Show returns every property. GET body carries frontendIPConfigurations, backendAddressPools, loadBalancingRules, probes and inboundNatRules as configured, with stable ids and resourceGuid. T2 Needs the inline and child sync, plus inboundNatRules support (worth adding is (verify)).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A real PATCH on a load balancer changes tags only. Treat any other body field as ignored or rejected (verify); do not run a generic deep merge.
  • resourceGuid is assigned once. Regenerating on PUT breaks diff checks in azurerm.
  • A bare 202 with no Location or Azure-AsyncOperation header is a polling trap; return 200 or 204 synchronously.
  • Real DELETE on a missing load balancer returns 204 in ARM, not 404.
  • PUT on an existing load balancer returns 200, not 201.
  • A child with a missing parent load balancer is 404 ParentResourceNotFound, not ResourceNotFound.
  • A missing or malformed api-version is 400; any well-formed version is accepted.

docs.title: Log Analytics
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks for workspaces; passthrough for deletedWorkspaces; bespoke for the ingestion and query data planes; sharedKeys is an engine-gap until Type.Actions lands. miniblue today: none (no internal/services/operationalinsights; Microsoft.OperationalInsights is not in supportedProviders, internal/services/subscriptions/handler.go:94-112). Suggested wave: new type after G2, in the same PR as Insights.

Workspace-based Application Insights components point at a workspace by resource id, so common azurerm modules need both. Ship workspaces first; the Insights page depends on it (its workspace-link and azurerm scenarios).

Scope: the ARM workspaces type, deletedWorkspaces, and a thin bespoke data plane. Tables, saved searches, linked services, data sources, solutions and clusters are out of scope and have no scenario ids.

docs.text: Resource type api-versions seen (real latest (verify)) Scopes Children Non-CRUD ops Engine fit Needs (ADR seams) Value Effort Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces 2026-03-01, 2025-07-01, 2025-02-01 (spec dirs; which azurerm pins is (verify)) RG; list by subscription tables, linkedServices, dataSources, savedSearches (not scoped) POST sharedKeys and getSharedKeys (verify) hooks Defaults with Request.Current (stable customerId), PatchMode merge (retentionInDays, tags), ListSubscription (PLAN 1.2), RG existence, Provisioned, Type.Actions for sharedKeys H S Microsoft.OperationalInsights/deletedWorkspaces same subscription; RG (verify) none none passthrough none L S Ingestion POST /api/logs (data plane) n/a workspace host none Log-Type header selects the custom table bespoke none (not ARM, stays chi) L S Query POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/query (data plane) v1 workspace id or resource id none KQL subset bespoke none (not ARM, stays chi) M L

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
• No service at all: no workspaces, no data plane, no provider registration entry (internal/services/subscriptions/handler.go:94-112).
  • customerId (the workspace GUID) must be generated once and stay stable across PUT; Request.Current makes that a Defaults hook job.
  • sharedKeys has no home yet. azurerm reads the shared keys after create to fill primary_shared_key; whether it tolerates a missing endpoint is (verify). The engine resource-action seam (Type.Actions) lands with the first listKeys consumer (redis, wave 2). Until then a chi route is the fallback.
  • List by subscription depends on the engine seam in PLAN 1.2.
  • Ingestion is trivial (accept and acknowledge). Query is the expensive part and should stay a small KQL subset.

docs.title: workspaces
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T77 Create a workspace with defaults. PUT workspaces/{n} => 201; properties.customerId is a GUID; provisioningState Succeeded; sku.name PerGB2018; retentionInDays 30. T2 Real PUT is long-running; sync-only returns the final state. The default retention of 30 for PerGB2018 is (verify). G2-T78 customerId survives updates. Repeat PUT with changed tags => 200; customerId identical to the first response. PATCH body {properties:{retentionInDays}} => 200 and next GET shows it; PATCH body {tags} => 200 and tags updated; untouched properties unchanged. T2 PatchMerge. Retention bounds are (verify). G2-T81 azurerm create and destroy azurerm_log_analytics_workspace. Apply and destroy succeed; workspace_id equals customerId; sku and retention_in_days as set. T3 New fixture. POST workspaces/{n}/sharedKeys => 200 with primarySharedKey and secondarySharedKey; values identical across calls. T2 new. Needs Type.Actions. Exact path and verb (sharedKeys versus getSharedKeys) (verify).

docs.title: deletedWorkspaces
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T84 List soft-deleted workspaces in a subscription. GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.OperationalInsights/deletedWorkspaces => 200 {value: []} on a clean subscription. T2 If soft delete is modelled, a deleted workspace appears here (verify).

docs.title: Data plane (bespoke)
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T82 Post custom log records (one record, many records, several Log-Type values). POST /api/logs with a Log-Type header => 200, empty body. T2 bespoke The real call needs a SharedKey signature and x-ms-date; an emulator can skip validation (verify). Missing Log-Type is a 400 (verify). G2-T83 Query a workspace. POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/query => 200; tables[0].name == "PrimaryResult"; custom-table rows come back through take, where, project, summarize count; workspace() resolves by customerId or resource id; union works. Standard tables such as AzureActivity and AzureDiagnostics return an empty table. T2 bespoke Unknown table is a 400 semantic error in real Azure (verify). Start with take, where, count.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• customerId is assigned once. Regenerating it on update breaks every consumer that stored the workspace id.
  • Defaults differ by product: workspaces default to 30 days retention, Application Insights components to 90 (verify). Do not share a constant.
  • A workspace id in query paths can be the customerId GUID or a full resource id; accept both.
  • A query for a table that does not exist is an error in real Azure, not an empty result (verify). Standard tables that exist in every workspace return empty.
  • A real PUT on an existing workspace returns 200; 201 only on create.
  • A missing or malformed api-version is 400; any well-formed version is accepted.
  • Real Azure serves sharedKeys as a POST. A GET on that path is not the real contract (verify).
  • The HTTP Data Collector API (/api/logs) is being retired by the real service (verify); keep it minimal.

docs.title: Managed Identity
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks for userAssignedIdentities; passthrough child plus Validate for federatedIdentityCredentials; bespoke for identities/default. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/identity (user-assigned identities by RG only: PUT, GET, PATCH tags, DELETE, list by RG). Suggested wave: wave 2 for the user-assigned identity ARM type (PLAN phase 4); federatedIdentityCredentials as a new type after G2 (cheap-win bundle).

Spec facts used below are confirmed against the msi stable spec 2024-11-30 (earlier stable versions 2023-01-31 and 2018-11-30). tenantId, principalId and clientId are read-only. properties.isolationScope is None or Regional. Federated credential names match ^[a-zA-Z0-9]{1}[a-zA-Z0-9-_]{2,119}$; issuer (a URI), subject and audiences are required.

docs.title: Types
docs.text: Resource type api-versions seen (real latest (verify)) Scopes Children Non-CRUD ops Engine fit Needs (ADR seams) Value Effort Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities 2024-11-30, 2023-01-31, 2018-11-30 RG; list by subscription federatedIdentityCredentials POST listAssociatedResources (verify) hooks Defaults with Request.Current (stable principalId, clientId, tenantId), PatchMode merge (PATCH is a full update in the spec), ListSubscription (PLAN 1.2), RG existence L S userAssignedIdentities/federatedIdentityCredentials 2024-11-30, 2023-01-31 child of identities none none passthrough child + Validate parent existence (ParentResourceNotFound), Validate (name pattern, required issuer, subject, audiences) H S {scope}/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/identities/default 2018-11-30 any resource scope none GET only bespoke reads the identity block of the resource at {scope}; no engine seam for a cross-type read (verify) M S

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • No federatedIdentityCredentials. No routes, store or tests. This is the cheap high-value addition (workload identity setups in Terraform use it).
  • No list by subscription (internal/services/identity/handler.go, list is by RG only). Depends on PLAN 1.2.
  • No identities/default. It also needs other services to expose an identity block on their resources.
  • DELETE answers 204 on success and 404 on a missing identity (handler.go:173-185). Real Azure answers 200 when the identity existed and 204 when it did not, and never 404 (verify).
  • PUT does its RG check through the legacy rg: key (handler.go:73) and returns 404 ResourceGroupNotFound; the engine check supersedes it.
  • principalId and clientId are derived deterministically from the resource id (deterministicUUID, handler.go:99-100), and tenantId is a constant (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001). Derivation keeps them stable across PUT, but delete and recreate yields the same ids; real Azure issues new ones.
  • PATCH updates tags only (handler.go:126); isolationScope is not modelled. PUT replaces tags wholesale.
  • Existing coverage: internal/services/identity/handler_test.go (TestUpdateIdentityDoesNotMutatePublishedRecord, TestUserAssignedIdentityLifecycleAndPatchTags) and the azurerm fixture tests/terraform/azurerm/identity-rbac/main.tf (an identity plus role assignments). No federated credential fixture.

docs.title: userAssignedIdentities
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T109 Create an identity. PUT userAssignedIdentities/{n} => 201; properties.principalId, clientId and tenantId are GUIDs; location and type as sent. T2 Already covered by the existing handler tests; port to an armtest Sample row. Assert GUID shape only, not the tenant value. G2-T110 Create in a missing resource group. PUT => 404 ResourceGroupNotFound. T1 Engine RG existence check. Already covered. G2-T111 Repeat the same PUT. Second PUT => 200 (not 201); principalId and clientId unchanged. T1 G2-T112 Tags at create and on PATCH. PUT with tags => 201 and tags stored; PATCH {tags} => 200 and tags updated; other properties unchanged. T1 Whether PATCH replaces or merges the tag set is (verify); PatchMerge merges key by key. G2-T113 List by RG and by subscription. GET .../resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities => 200 with only that group's identities; GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities => 200 with all. T1 Subscription list is new; needs ListSubscription (PLAN 1.2). G2-T114 Two identities are distinct. principalId and clientId differ between identities. T2 Derive from the resource id (distinct inputs, distinct outputs). G2-T120 azurerm and azapi create and destroy an identity; add a federated credential. Apply and destroy succeed; tags preserved; azurerm_federated_identity_credential (new) applies, reads back issuer, subject, audience, and destroys. T3 Extend tests/terraform/azurerm/identity-rbac/main.tf; add an azapi variant. The federated credential part is new and needs the FIC scenarios first. G2-N13 new: delete an identity. DELETE existing => 200 then GET => 404 ResourceNotFound; DELETE again => 204. T1 new. Today answers 204 then 404 (handler.go:173-185). G2-N14 new: isolation scope. PUT with properties.isolationScope Regional => 201 and GET returns it; omitted behaves as None (verify). T2 new. Spec enum confirmed (None, Regional); default is (verify).

PUT .../federatedIdentityCredentials/{n} => 201; update => 200; GET round-trips properties.issuer, subject, audiences; list shows it; DELETE => 200 then GET => 404. T2 Passthrough child. A body is required. Name pattern is enforced by Validate. G2-T117 Missing parent identity, missing credential. PUT or GET of a credential under a missing identity => 404 (ParentResourceNotFound per the engine rule; the real provider may return ResourceNotFound (verify)); GET of a missing credential => 404 ResourceNotFound. docs.title: identities/default
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T119 Read the system-assigned identity of a resource. GET {scope}/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/identities/default on a resource with no system identity => 404 IdentityNotFound (verify); with one => 200, location present, principalId and tenantId matching the resource's identity block. T2 bespoke Bespoke: depends on other services' identity blocks.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• principalId and clientId are stable for the life of the identity, and different after delete and recreate. A deterministic derivation from the resource id gets the first and not the second.
  • Real DELETE is 200 when the resource existed and 204 when it did not. It never returns 404.
  • The not-found code for a missing parent is ParentResourceNotFound in the engine and ResourceNotFound for the resource itself. A per-service code such as ManagedIdentityNotFound is not a real ARM code.
  • PUT is 201 on create and 200 on replace.
  • A missing identity named in another resource's identity.userAssignedIdentities is rejected or echoed by real Azure (verify); decide once and test it where the consumer lives.
  • Missing or malformed api-version is 400; any well-formed version is accepted.
  • A federated credential's audiences is an array (azurerm exposes it as audience); issuer must be a valid HTTPS URI (verify).

docs.title: Management Groups
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks plus engine-gap for managementGroups (typed errors, GET and DELETE hooks, a hierarchy index, cross-resource effects), passthrough for settings, bespoke for subscriptions, descendants, getEntities and checkNameAvailability. miniblue today: none (no Microsoft.Management registration, no root group). internal/arm already parses management group ids, and internal/services/policy registers policyDefinitions at subscription scope only. Suggested wave: new type after G2 (SPIKE rank 3); the policy scope-mask change can ship earlier on its own.

Sync-only is the rule (ADR-0006), and real management group PUT and DELETE are long-running. The chosen miniblue behaviour is stated under Pitfalls and flagged in the affected rows.

In the tables below, MG is /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Latest stable api-version is 2023-04-01 (confirmed in the REST spec repo). Older stable versions are 2019-11-01, 2020-02-01, 2020-05-01, 2020-10-01 and 2021-04-01; the latest preview is 2024-02-01-preview. azurerm and azapi pins were not checked (verify). APIVersions is metadata only (ADR-0005), so any well-formed version is accepted.

Resource type api-versions seen (real latest (verify)) Scopes Children Non-CRUD ops Engine fit Needs (ADR seams) Value Effort Microsoft.Management/managementGroups 2023-04-01 tenant (Scopes: arm.ScopeTenant) subscriptions, settings GET {g}/descendants; GET {g} with $expand (children, path, ancestors), $recurse, $filter hooks, engine-gap azerr.Error typed errors; GET hook (computed details.parent, $expand); DELETE hook (refuse when children exist); PatchMode merge with flat body; Request.Current; hierarchy index over the store (children, recursive descendants); root bootstrap H M managementGroups/subscriptions (association) 2023-04-01 child of managementGroups none GET {g}/subscriptions (list, later) bespoke cross-resource effect: a PUT moves the subscription out of any other group; computed properties from the subscriptions service H M managementGroups/settings (singleton default) 2023-04-01 child of managementGroups none GET {g}/settings list passthrough Hooks.Validate (name must be default) L S MG/{g}/descendants 2023-04-01 read-only none GET with $top, $skiptoken bespoke (chi route beside the engine) hierarchy index M S POST /providers/Microsoft.Management/getEntities 2023-04-01 provider level none POST; $search, $filter, $view, $select, $top, $skiptoken, groupName bespoke (provider-level chi route, allowed by ADR-0001) hierarchy index M S POST /providers/Microsoft.Management/checkNameAvailability 2023-04-01 provider level none POST body {name, type} bespoke (provider-level, ADR-0001) name rule shared with Validate (CheckName, ADR-0003) L S Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions at MG scope 2023-04-01 (policy) adds MG (and tenant for built-ins) none none passthrough scope mask only: add arm.ScopeManagementGroup to Scopes M S Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments at MG scope per Slice 1 includes MG none none passthrough Slice 1 scope mask; transitive ancestry only if RBAC is enforced at MG scope M S Microsoft.Resources/deployments at MG scope per deployments MG none validate, cancel, whatIf bespoke (deployments owner) owned by the deployments page M M operations, startTenantBackfill, tenantBackfillStatus 2023-04-01 provider level none static list; backfill pair bespoke no scenario in the source; static responses only if a client asks L S

Phasing inside the type (M overall, L including the engine primitives):

  1. Group CRUD, list, $expand=children, the name rule, the root group. Effort M.
  2. Subscription association with move semantics, descendants, root auto-placement, getEntities. Effort M.
  3. Settings, checkNameAvailability, the policy scope mask. Effort S.
  4. Later: $expand=path|ancestors, $recurse, $filter, GET {g}/subscriptions, a cycle check on reparent (the cycle check should land in phase 1 if reparent ships there).

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • No management group service exists. Microsoft.Management is unregistered, so every MG/... path 404s. ROADMAP.md:22 lists it as "Medium: hierarchy, subscription assignment".
  • No root group and no hierarchy. The tenant id used by the subscriptions service is 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 (internal/services/subscriptions/handler.go:56-57), so the root group is named by that id with display name "Tenant Root Group".
  • The subscriptions service serves one static subscription (internal/services/subscriptions/handler.go:83-92) and has no creation callback. Root auto-placement is cheapest derived at read time: a subscription with no association record is a child of the root group. That avoids a cross-service hook.
  • arm.ID parses management group ids and classifies MG-scoped resources as ScopeManagementGroup (internal/arm/id.go, covered by internal/arm/id_test.go). The Parent() of a management group is the tenant, not the parent group, so any ancestry walk (RBAC, policy inheritance) needs a resolver over the hierarchy.
  • policyDefinitions is registered at subscription scope only (internal/services/policy/policy.go:13). TestPolicyDefinitionOnlyAtSubscriptionScope (tests/arm_policydefinition_test.go:78) pins the MG-scope PUT to 404 today, so the scope-mask change must flip that assertion.
  • The engine already does CRUD at MG scope for extension resources: TestEngineCRUDAtEveryScope (internal/arm/engine_test.go:82-86) puts a resource under a group that was never created. Per ADR-0003, extension resources at MG scope are not existence-checked, so writes under a missing group succeed until the MG type supplies an existence check.
  • No getEntities, descendants, checkNameAvailability or settings routes.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text: Status codes follow ADR-0006 (sync): PUT 201 on create and 200 on replace, DELETE 200 if it existed and 204 if missing, PATCH 200. Tests that also run against real Azure must accept the LRO forms (see Pitfalls).

PUT MG/{g} with a 91-character name, a leading -, a trailing ., a space, or / => 400; a-b_c.(d) => 201 T2 new (real API only). Implement in Hooks.Validate with CheckName (ADR-0003); error code is (verify). Blocking only path-traversal characters is not enough. Unit-test the regexp in internal/arm. G2-T30 checkNameAvailability reports whether a name can be used. POST /providers/Microsoft.Management/checkNameAvailability body {name, type:"Microsoft.Management/managementGroups"} => 200 {nameAvailable, reason, message}; reason is Invalid for a rule violation and AlreadyExists for a name in use T2 new (spec 2023-04-01). Provider-level chi route (ADR-0001). Reuse the G2-T29 rule. A wrong type is Invalid (verify).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Real PUT (200 or 202, status: NotStarted in the 202 body) and DELETE (202 with a Location header, or 204) on a group are long-running. ADR-0006 is sync-only, so miniblue returns 201 or 200 on PUT and 200 or 204 on DELETE, with no async headers. SDK pollers and az accept a synchronous terminal response. A suite that also runs against real Azure must accept 200, 201, 202 and 204 and poll the Location header.
  • getEntities is POST in real Azure. Asserting GET would be wrong.
  • The PATCH body is flat (displayName, parentGroupId). Wrapping it in properties is wrong. PUT uses properties.displayName and properties.details.parent.id.
  • "Has children" is an exact match on the stored parent id. A prefix or suffix match wrongly counts mg1-eu or mg10 as children of mg1.
  • Reparenting needs a cycle check (a group cannot move under its own descendant).
  • Ids are case-insensitive. Look up by the normalised id and return canonical casing; two groups differing only in case are one group.
  • Validating only path-traversal characters in names accepts names that real Azure rejects (the rule in G2-T29).
  • The root group id is the tenant id, GET MG includes it, and it cannot be deleted or reparented (verify).
  • A subscription belongs to exactly one group. Association PUT is a move, not an add. Removing the association re-homes the subscription (verify).
  • Real Azure rejects an association for a subscription that does not exist (verify). miniblue's subscriptions service echoes any id today (internal/services/subscriptions/handler.go:83-92), so a check would either always pass or reject all but the static subscription. Decide the behaviour and note it in the PR.
  • Settings PUT replaces and PATCH merges; settings DELETE returns 200 (not 204).
  • Extension resources at MG scope are not existence-checked (ADR-0003). Role, policy and deployment writes under a non-existent group succeed until a group existence check is added.
  • RBAC at MG scope needs a transitive ancestry walk over the hierarchy. The Parent() of a management group id is the tenant, not its parent group.
  • Policy at MG scope is only a scope-mask change because miniblue does not evaluate policy. If evaluation is ever added, inheritance down the hierarchy becomes part of the work.

docs.title: Redis
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks for redis plus Type.Actions for listKeys and regenerateKey; passthrough child for firewallRules. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/redis (PUT, GET, DELETE, list by RG, static listKeys); PUT ignores the request body, see below. Suggested wave: wave 2 (PLAN phase 4); firewallRules as a new type after G2.

Scope: the ARM control plane only. The RESP data plane is not ARM; miniblue proxies connectivity to a real Redis through REDIS_URL and does not implement the protocol.

Spec facts used below are confirmed in the Microsoft.Cache stable spec (latest 2024-11-01, then 2024-03-01): create is a PUT (200 or 201, long-running); PATCH is 200 or 202; DELETE is 200, 202 or 204; list exists by RG and by subscription; the create body requires location and properties.sku with name, family and capacity; sku name is Basic, Standard or Premium; family is C or P; capacity is 0 to 6 for C and 1 to 4 for P; enableNonSslPort defaults to false; minimumTlsVersion is 1.0, 1.1 or 1.2; publicNetworkAccess is Enabled or Disabled; accessKeys appear only on create and update responses; POST listKeys returns primaryKey and secondaryKey; POST regenerateKey takes {keyType: Primary|Secondary}; firewallRules require properties.startIP and endIP.

Path casing for the provider-level name check is (verify).

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • PUT ignores the request body. CreateOrUpdateCache (internal/services/redis/handler.go:99-126) never reads r.Body. buildCacheResponse (handler.go:69-97) hard-codes location eastus, sku Basic / C1, enableNonSslPort true, redisVersion 7.2 and publicNetworkAccess Enabled, and drops tags. Everything the client sends is lost, so azurerm shows permanent drift.
  • hostName is not the cache's. redisHostPort (handler.go:40) yields the REDIS_URL host or localhost, not {name}.redis.cache.windows.net. Derive it from the cache name; keep the REDIS_URL target as the proxy destination.
  • listKeys returns static keys (miniblue-redis-key and -2, handler.go:160-174); there is no regenerateKey.
  • No firewallRules, no PATCH, no list by subscription, no RG-exists check.
  • DELETE answers 200 and 404 on a missing cache (handler.go:141-151); real Azure answers 200 when it existed and 204 when it did not.
  • Connectivity check. When REDIS_URL is set and unreachable, PUT returns 503 RedisUnreachable (handler.go:104-113). Keep this as an opt-in Validate hook, not a default.
  • No tests. The route table is at handler.go:24-34. No file under tests exercises Microsoft.Cache redis (the only match is an unrelated VM identity test).

PUT redis/{n} => 201; properties.hostName contains the cache name; port 6379; sslPort 6380; provisioningState Succeeded; sku, tags and location echo the request. T2 Fails today: body ignored. Fix first; T127 depends on it. G2-N15 new: required body fields. PUT without location, or without properties.sku, or with a sku name outside Basic, Standard, Premium => 400. T2 new. GET => 200; PATCH {tags} => 200 with tags updated; DELETE => 200 then GET => 404 ResourceNotFound; list by RG and by subscription include every cache. POST listKeys => 200 with primaryKey and secondaryKey, identical across calls; POST regenerateKey {keyType: Primary} => 200 and only the primary changes; Secondary changes only the secondary. TLS is reflected, not enforced. G2-T128 az CLI create, show, delete, list, list-keys, regenerate-keys. Equivalent REST calls succeed with the same shapes as T121 to T123. docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G2-T124 Rule lifecycle. PUT redis/{c}/firewallRules/{r} => 201; update the range => 200; GET round-trips properties.startIP and endIP; DELETE => 200 then GET => 404; list shows current rules. T2 Passthrough child. G2-T125 Invalid rule body. PUT without properties, or with a blank startIP or endIP => 400 InvalidRequestContent (verify). T2 Spec marks both IPs required. G2-T126 Rule under a missing cache. PUT or GET => 404 ParentResourceNotFound (engine rule); the real provider may return ResourceNotFound (verify). T1 Engine parent-exists check.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• enableNonSslPort defaults to false in the spec; a hard-coded true makes azurerm report drift on every plan.
  • The create body requires location and the full sku triple; a missing one is a 400, not a silently applied default.
  • Real DELETE returns 200 when the cache existed and 204 when it did not; a 404 on a missing cache is wrong.
  • PUT is 201 on create and 200 on replace.
  • Access keys appear in the create response and in listKeys only; a plain GET does not return them.
  • Keys must be stable across listKeys calls and change only on regenerateKey, and only the targeted key.
  • A child (firewallRules) with a missing parent is 404 ParentResourceNotFound in the engine; the real code may differ (verify).
  • A missing or malformed api-version is 400; any well-formed version is accepted.
  • hostName and sslPort are what clients dial. If they are not reachable, azurerm succeeds but applications fail.

docs.title: Resource groups
docs.text:
Engine fit: bespoke today (cascade across legacy services); hooks once served by the engine, with Validate for name and location rules and a DELETE-missing override. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/resourcegroups. Suggested wave: PLAN 3.3 (refactor(resourcegroups): serve resource groups via arm engine), preceded by PLAN 0.6 (cascade via scope cleaners) and PLAN 1.2 (Engine.DeleteScope).

Resource groups are the parent scope for every RG-scoped type, so their behaviour is shared by all other catalogue pages. The delete-cascade scenario is the acceptance test for every type that migrates (ADR-0004 scope cleaners, ADR-0007 recipe step 6).

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Resource type api-versions seen (real latest (verify)) Scopes Children Non-CRUD ops Engine fit Needs (ADR seams) Value Effort Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups any well-formed version; spec repo has 2024-11-01, 2025-03-01, 2025-04-01 (latest (verify)) subscription every RG-scoped type HEAD existence (204/404); PATCH; list; POST exportTemplate (200/202); POST moveResources and validateMoveResources (202/204, out of scope) bespoke now; hooks after PLAN 3.3 Hooks.Validate (name pattern, location immutability), DELETE-missing 404 override (ADR-0006 default is 204), ScopeExists native, Engine.DeleteScope plus cleaners, store.SchemaVersion bump H M GET /subscriptions/{s}/resourcegroups/{rg}/resources (and GET /subscriptions/{s}/resources) same subscription, RG none $filter, $expand (createdTime, changedTime, provisioningState), $top engine-gap prefix-scan list across engine types plus subscription-wide list (PLAN 1.2); legacy types stay invisible until they migrate M S

Real resource group facts (confirmed in the REST spec, api-version 2025-04-01):

  • Name is 1 to 90 characters matching ^[-\w\._\(\)]+$, case-insensitive.
  • Body is a tracked resource (location required on PUT) plus managedBy and properties.provisioningState.
  • PUT returns 200 or 201, PATCH 200, HEAD 204 or 404, DELETE 200 or 202 (the spec lists no 204).
  • DELETE takes an optional forceDeletionTypes query parameter. Deleting a group deletes its deployments and their stored operations.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • Cascade is incomplete and hard-coded. handler.go:141-205 is a literal DeleteByPrefix list that imports aks and vm for cleanup. Missing: the deployment: prefix (deployments survive RG deletion, real Azure removes them), keyvault, and every arm: engine key (index finding 6). The engine keys are covered by PLAN 1.2 DeleteScope; the keyvault cleaner by PLAN 0.6.
  • /resources always returns an empty list (handler.go:215). Real Azure lists every resource in the group with id, name, type, location, tags. This breaks az resource list, terraform data sources and any "is the RG empty" check. PLAN 3.3 serves it from the engine.
  • DELETE is async-shaped. Existing RG returns 202 with a Location to operationresults/delete-rg-{name} (handler.go:197-204), and the operation result returns a bare 200 (handler.go:221). PLAN 3.3 makes DELETE synchronous 200 and drops operationresults. Tests must accept 200 and 202 until then.
  • PATCH panics after a persisted restart. handler.go:105 type-asserts the stored value to ResourceGroup; a value reloaded from the persistence backend is a map, not the struct (index finding 1). Fixed by the engine's uniform JSON storage (ADR-0004).
  • No validation on PUT. No name pattern or length check, no location immutability check, no subscription check. location is required (400 InvalidRequestContent).
  • GET and DELETE on a missing RG return ResourceNotFound, not ResourceGroupNotFound (verify). tests/resourcegroups_test.go asserts the current code; update it with the migration.
  • tags is omitted when empty (omitempty at handler.go:20), and there is no managedBy.
  • PATCH only handles tags. managedBy and properties are ignored.
  • Existing coverage: tests/resourcegroups_test.go (create, duplicate, PATCH tags, not found, HEAD, vnet-only delete cascade, missing location) and tests/cascade_test.go (all legacy services plus a cross-RG VM case).

A second identical PUT is an update. PUT => 201 then PUT => 200; GET => 200 T1/T2 Tags on a tagless RG: real Azure omits tags (verify); accept absent or {} and reject null. Add managedBy round-trip. Covered in part by tests/resourcegroups_test.go. G3-T2 PATCH sets tags (env=prod, team=platform). Tags persist on GET and location is unchanged. PATCH on a missing RG fails. PATCH => 200, tags set, location unchanged; PATCH missing => 404 ResourceGroupNotFound T2 Whether PATCH replaces or merges the tag map is (verify); pick one and assert it (PatchMode). Today's missing-RG code is ResourceNotFound. G3-T3 PUT an existing RG with no tags replaces the tag map with an empty one. PUT => 200, tags empty or absent T2 PUT is replace, not merge. Counterpart to T2. G3-T4 List returns exactly the N groups created (rg1..rg3) and none belonging to another subscription. GET /subscriptions/{s}/resourcegroups => 200, value has N items T2 Assert as a set: real Azure gives no ordering guarantee. The cross-subscription half needs a second subscription and is conditional on a subscription store (see Subscriptions and providers). G3-T5 DELETE a missing RG fails; DELETE an existing RG succeeds and the RG is then gone. missing => 404 ResourceGroupNotFound (verify); existing => 202 + Location today, 200 after PLAN 3.3; subsequent GET => 404 T2 Spec allows 200 or 202 and no 204. Accept both until PLAN 3.3. azurerm tolerance of a synchronous 200 is (verify). Covered, spot check only. G3-T7 PUT an RG in a subscription that does not exist fails. 404 SubscriptionNotFound (verify) T2 Conditional: only meaningful once a subscription store exists. With one fixed subscription the engine never sees an unknown id. G3-T8 PUT that changes location of an existing RG fails. PUT with an invalid location fails. 4xx InvalidResourceGroupLocation (verify status; message says the group already exists in another location); invalid location => 400 (verify) T1/T2 Hooks.Validate using Request.Current. Location compare is case-insensitive and ignores spaces (verify).

docs.title: Delete cascade
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T6 Cascade matrix. Create a storage account with a blob container, a SQL server with a database and firewall rule, a Service Bus namespace with queue, topic, subscription and rule, a VNet with subnet and peering, an availability set, and a deployment. DELETE the RG. Every child GET afterwards returns not found and no list shows them. each child GET => 404 (ResourceNotFound or ResourceGroupNotFound); every list => value without the deleted items T2 Acceptance test for every migrated type (ADR-0007 step 6). Include a deployment, which is missing from the cascade today. Each new type needs a cleaner or engine DeleteScope coverage, no orphan prefix. Child types that do not exist yet (Service Bus subscriptions and rules, SQL firewall rules, VNet peerings) are skipped, not stubbed; add each row when its type lands.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• RG DELETE never returns 204 in real Azure: 200 or 202 when it existed, 404 when it did not. Asserting 204 for a missing group is wrong, and the engine's default of 204 on a missing resource (ADR-0006) needs an override for this type.
  • PUT in an unknown subscription is a 404, not a server error.
  • Location is immutable once the group exists. A PUT that changes it fails; it is not a silent update.
  • A list of resource groups has no defined order. Assert sets, never positions.
  • GET .../resources must include resources in the group regardless of which service owns them. An empty list is a visible bug, not a safe default.
  • After a restart with PERSISTENCE=1, stored values come back as generic JSON. Any handler that type-asserts a stored struct breaks (the PATCH panic above).
  • Long-running-operation pollers wait for the group to be gone. A 202 whose Location never completes hangs them; a synchronous 200 is the safe shape for a single-process emulator.

docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • No subscriptions, rules, authorizationRules, listKeys or regenerateKeys. azurerm_servicebus_subscription and azurerm_servicebus_namespace (connection strings) cannot work.
  • No ARM DELETE for subscriptions, which azurerm_servicebus_subscription destroy needs. Real Azure has it (spec: 200/204).
  • No networkRuleSets/default, no list by subscription, no PATCH.
  • Namespace responses are fixed: location eastus, hard-coded createdAt/updatedAt (handler.go:220, handler.go:230-231). Queue and topic ARM PUT also build a fixed body (handler.go:311-325), so request body properties and tags are dropped.
  • Namespace DELETE removes only data-plane keys (sb:queue:, sb:topic:) (handler.go:277-278). ARM queues and topics (sb:armqueue:, sb:armtopic:; handler.go:292, handler.go:367) survive and reappear if the namespace is recreated.
  • Namespace DELETE of an existing namespace returns 202 with no Location (handler.go:281); a missing one returns 404 (real: 204).
  • ARM queues and topics are a separate key space from the data-plane queues and topics, so an entity created over ARM is not the same object the data plane sends to.
  • The RG cascade covers sb:namespace:, sb:armqueue:, sb:armtopic: (resourcegroups/handler.go:192-194) but not data-plane keys or any new type.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Real Azure has an ARM DELETE for subscriptions (200/204). Omitting it breaks terraform destroy.
  • On the ARM surface a correlation filter uses label, not subject; timestamps are createdAt and updatedAt.
  • Entity not-found is the generic ResourceNotFound, not a per-entity code (verify).
  • Child PUTs are 200 in the spec, not 201; see the new-case row.
  • Namespace names are global, and a deleted namespace must release its name and every child (ARM and data-plane keys).
  • networkRuleSets/default must be GET-able; azurerm reads it during namespace refresh (verify for non-Premium).
  • Real namespace DELETE can be asynchronous (202); the engine is sync, so assert 200 or 204.
  • Key material appears only in listKeys and regenerateKeys responses, never in an authorization rule GET or list. listKeys is a POST.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Never return administratorLoginPassword (spec: create/update only). Strip it before the document is stored, not only on read, so dumps and logs stay clean.
  • DELETE of a missing server or database is 204, not 404. The spec lists no 404 for DELETE.
  • Real Azure may answer SQL writes and deletes with 202 plus a poll URL (long-running). The engine is sync: 201 or 200 on write, 200 or 204 on delete, no Location.
  • fullyQualifiedDomainName must be a real-looking host, not localhost; azurerm and clients build connection strings from it.
  • Server names are global across subscriptions, so the uniqueness check cannot be scoped to the RG.
  • A password supplied on a later PUT must not make the response differ from a GET.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Engine fit: bespoke for accounts and the data plane; hooks plus gaps (global-unique name, merge PATCH, post-actions) if the ARM shell migrates; passthrough child for ARM queues and tables once the account parent exists. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/storageaccounts (ARM shell) plus the Blob/Queue/Table data planes. Suggested wave: wave 4 (PLAN phase 4, storageaccounts (ARM)), optional; the data plane never migrates.

The account stays bespoke because blob shared-key authentication reads the account record directly, and because account PUT must keep returning 200 (SPIKE.md, storage ARM row). The engine's create path returns 201 then 200 (ADR-0005), so a migration would change the status code. The ARM shell is migrated only if a fidelity or enforcement need appears (ADR-0007, wave 4). Type.Actions lands with the first listKeys consumer; storage is a natural first one.

Real facts confirmed in the REST spec (api-version 2025-01-01):

  • Account name is 3 to 24 characters, ^[a-z0-9]+$ (lowercase letters and digits only).
  • PUT returns 200 or 202 (long-running); DELETE 200 or 204; PATCH 200; listKeys, regenerateKey, ListAccountSas, ListServiceSas and checkNameAvailability return 200.
  • checkNameAvailability takes {name, type} with type Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts; reason is AccountNameInvalid or AlreadyExists.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • No account PATCH. Terraform and azapi update tags and properties with PATCH or a full PUT; the PATCH route is missing.
  • PUT rebuilds the whole record. creationTime and keyCreationTime are regenerated on every PUT, and PUT always returns 200 (never 201) (buildStorageAccountResponse).
  • Unknown properties are dropped. The body properties are filtered through an allow-list of about 24 keys; anything else is not echoed back. azapi sends the properties it was given and treats a missing echo as drift.
  • Keys are derived, not stored. Keys come deterministically from subscription, resource group and account name, so there is no regenerateKey and a rotation cannot persist.
  • No checkNameAvailability, no SAS list actions (ListAccountSas, ListServiceSas), and no revokeUserDelegationKeys.
  • No validation, no uniqueness, no RG check. No name rules on PUT, no global name uniqueness, and no resource group existence check.
  • No ARM queues/{q} or tables/{t} children. Only the queueServices/default and tableServices/default property endpoints exist.
  • etag is a static W/"miniblue". Real Azure returns a changing etag; clients rarely rely on it.
  • Endpoints honour MINIBLUE_STORAGE_ENDPOINT when set.
  • ARM container CRUD and list already exist, so the container delta is small.
  • DELETE returns 200 when the account existed and 204 when it did not, and removes blob:armcontainer, managementpolicy and svcprops records.
  • Existing coverage: tests/blobarm_test.go (account CRUD, list, listKeys, container CRUD, endpoint formats, shared-key data plane, queue/table/file/blob service props), internal/services/storageaccounts/{cleanup,delete,management_policy,service_properties}_test.go, and the azurerm fixture tests/terraform/azurerm/storage/main.tf (account plus container through storage_account_id). There is no azapi storage fixture (the azapi directory holds only policy_definition).

PUT .../tableServices/default/tables/{t} and the same status set T2 Missing today. Table name rules (letters and digits, 3 to 63, starting with a letter) (verify).

docs.title: Data plane (bespoke)
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T51 Account SAS (ListAccountSas) and service SAS (ListServiceSas) tokens carry sv and sig. Using one on a blob read works. An expired token or a token without the needed permission is refused. POST .../ListAccountSas and .../ListServiceSas => 200 with a token; blob GET with the token => 200; expired => 403 AuthenticationFailed; wrong permission => 403 (verify) code T2 Bespoke. SAS signing is HMAC-SHA256 over the stored key, signed version (verify). The two control-plane POST actions are the missing piece. G3-T53 Table entity upsert and get by partition key and row key (pk1, rk1). PUT or MERGE entity => 204; GET entity => 200 with the stored properties T2 Bespoke. The Table data plane is thin today. Optional follow-up: an azurerm_storage_table_entity fixture.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Account create is long-running in real Azure: the spec lists 200 or 202 for PUT and no 201. A synchronous emulator returns 200 with provisioningState: Succeeded, which pollers treat as done (ADR-0006).
  • Account names are globally unique across all of Azure and fixed to 3 to 24 lowercase letters and digits. Uppercase is rejected, not lower-cased.
  • A PUT on an existing account is an update: creationTime, keyCreationTime and both keys must not change. Rebuilding the record on every PUT makes Terraform plans drift.
  • Do not drop properties the emulator does not model. azapi and Bicep send the full body and compare the response; a filtered echo causes a perpetual diff.
  • Keys need real state. If keys are derived from the name, regenerateKey cannot change them and the shared-key data plane cannot honour a rotation.
  • listKeys is a POST action, not a GET, and always returns two keys.
  • DELETE on a missing account is 204 (spec 200 or 204), not 404. This differs from resource groups.
  • checkNameAvailability is a subscription-level provider action, not an account sub-route; it must agree with what a later PUT accepts.
  • ARM queues and tables are separate from data-plane queues and tables in the service model, but one namespace in real Azure. Decide the shared store explicitly.
  • Shared-key signatures are over the stored key. A SAS minted from ListAccountSas must validate against the same key the data plane uses.

docs.title: Dropped
docs.text: ID Reason G3-T52 User-delegation SAS and bearer-auth blob access need Entra token validation and a user delegation key; data plane, low value, out of scope for the ARM foundation.

docs.title: Subscriptions, locations and providers
docs.text:
Engine fit: engine-gap for subscriptions and locations (singleton plus a subscription list), engine-gap for providers (provider gate, registry-derived list); no passthrough types. miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/subscriptions. Suggested wave: PLAN 3.3 (subscriptions move onto the engine alongside resource groups) and PLAN 3.4 (/providers derived from the registry).

Subscriptions are read-only in real ARM at /subscriptions/{id}. Creating, cancelling and renaming subscriptions belongs to the separate Microsoft.Subscription provider and is out of scope for a single-subscription emulator, so those scenarios are in Dropped.

docs.text:

Real facts confirmed in the REST specs:

  • Subscription carries id, subscriptionId, displayName, tenantId, state (Enabled, Warned, PastDue, Disabled, Deleted), subscriptionPolicies (locationPlacementId, quotaId, spendingLimit), authorizationSource, managedByTenants, tags.
  • Location carries id, subscriptionId, name, type, displayName, regionalDisplayName, metadata, availabilityZoneMappings.
  • Provider carries namespace, registrationState, registrationPolicy, resourceTypes[], providerAuthorizationConsentState. Each resource type has resourceType, locations, apiVersions, defaultApiVersion, capabilities.
  • The 2022-12-01 subscriptions spec has no create, PATCH or DELETE on /subscriptions/{id}.

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • Providers are static. 17 namespaces, always Registered, no registrationPolicy, and only Storage, KeyVault and DocumentDB have resourceTypes; the rest return []. There is no unregister, no tenant-level GET /providers, and no .../resourceTypes. The provider-entry id is hard-coded to the default subscription. PLAN 3.4 derives the list from the engine registry and merges with the static list until legacy types register.
  • No provider gate. Nothing returns 409 MissingSubscriptionRegistration, because nothing can be unregistered.
  • No /subscriptions/{id}/locations. Several SDKs and az account list-locations call it.
  • Any subscription id is Enabled. GET /subscriptions/{any} returns the single default subscription's shape with the requested id. There is one fixed subscription (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, display name miniblue, tenant ...0001).
  • Subscription body is thin. authorizationSource is Legacy; subscriptionPolicies is absent.
  • GET /tenants is served. tagNames is not.
  • Existing coverage: internal/services/subscriptions/handler_test.go, tests/subscriptions_test.go, tests/subscriptionlist_test.go (list by subscription for vnet, nsg, publicip, lb).

docs.title: Providers
docs.text: ID Behaviour (real Azure) Expect Tier Notes G3-T18 List providers for a subscription: at least 10 namespaces including Microsoft.KeyVault, Microsoft.Storage, Microsoft.ContainerRegistry, Microsoft.ServiceBus, Microsoft.EventHub. Every entry has registrationState and registrationPolicy. GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers => 200, value meets those checks T2 registrationPolicy is missing today. Namespace match is case-insensitive. G3-T19 GET one provider: namespace=Microsoft.KeyVault, registrationState=Registered, registrationPolicy=RegistrationRequired. GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault => 200 T2 Policy string value (verify). Unknown namespace => 404 (verify) code. G3-T20 Unregister Microsoft.Storage, then GET and list show Unregistered; register it again and both show Registered. POST .../unregister => 200; POST .../register => 200 T2 Unregister is missing today. Real Azure passes through Registering and Unregistering states (verify enum); the emulator may collapse them to the final state. Real unregister also fails while resources of that provider exist (verify); do not port. G3-T21 Provider gate. PUT a Key Vault while its namespace is unregistered for the subscription. The portal and az then auto-register and retry. PUT .../Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/{n} => 409 MissingSubscriptionRegistration T2 Gate only; the client auto-register half is client behaviour, not an emulator scenario. Default every namespace to Registered so existing flows are untouched; the gate fires only after an explicit unregister. Gate placement (middleware or an Admitter) is undecided. G3-T22 Tenant-level provider list; every namespace has a non-empty resourceTypes array. GET /providers => 200 T2 Missing today. Only meaningful once PLAN 3.4 derives resourceTypes from the registry; until then only the registered types are non-empty, so restrict the assertion to those.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Subscription creation is not a /subscriptions/{id} operation. Real ARM exposes only GET, list, locations and tenants there; creating a subscription uses Microsoft.Subscription aliases and cancel/enable are billing-owned POSTs under that provider. A PATCH or DELETE on /subscriptions/{id} has no real counterpart.
  • A single fixed subscription is a feature for emulator users who set ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID to any GUID. Returning 404 SubscriptionNotFound for unknown ids is real, but must stay opt-in or it breaks those setups. Treat the strict check as conditional.
  • A PUT or GET under an unknown subscription is 404, not a server error.
  • GET /subscriptions lists subscriptions the caller can see; with one fixed subscription it returns one. Do not assert multiple results.
  • Provider registration is per subscription, not global, and state names are exact strings. A gate that rejects after registering (stale state) is a worse failure than no gate.
  • registrationPolicy and registrationState are separate fields: the policy says whether registration is required; the state says whether this subscription did it.
  • Tag name and tag value PUT can return 200 or 201 depending on whether the entry is new.

docs.title: Dropped
docs.text: ID Reason G3-T12 List with multiple subscriptions needs a way to create or seed them. Create is not real ARM at this path (see the create row below) and no seeding mechanism is designed; the single fixed subscription is the supported model. G3-T14 Subscription tag update, value update and removal through a PATCH on /subscriptions/{id}. Not a real ARM operation. G3-T15 Create (POST), delete and PATCH on /subscriptions/{id}. Not real ARM; creation goes through Microsoft.Subscription aliases, out of scope. G3-T16 Cancel and enable. Real routes (POST /subscriptions/{id}/providers/Microsoft.Subscription/cancel and enable) belong to the Microsoft.Subscription provider and are billing-owned; out of scope for a fixed single subscription. G3-T17 Create validation of a malformed id or empty body. The create route is not real ARM (see the create, delete and PATCH row).

docs.title: Virtual network
docs.text:
Engine fit: hooks (virtualNetworks), passthrough child (subnets, virtualNetworkPeerings) plus a state hook (peerings), engine-gap (inline subnet sync, privateEndpoints side effects). miniblue today: hand-written service internal/services/network (vnets, subnets). Suggested wave: PLAN wave 4 for virtualNetworks and subnets; peerings as a new type after G2; privateEndpoints deferred.

Paths below are relative to /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.Network. Spec facts come from Microsoft.Network/Network virtualNetwork.json (checked at 2025-01-01; later stable directories exist, the newest listed is 2026-03-01).

docs.title: miniblue gaps
docs.text:
Ordered by value.

  • resourceGuid is regenerated with uuid.New() on every PUT (handler.go:173). azurerm and azapi see drift on each apply.
  • virtualNetworkPeerings is always [] (handler.go:177) and there are no peering routes. azurerm_virtual_network_peering cannot work.
  • Subnet delegations is always [] (handler.go:350); service endpoints and policies are also not echoed, so azurerm_subnet delegation shows drift.
  • No PATCH and no CheckIPAddressAvailability; no privateEndpoints.
  • Inline properties.subnets on a VNet PUT deletes and recreates every subnet, but only when the key is present (handler.go:236-237, handler.go:252). Subnet PUT and DELETE sync the list back into the VNet document (handler.go:412, handler.go:447).
  • DELETE of an existing vnet or subnet returns 202 with no Location (handler.go:314, handler.go:448); a missing one returns 404 (real: 204).
  • VNet PUT does not check that the resource group exists; a missing location defaults to eastus (handler.go:161-163). Subnet PUT checks the vnet.
  • etag is the constant W/"miniblue" (handler.go:212, handler.go:388); real etags change on each write.
  • Only vnet: and subnet: are in the RG cascade list (resourcegroups/handler.go:153-154); peerings and private endpoints will need prefixes or DeleteTree.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Echo the request location, not the RG location. Create is 201 and update is 200.
  • resourceGuid is stable across PUTs and GETs.
  • CheckIPAddressAvailability evaluates the VNet address space, and each subnet reserves its first four addresses and the last one.
  • Peering peeringState is Initiated until the reverse peering exists, then Connected; it is not Connected on first PUT.
  • Not-found is the generic ResourceNotFound for subnets and peerings; do not mint per-type codes such as a subnet-specific one.
  • Subnet fields the emulator does not model (delegations, serviceEndpoints) must still round-trip, or azurerm shows permanent drift.
  • Real Azure may answer vnet writes and deletes with 202 plus a poll URL; the engine is sync (201 or 200, 200 or 204).
  • A 202 with no Location can stall azurerm; see ADR 0006.

docs.title: Dropped
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Slice 1: Role assignments on the engine, with opt-in enforcement
docs.text:
Proves:

  • Request.Current (stable createdOn, immutable fields);
  • Reader cross-lookups (role definitions, duplicates);
  • the List override;
  • PatchNone;
  • typed errors;
  • extension resources at every scope;
  • the Authorizer seam.

Depends on: PLAN phase 1 (Engine.Do, hooks, Reader, Principal, token package).

docs.title: Today
docs.text:
internal/services/authorization/handler.go:

  • PUT (:177) rebuilds the doc from an allow-list. createdOn and updatedOn are time.Now() on every PUT (:206).
  • No validation beyond "properties present".
  • Key is authorization:roleAssignment:<scope as sent>:<name> (:169). It is case-sensitive, so a scope sent with different casing misses.
  • List (:231) is exact-scope prefix only.
  • Delete of a missing assignment returns 404. Real ARM returns 204.
  • principalType is echoed, or "" when absent (:205). Keep that.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
// internal/services/authorization/types.go
func Register(reg *arm.Registry, h *Handler) {
    reg.Register(arm.Type{
        Name:        "Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments",
        APIVersions: []string{"2022-04-01"},
        Scopes:      arm.ScopeTenant | arm.ScopeManagementGroup | arm.ScopeSubscription | arm.ScopeResourceGroup | arm.ScopeResource,
        Patch:       arm.PatchNone,
        List:        h.listAssignments,
        Hooks:       arm.Hooks{Validate: h.validateAssignment, Defaults: defaultAssignment},
    })
}

arm.ID already parses extension resources on arbitrary resource scopes (id.go:25,106). Add an armtest case at a child-resource scope anyway.

A resource-scope assignment is not existence-checked against its scope (ADR-0003, phase 5), because the scope is usually a legacy resource the engine cannot see. RG and subscription scopes are checked through ScopeExists.

docs.title: Validate (under lock, sees Current)
Defaults (idempotent)
docs.text:
• properties.scope = r.ID.Scope.String() (as sent).
  • createdOn = Current.properties.createdOn, else now.
  • updatedOn = now on create; on update, now only if the properties changed, else Current's value.
  • Echo principalType ("" when absent, as today), condition, conditionVersion, delegatedManagedIdentityResourceId and description.
  • Drop all other input properties. This matches today's allow-list.

docs.title: List override
docs.text:
Collection GET at {scope}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:

$filter Result none at, above and below scope (verify against a real subscription before PR 1) atScope() at and above principalId eq '{id}' at, above and below, for that principal
  • Combine clauses by splitting on and (case-insensitive). An unknown clause gives 400 InvalidFilter (verify).
  • assignedTo('{id}') is not documented for 2022-04-01, so it is not implemented. Add it only if a client is seen sending it.
  • "Above" walks scope.Parent() with Reader.Children. "Below" uses Reader.Under(scope, type).

docs.title: Persisted state
docs.text: Bump store.SchemaVersion, with the CHANGELOG line state reset required: role assignments moved to the ARM engine. There is no data migration (ADR-0004 §5). The case-sensitive legacy keys go away with the reset.

docs.title: Removal
docs.text:
In handler.go, delete:

  • handleRoleAssignments and the create, get, list and delete functions;
  • roleAssignmentKey and roleAssignmentPrefix;
  • the roleAssignments lines in registerScope.

Narrow Middleware (:45) to roleDefinitions paths only, and let everything else fall through. The overlap guard fails boot if any chi roleAssignments route is left.

docs.title: Enforcement (MINIBLUE_RBAC=enforce)
docs.text:
Enforcer as specified in ADR-0008, wired with arm.WithAuthorizer when the env var is set.

In the same PR as the Enforcer (or just before it):

  • fix Contributor notActions;
  • add User Access Administrator.

Tests (in-process, internal/services/authorization):

Test Expect Enforcement off (default), non-default principal Every write is allowed On, default principal (...0002) Allowed (implicit admin) On, principal with no assignments 403 AuthorizationFailed on PUT. The message names the action and scope. Reader at subscription GET in RG allowed; PUT in RG denied (inheritance) Contributor at RG PUT resource allowed; PUT roleAssignment denied (notActions) Custom role Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/read Read allowed, write denied Assignment at resource scope Applies to that resource and its children only Mixed-case scope in assignment vs request Still matches Custom role definition stored at its legacy key Resolved through RoleResolver; permissions apply Store read fails during the walk 500, not 403 and not allow

Tokens come from internal/token.Issue with distinct client ids, so tests also cover the per-client oid.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
• The armtest sample for roleAssignments passes. Update changes only description. Invalid uses a non-GUID principalId.
  • Existing authorization/handler_test.go and tests/ stay green. The listed intentional changes:
    • delete-missing returns 204;
    • list includes above and below scope;
    • createdOn is stable.
  • Optional local run: azurerm_role_assignment apply, then a second plan is empty, then destroy.

docs.text:

  2. fix(authorization): contributor notActions; add User Access Administrator
  3. feat(authorization): opt-in RBAC enforcement

docs.title: Slice 2: APIM Consumption control plane
docs.text:
Proves:

  • a new RP costs only registration, hooks and samples;
  • Current-aware Defaults (stable identity and URLs);
  • PatchMerge;
  • parent existence;
  • subscription-wide list;
  • Provisioned;
  • opaque ;rev= names;
  • the skip-polling header.

No bespoke chi routes are needed.

Depends on: PLAN phase 1. It is independent of Slice 1.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
// internal/services/apim/types.go
func Register(reg *arm.Registry) {
    reg.Register(arm.Type{
        Name:        "Microsoft.ApiManagement/service",
        APIVersions: []string{"2024-05-01", "2022-08-01"},
        Scopes:      arm.ScopeResourceGroup,
        Provisioned: true,
        Hooks:       arm.Hooks{Validate: validateService, Defaults: defaultService},
        Children: []arm.Type{
            {Name: "apis", Hooks: apiHooks, Children: []arm.Type{{Name: "operations", Hooks: operationHooks}}},
            {Name: "products", Hooks: productHooks, Children: []arm.Type{{Name: "apis"}}},
            {Name: "namedValues", Hooks: namedValueHooks},
            {Name: "backends", Hooks: backendHooks},
        },
    })
}
  • Children default to PatchMerge (the zero value). That is harmless, and right for azapi.
  • products/apis echoes its body.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Type Validate Defaults service CheckName(^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9]$, 1, 50); location; sku.name in the known set; sku.capacity (Consumption 0); publisherEmail and publisherName required, max 100 (verify) customProperties {} when absent (azurerm dereferences it without a nil check); virtualNetworkType=None; publicNetworkAccess=Enabled; disableGateway=false; platformVersion=stv2; notificationSenderEmail; URLs derived from the name (gatewayUrl, gatewayRegionalUrl, managementApiUrl, scmUrl, portalUrl, developerPortalUrl); DefaultIdentity(doc, cur, uami) apis path required, max 400; displayName required, max 300; name part before ;rev= 1 to 256, ^[^*#&+:<>?]+$ authenticationSettings {oAuth2AuthenticationSettings:[], openidAuthenticationSettings:[]}; subscriptionKeyParameterNames {header:"Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key", query:"subscription-key"}; type=http; protocols=["https"] when absent; subscriptionRequired=true; apiRevision from ;rev=N (default "1"); isCurrent=true; isOnline=true operations displayName, method and urlTemplate required; name 1 to 80 echo products displayName required, max 300; approvalRequired only with subscriptionRequired state=notPublished; subscriptionRequired=true namedValues displayName 1 to 256, ^[A-Za-z0-9-._]+$; exactly one of value and keyVault secret=false; tags=[] backends url required; protocol in echo credentials, proxy, tls, circuitBreaker

Validation errors are 400 ValidationError with target set to the property path (verify the code against real APIM).

Rules:

  • Never emit createdAtUtc.
  • Never emit hostnameConfigurations unless the client sent it.
  • Never seed APIs or products. azurerm lists and deletes them right after create.

docs.title: Client behaviours to honour
docs.text:
• azurerm service create:
    • GET locations/{loc}/deletedservices/{n}: strict 404 is enough, so no route is needed.
    • PUT, then LIST apis and products. Both must return {"value":[]}.
  • azurerm service update is PATCH (sku, properties, identity, tags), so it needs PatchMerge.
  • azurerm api paths are always apis/{name};rev=1 with If-Match: *.
    • The name is opaque: key on the decoded segment, echo it in id and name.
    • armtest covers both raw ; and %3B.
    • Never require If-Match.
  • Never send a Location header (an asyncId one triggers azurerm's custom poller), and never return 202.
  • namedValue PUT goes through CreateOrUpdateThenPoll. The skip-polling header (ADR-0006) avoids a 10 s wait.

docs.title: Out of scope (documented deviations)
docs.text:
• checkNameAvailability.
  • Soft-delete, deletedservices and purge: purge_soft_delete_on_destroy=true is unsupported.
  • Tier B SKUs: portalsettings, tenant access, listSecrets.
  • Subscriptions, users, groups, policies, loggers, diagnostics, certificates, gateways.
  • apis/{name} to ;rev=<current> aliasing.
  • Secret masking.
  • $filter and paging.
  • Gateway runtime.

Each of these is a later PR. Actions lands with the first one that needs it (listSecrets).

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:

  • Unit tests (internal/services/apim):

    • apply, then a second plan is empty, then destroy is clean.
    • A matching azapi_resource fixture for service plus api, with azapi_update_resource on tags.
  • Startup time and memory are unchanged within noise.
